ecs: Cloud server instance
eni: Network interface card
Parameter - N: Indicates the backend server sequence number. Valid range: 1 to 20

AclStatus.description_cn:
Enable access control?
Available values:
on: Enable
off: Disable
If you do not specify a value for this parameter, the current configuration remains unchanged and access control settings are not modified. Setting this parameter will clear the existing AclType and AclIds values.
Note: Changing this parameter from 'on' to 'off' will clear the values of AclType and AclIds. Changing from 'off' to 'on' requires you to set both AclType and AclIds.

Note: Changing this parameter from 'on' to 'off' will clear the values of AclType and AclIds. Changing from 'off' to 'on' requires you to set both AclType and AclIds.

AclType.description_cn:
Access control mode. Available options:
white: Whitelist mode. The listener only forwards requests from IP addresses or ranges specified in the selected access control policy group. If no IP addresses are added to the selected policy group, the listener does not forward any requests.
black: Blacklist mode. The listener only blocks requests from IP addresses or ranges specified in the selected access control policy group. If no IP addresses are added to the selected policy group, the listener forwards all requests.
Note: When the AclStatus parameter is set to on, both AclType and AclIds.N are required.

Note: When the AclStatus parameter is set to on, both AclType and AclIds.N are required.

Bandwidth.description_cn:
Listener bandwidth peak, in Mbps.

Set to -1 to disable rate limiting for the listener. In this case, the listener's bandwidth peak defaults to the remaining bandwidth of the CLB instance.
The listener's bandwidth peak cannot exceed the specification bandwidth of its CLB instance. For details on CLB instance specification bandwidth, see Product Specifications.

Note
Listener rate limiting is currently in invite-only testing. To use this feature, please submit a ticket or contact your account manager to apply.

HealthCheck.Domain.description_en: The domain name for health checks must be set to the actual service address provided by the backend server. It must contain at least one '.', and cannot start or end with a '.'. Each string can include letters, numbers, '-', and '.' characters. '-' cannot appear at the beginning or end of the string. Length must be between 1 and 128 characters. If this parameter is not provided or no value is specified, the default is blank, meaning the load balancer uses the private IP address of each backend server for health checks. Note: This parameter takes effect only when Protocol is set to HTTP or HTTPS and HealthCheck.Enabled is set to on.

HealthCheck.Timeout.description_en:

If this parameter is not specified or no value is provided, the default is '/'. Note: This parameter takes effect only when Protocol is set to HTTP or HTTPS and HealthCheck.Enabled is set to on.

Scheduler.description_cn:
Scheduling algorithm used by the listener. Available options:
wrr (default): Weighted round robin. Backend servers with higher weights are selected more frequently.
wlc: Weighted least connections. Assigns different weights to each server based on their processing capacity, so servers handle a number of requests proportional to their weight, based on the least number of connections.
sh: Source hash. Uses consistent hashing based on the source IP address. Requests from the same source IP are always routed to the same backend server.
When EnhancedSchedulerEnable is set to "on" for the listener, the above algorithms are unavailable. Available options: wlr, wlrt, wl. When set to wl, you must configure the LoadType field.

When EnhancedSchedulerEnable is set to "on" for the listener, the above algorithms are unavailable. Available options: wlr, wlrt, wl. When set to wl, you must configure the LoadType field.

Ciphers.description_cn:
Update the cipher suites for the TLS custom security policy. Supported cipher suites for each TLS protocol version are as follows:

* TLSv1.0 & TLSv1.1:
   * ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-SHA
   * ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-SHA
   * ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA
   * ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA
   * AES128-SHA
   * AES256-SHA
   * DES-CBC3-SHA
* TLSv1.2:
   * ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
   * ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
   * ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-SHA256
   * ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-SHA384
   * ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
   * ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
   * ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256
   * ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA384
   * AES128-GCM-SHA256
   * AES256-GCM-SHA384
   * AES128-SHA256
   * AES256-SHA256
* TLSv1.3:
   * TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256
   * TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
   * TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
   * TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256
   * TLS_AES_128_CCM_SHA256
   * TLS_SM4_GCM_SM3
   * TLS_SM4_CCM_SM3

* When passing this parameter, you must provide all cipher suites to be supported. Adding or removing cipher suites individually via this API is not supported.
* If only `Ciphers.N` is provided and `TlsVersions.N` is not, validation is based on the TLS protocol versions supported by the current listener and the cipher suites provided in the request.
* If both `TlsVersions.N` and `Ciphers.N` are provided, validation is based on the TLS protocol versions and cipher suites provided in the request.
* The cipher suites TLS_SM4_GCM_SM3 and TLS_SM4_CCM_SM3 are currently in invitation-only testing. To request access, please contact your account manager.
Ciphers.description_en:
Update the cipher suites for the TLS custom security policy. Supported cipher suites for each TLS protocol version are as follows:

HealthCheck.Domain.description_en:
Health check domain name. Must be set to the actual address used by the server to provide external services

* Must contain at least one period (.), and cannot start or end with a period (.)
* Only uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens (-), and periods (.) are supported. '-' cannot appear at the beginning or end of the string
* Length limit: 1–80 characters
* If this parameter is not provided, the backend server's private IP address is used for health checks by default

HealthCheck.Enabled.description_en:
Enable health check for the listener.
Enter the value exactly as shown below. Do not use any other values.

* true: Enable
* false: Disable

The following parameters are valid only when this parameter is set to "true".

HealthCheck.HealthyThreshold.description_en:
Health check threshold range: 2 to 10 times
A backend server is considered healthy if it passes the specified number of consecutive health checks with a status of 'normal'

HealthCheck.HttpCode.description_en:
HTTP status codes indicating a healthy health check. Available values:

* http_2xx
* http_3xx
* http_4xx
* http_5xx

This parameter takes effect when `HealthCheck.Type` is set to "HTTP". Use commas to separate multiple status codes.

HealthCheck.Method.description_en:
Health check methods. Available values:

* GET: The server must support the GET method
* HEAD: The server returns only HEAD header information, reducing backend overhead, but must support the HEAD method

This parameter is effective when `HealthCheck.Type` is set to "HTTP"

HealthCheck.Port.description_en:
Health check port, range: 1–65535

* If the server group does not enable full port forwarding, this parameter defaults to 0, meaning the health check uses the backend server port.
* If the server group enables full port forwarding, you must specify this parameter.

HealthCheck.Timeout.description_en:
Health check response timeout range: 1 to 60 seconds.
If the backend server does not respond correctly within the specified time, the health check is marked as "abnormal."

HealthCheck.Type.description_en:
Health check types. Available values:

* TCP: Sends a SYN handshake packet to check if the backend server port is functioning properly
* HTTP: Sends a HEAD or GET request to simulate browsing behavior and verify if the backend server application is running normally
* UDP: Sends ICMP or UDP probe packets to check if the backend server is operating correctly

HealthCheck.URI.description_en:
Health check path.

* Must start with the character “/”.
* Can include letters, numbers, hyphens (-), underscores (_), slashes (/), periods (.), percent signs (%), question marks (?), hash signs (#), ampersands (&), and equal signs (=).
* Length must be between 1 and 128 characters.

This parameter takes effect when `HealthCheck.Type` is set to "HTTP".

HealthCheck.UdpExpect.description_en:
Expected response string for UDP health check

* Only letters and numbers are allowed, with a maximum length of 64 characters
* This parameter is effective when Protocol is set to UDP and HealthCheck.Enabled is set to on
* The values of HealthCheck.UdpRequest and HealthCheck.UdpExpect must either both be empty or both not empty

HealthCheck.UdpRequest.description_en:
UDP health check request string.

* Only letters and numbers are allowed. Maximum length is 64 characters.
* This parameter takes effect when Protocol is set to UDP and HealthCheck.Enabled is set to on.
* HealthCheck.UdpRequest and HealthCheck.UdpExpect must either both be empty or both be non-empty.

HealthCheck.UnhealthyThreshold.description_en:
Unhealthy threshold for health checks: 2 to 10 times
If a backend server returns "abnormal" for the specified number of consecutive health checks, it will be marked as unhealthy

Scheduler.description_cn:
Rules followed by NLB when forwarding traffic.

* wrr: Weighted round robin. Backend servers with higher weights are selected more frequently.
* wlc: Weighted least connections. Based on the least number of connections, assigns different weights to each backend server according to their processing capabilities, allowing them to handle a corresponding number of service requests.
* sh: Source address hash. Uses consistent hashing based on the source IP address; the same source address is routed to the same backend server.

Rules.N.ActionType.description_en:
Forward action
- Forward: Forward to backend server group
- Redirect: Redirect
Note:
If this parameter is not specified or is an empty string, no changes are made by default
No error is reported if the value provided matches the current value

Rules.N.Description.description_en:
Forwarding rule description. Default value is an empty string

Parameter - N: Indicates the forwarding rule number, ranging from 1 to 50
Use '&' to separate multiple forwarding rules
Specification:
Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Allowed characters include letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space, equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。)
Length limit: 0 to 255 characters

Rules.N.RedirectConfig.Host.description_en:
Redirect target domain name. Only exact domain names are supported.
- Parameter N: Indicates the domain name sequence number, valid range is 1–50
- Use '&' to separate multiple domain names
Requirements:
- Must contain at least one '.' and cannot start or end with '.'
- Only letters, numbers, '.', and '-' are allowed
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
- Exact domain name: A domain name that meets the format requirements, such as www.test.com
> Note:
> When `Rules.N.ActionType` is changed from `Forward` to `Redirect`, if this parameter is not specified or is set to an empty string, it will default to an empty string, and the redirect will use the request domain as the target domain.
> In other cases, if this parameter is not specified, it will remain unchanged by default; if set to an empty string, it will be updated to an empty string.

Rules.N.RedirectConfig.Path.description_en:
Redirect destination path
- Parameter N: Indicates the port number; valid values are 1–50
- Use '&' to separate multiple ports
- Port value range: 1–65535
> Note:
> When `Rules.N.ActionType` is changed from `Forward` to `Redirect`, if this parameter is not specified or is an empty string, it defaults to an empty string, making the redirect path match the request path
> In other cases, if this parameter is not specified, the default is no change; if an empty string is provided, it will be set to an empty string

Rules.N.RedirectConfig.Port.description_en:
Target port for redirection
- Parameter N: Indicates the domain sequence number; valid values are 1–50
- Separate multiple domains with “&”
- Port range: 1–65535
> Note:
> When `Rules.N.ActionType` changes from `Forward` to `Redirect`, if this parameter is not specified or is an empty string, it defaults to an empty string, and the port will be set to the same as the request port
> In other cases, if this parameter is not specified, it remains unchanged by default; if an empty string is provided, it will be set to an empty string

Rules.N.RedirectConfig.Protocol.description_en:
Redirect protocol
- Parameter - N: Indicates the rule sequence number, ranging from 1 to 50
- Use '&' to separate multiple forwarding rules
- Valid values: HTTP, HTTPS (default)
> Note:
> When `Rules.N.ActionType` changes from `Forward` to `Redirect`, if this parameter is not specified or is an empty string, HTTPS is used by default

TemplateRules.LevelConditions.Conditions.description_cn:
Comparison symbol. Supports standard threshold alerts: >, >=, <, <=, !=, =, as well as the following period-over-period alerts:

- last_period_increase_pct: increased compared to the previous period
- last_period_decrease_pct: decreased compared to the previous period
- last_period_abs_pct: increased or decreased compared to the previous period
- last_day_increase_pct: increased compared to the same period yesterday
- last_day_decrease_pct: decreased compared to the same period yesterday
- last_day_abs_pct: increased or decreased compared to the same period yesterday
- last_week_increase_pct: increased compared to the same period last week
- last_week_decrease_pct: decreased compared to the same period last week
- last_week_abs_pct: increased or decreased compared to the same period last week

MessageQueue.description_cn:
When the alert notification method is message queue Kafka, this is the triggered message queue.

- Currently, only topics in the Beijing region of message queue Kafka are supported.
- For instances bound to an allowlist, only IPs configured in the allowlist can access the corresponding Kafka instance. Please note:
	- When pushing to message queue Kafka, do not select instances from the allowlist.
	- After configuring to push to a specific instance, do not add that instance to the allowlist.
- When you select to deliver to this Kafka topic for the first time in the event rule, a user named __volcevent_xxxvolc will be automatically created under **User Management** for this topic. Do not delete this user, otherwise Cloud Monitoring will not be able to deliver messages to this topic.

- When you select to deliver to this Kafka topic for the first time in the event rule, a user named __volcevent_xxxvolc will be automatically created under **User Management** for this topic. Do not delete this user, otherwise Cloud Monitoring will not be able to deliver messages to this topic.

GroupBy.description_cn:
The grouping dimensions used for the metric to query. See [Cloud Monitoring Metric Query](https://console.volcengine.com/cloud_monitor/metricDoc?tabKey=metric) for the **Dimensions** of each product.
- If the **Dimension** column for the metric is not marked as **optional**, it means there are no optional Dimensions. By default, all Dimensions are required and are used as grouping dimensions for the metric.
    Required means that regardless of whether you pass these Dimension parameters, the returned data will be grouped by these Dimensions.
    For example, for the Redis cache database metric **AggregatedTotalQps**, the Dimension column is **ResourceID,Node**.
    - If you pass the Dimension parameter Node but not ResourceID:
        - Query condition: Node=xxx and ResourceID=*
        - Grouping dimensions: Node,ResourceId
    - If you pass both Node and ResourceID:
        - Query condition: Node=xxx and ResourceId=yyy
        - Grouping dimensions: Node,ResourceId

- If the **Dimension** column for the metric is marked as **optional**, it means there are optional Dimensions. You need to specify the GroupBy parameter additionally. For examples, see **GroupBy instructions**.

The SDK must be upgraded to the following versions to support filtering grouping dimensions using GroupBy.

- Python: version 1.0.37 or above
- Go: version 1.0.97 or above
- Java: version 0.1.75 or above

- For an explanation of StartTime and EndTime offsets after passing in Period, see **Period description**.

TemplateRules.LevelConditions.Conditions.description_cn:
Comparison operator. Supports standard threshold alerts: >, >=, <, <=, !=, =, as well as the following period-over-period alerts:

- last_period_increase_pct: increase compared to the previous period
- last_period_decrease_pct: decrease compared to the previous period
- last_period_abs_pct: increase or decrease compared to the previous period
- last_day_increase_pct: increase compared to the same period yesterday
- last_day_decrease_pct: decrease compared to the same period yesterday
- last_day_abs_pct: increase or decrease compared to the same period yesterday
- last_week_increase_pct: increase compared to the same period last week
- last_week_decrease_pct: decrease compared to the same period last week
- last_week_abs_pct: increase or decrease compared to the same period last week

Tags.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key (Key) for the shared virtual interface.

* Tags.N.Key: Indicates the sequence number of the tag key (Key). Value range: 1–50, and N should be in consecutive ascending order.
* Separate multiple tag keys (Key) with &.
* Cannot start with `volc:` or `sys:`, in any case format. `volc:` and `sys:` are reserved for system tags and cannot be created.
* Length range: 1–128 characters. Supports characters from all languages, numbers, spaces (), underscores (_), periods (.), colons (:), slashes (/), equals (=), plus (+), hyphens (-), and @ (@).

Tags.N.Value.description_en:
Tag value (Value) for the shared virtual interface.

* N indicates the sequence number of the tag value (Value), ranging from 1 to 50, and must be in continuous ascending order.
* Multiple tag values (Value) are separated by &.
* Length range: 0–256 characters. If not specified, the default is empty.
* Supports input in any language, numbers, spaces (), underscores (_), periods (.), half-width colons (:), slashes (/), equals signs (=), plus signs (+), hyphens (-), and @ (@).
* Case-sensitive. Cannot start or end with a space.

> Note
> If `Tags.N.Value` is provided, `Tags.N.Key` must also be provided.

VlanId.description_cn:
VLAN ID for connecting to the local IDC. Make sure this VLAN ID is not in use. Value range: 0–2999.

* 0: Indicates no VLAN is configured on the physical dedicated connection switch port, using Layer 3 routing interface mode. Only one shared virtual interface without a VLAN tag can be created per physical dedicated connection in this mode.
* 1–2999: Indicates the switch port of the physical dedicated connection uses Layer 3 sub-interface mode. Each sub-interface is configured with a different VLAN ID mapped to a virtual interface. Multiple shared virtual interfaces can be created per physical dedicated connection in this mode.

BgpAsn.description_cn:
The ASN (Autonomous System Number) of the Direct Connect Gateway.

* The valid range for the Direct Connect Gateway ASN is: 137718, 64512 ~ 65534, 4200000000 ~ 4294967294. Among these, 137718 is the ASN for BytePlus.
* If the Direct Connect Gateway is used only in standard scenarios (such as a local IDC accessing a single cloud VPC resource via Direct Connect), use the BytePlus ASN (137718).
* If the Direct Connect Gateway is used in special scenarios (such as a single IDC accessing multiple Cloud Enterprise Networks via Direct Connect), each Direct Connect Gateway must use a custom ASN and avoid using the BytePlus ASN (137718), ensuring that the ASN for each Direct Connect Gateway is unique.

QueueType.description_cn:
Traffic queue type

* **High**: High-priority queue. High-priority queues are allocated bandwidth first. Only one high-priority traffic queue can be created per QoS policy
* **Medium**: Regular queue. Bandwidth is allocated based on the bandwidth percentage after the high-priority queue allocation

Each QoS policy supports creating a maximum of **1** `High` type traffic queue (non-upgradable) and **2** `Medium` type traffic queues (upgradable). For more usage restrictions related to QoS policy configuration for dedicated connections, see [Constraints](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/directconnect/Limits)

Tags.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key (Key) for the virtual interface.

* Parameter - N - Parameter: Indicates the sequence number of the tag key (Key). Value range: 1, 2, 3, ..., 49, 50. N must be in continuous ascending order.
* Separate multiple tag keys (Key) with &.
* Cannot start with `volc:` or `sys:`, regardless of case. Tags starting with `volc:` or `sys:` are reserved for the system and cannot be created.
* Length range: 1–128 characters. Supports input of letters from any language, numbers, spaces, underscores (_), periods (.), colons (:), slashes (/), equals signs (=), plus signs (+), hyphens (-), and at signs (@).

Tags.N.Value.description_en:
Tag value (Value) for the virtual interface.

* Parameter - N - Parameter: Indicates the sequence number of the tag value (Value). Value range: 1, 2, 3, ..., 49, 50. N must be in continuous ascending order.
* Separate multiple tag values (Value) with &.
* Length range: 0–256 characters. If not specified, will be empty by default.
* Supports input of letters from any language, numbers, spaces, underscores (_), periods (.), colons (:), slashes (/), equals signs (=), plus signs (+), hyphens (-), and at signs (@).
* Case-sensitive. Cannot start or end with a space.

If `Tags.N.Value` is provided, `Tags.N.Key` must also be provided.

VlanId.description_cn:
VLAN ID used to connect to the local IDC. Make sure this VLAN ID is not already in use. Value range: 0–2999.

* 0: Indicates that no VLAN is configured on the physical dedicated connection switch port, using Layer 3 routing interface mode. In this mode, only one virtual interface without a VLAN tag can be created on a single physical dedicated connection.
* 1–2999: Indicates that the switch port of the physical dedicated connection uses Layer 3 subinterface mode. Each subinterface is configured with a different VLAN ID, corresponding to a virtual interface. In this mode, multiple virtual interfaces can be created on a single physical dedicated connection.
VlanId.description_en:
VLAN ID used to connect to the local IDC. Make sure this VLAN ID is not already in use. Value range: 0–2999.

* 1–2999: Indicates that the switch port of the physical dedicated connection uses Layer 3 subinterface mode. Each subinterface is configured with a different VLAN ID, corresponding to a virtual interface. In this mode, multiple virtual interfaces can be created on a single physical dedicated connection.

TagFilters.N.Values.N.description_en:
Tag value (Value) for cloud resource instances

Parameter - N - Parameter - N: The first N indicates the index of the tag key corresponding to the tag value, which should match the index of the tag key TagFilters.N.Key. Valid values: 1, 2, 3, …, 9, 10. N must be in consecutive ascending order. The second N indicates the index of the tag value, with valid values: 1, 2, 3.

You can omit Value to query without restricting Value.
If Value is an empty string, the query returns tags where Value is empty.
If you specify multiple TagFilters.N.Values.N for the same TagFilters.N.Key, these TagFilters.N.Values.N are combined using logical OR.

TagFilters.N.Value.N.description_en:
Tag values for Cloud Enterprise Network (CEN) instances. Each tag key can have up to 3 tag values.

If this parameter is not specified, all tag values under the specified tag key and their associated CEN instances are queried.
If this parameter is set to empty, CEN instances associated with tags whose value is empty under the specified tag key are queried.
If multiple tag values are specified for the same tag key, the result is the set of CEN instances associated with each tag value under that tag key.
If this parameter is specified, TagFilters.N.Key must be specified first.

TagFilters.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key (Key) of the cloud resource instance.

* Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag key; value range: 1–10.
* Separate multiple tag keys with `&`.
* If multiple `TagFilters.N.Key` are provided, the relationship between them is logical "AND"; duplicates are not allowed.

TagFilters.N.Values.N.description_en:
Tag value (Value) for cloud resource instances

Parameter - N - Parameter - N: The first N indicates the sequence number of the tag key and should match the sequence number of TagFilters.N.Key. Valid values: 1, 2, 3, …, 9, 10. N must be in consecutive ascending order. The second N indicates the sequence number of the tag value, with valid values: 1, 2, 3.
You can omit Value to query without restricting Value.
If Value is an empty string, the query returns tags where Value is empty.
If you specify multiple TagFilters.N.Values.N for the same TagFilters.N.Key, the relationship between these TagFilters.N.Values.N is logical OR.

Bandwidth.description_cn:
Bandwidth of the virtual interface, unit: Mbps.

* -1: Unlimited.
* 1–100000: Maximum bandwidth for inbound and outbound directions to the cloud. Cannot exceed the bandwidth of the associated physical Direct Connect. You can call [DescribeDirectConnectConnections](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/directconnect/DescribeDirectConnectConnections) to query information about the physical Direct Connect.
* If the virtual interface is associated with a shared Direct Connect, it inherits the bandwidth of the shared Direct Connect. You do not need to provide this parameter. If you do provide it, ensure the value matches the bandwidth of the associated shared Direct Connect. You can call [DescribeSharedDirectConnectConnections](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/directconnect/DescribeSharedDirectConnectConnections) to query shared Direct Connect information (the shared Direct Connect feature is currently in invite-only testing; only accounts with this feature enabled can use it and view supporting documentation. Contact your account manager to apply for a trial if needed).
* Leave blank to retain the original configuration.

Tags.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key for the resource

* Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag key, range: 1–20
* Separate multiple tag keys with &
* Cannot start with volc: or sys:, in any case
* Length range: 1–128 characters; supports input of characters from all languages, numbers, spaces ( ), underscores (_), periods (.), colons (:), slashes (/), equals signs (=), plus signs (+), hyphens (-), and at signs (@)
* If the tag key starts or ends with a space, the system automatically removes it

> Tag keys for the same resource must not be duplicated

Tags.N.Value.description_en:
Tag value for the resource

* Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag value, range: 1–20
* Separate multiple tag values with &
* Length range: 0–256 characters; if not specified, defaults to empty
* Supports input of characters from all languages, numbers, spaces ( ), underscores (_), periods (.), colons (:), slashes (/), equals signs (=), plus signs (+), hyphens (-), and at signs (@)
* Case-sensitive
* If the tag value starts or ends with a space, the system automatically removes it

> If this parameter is provided, Tags.N.Key must be specified first

AutoPlacement.description_cn:
Whether to add the dedicated host to the automatic deployment resource pool. Options:
- On: Add to the automatic deployment resource pool. When creating an Instance, you do not need to specify a DDH. The system will select a suitable DDH from the pool to deploy the Instance.
- Off (default): Do not add to the automatic deployment resource pool. You need to deploy the Instance on a DDH yourself, that is, specify the DDH when creating the Instance.

For instructions on creating an Instance, see [RunInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/RunInstances).

EipAddress.BandwidthMbps.description_en:
Bandwidth limit for public IP. Default value: 1, unit: Mbps
- If `ChargeType` is set to `PayByBandwidth`: range is 1–500
- If `ChargeType` is set to `PayByTraffic`: range is 1–200

EipAddress.BandwidthPackageId.description_en:
The ID of the shared bandwidth package, indicating the public IP will be added to this shared bandwidth package
- You can call the [DescribeBandwidthPackages](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/bandwidthpackage/DescribeBandwidthPackages) API to query the shared bandwidth package ID
- To add a public IP to a shared bandwidth package, all of the following conditions must be met:
  - Both must have the same security protection type
  - Both must be in the same region
  - The public IP must use pay-as-you-go billing
  - The shared bandwidth package must be of IPv4 type

EipAddress.ChargeType.description_en:
Billing methods for public IP addresses:
- PayByBandwidth (default): Pay-As-You-Go by bandwidth cap
- PayByTraffic: Pay-As-You-Go by actual data transfer
- PrePaid: Subscription (monthly or yearly)

When the Instance billing type (`InstanceChargeType`) is set to `PostPaid`, this parameter cannot be set to `PrePaid`.

EipAddress.ISP.description_en:
Line type for public IP. Default is BGP
Available values:
- BGP: BGP (multi-line)
- If your account has static single line access, you can use:
  - ChinaMobile: China Mobile static single line
  - ChinaTelecom: China Telecom static single line
  - ChinaUnicom: China Unicom static single line
- If your account has SingleLine_BGP access, you can use SingleLine_BGP
- If your account has Static_BGP access, you can use Static_BGP

EipAddress.ReleaseWithInstance.description_en:
Whether the public IP is released with the Instance. Only applies to pay-as-you-go public IPs. Options:
- true: The public IP is released with the Instance. When the Instance is automatically recycled by the system (such as 24 hours after unsubscription or upon expiration) or deleted using the [DeleteInstance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DeleteInstance) or [DeleteInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DeleteInstances) APIs, the public IP is released together with the Instance
- false (default): The public IP is not released with the Instance

EipAddress.SecurityProtectionInstanceId.description_en:
DDoS Native Protection (Enterprise Edition) ID
- You can call the [DescInstanceList](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6352/1263659) API to query the DDoS Native Protection (Enterprise Edition) ID.
- This parameter is required when `SecurityProtectionTypes` is set to `AntiDDoS_Enhanced`.

EipAddress.SecurityProtectionTypes.N.description_en:
Security protection types for public IP addresses
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the security protection type. Currently, only 1 is supported
- Values:
  - AntiDDoS_Enhanced: Apply for a public IP address with enhanced protection. It can be added to a DDoS Native Protection (Enterprise Edition) Instance.

        - If `EipAddress.SecurityProtectionTypes.N` is set to `AntiDDoS_Enhanced`, `EipAddress.ChargeType` cannot be `PrePaid`, and `EipAddress.ISP` must be set to `BGP`
    - Enhanced protection public IP addresses are currently in invite-only testing. If you want to try it, contact your account manager to apply.
    
  - Leave blank to apply for a public IP address with default protection

Hostname.description_cn:
Instance hostname refers to the computer name within the instance operating system.

- Linux instance:
  - Letters, numbers, periods ("."), and hyphens ("-") are allowed
  - Cannot start or end with a hyphen or period, and hyphens and periods cannot appear consecutively
  - Length must be between 2 and 63 characters

- Windows instance:
  - Letters, numbers, and hyphens ("-") are allowed; the name cannot be all numbers
  - Cannot start or end with a hyphen, and hyphens cannot appear consecutively
  - Length must be between 2 and 15 characters

- If left blank, the system automatically generates a hostname following the iv- + initial hostname rule, for example: iv-3tigy72q3u3vj0******
- Initial hostname generation logic:
  - Linux: Uses all characters after 'i-' in the instance ID
  - Windows: Uses the last 12 characters after 'i-' in the instance ID

- When creating instances in batches, you can customize sequential hostnames using the `name_prefix[begin_number,bits]name_suffix` format. For details, see [Batch set sequential instance names or hostnames](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Batch-configuring-sequential-instance-names-or-hostnames)

KeyPairName.description_cn:
To log in to an Instance using an SSH key, specify the name of an existing key pair.
You can call [DescribeKeyPairs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeKeyPairs) to view existing key pairs. If none are available, call [CreateKeyPair](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/CreateKeyPair) to create a new key pair.
- Windows Instances do not support SSH key login. Even if you provide this parameter, only the password (`Password`) is used.
- Linux Instances support login with either a password or a key pair. If you set both `KeyPairName` and `Password` when calling this API, only the key pair (`KeyPairName`) will be used.
KeyPairName.description_en:
To log in to an Instance using an SSH key, specify the name of an existing key pair.
You can call [DescribeKeyPairs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeKeyPairs) to view existing key pairs. If none are available, call [CreateKeyPair](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/CreateKeyPair) to create a new key pair.
- Windows Instances do not support SSH key login. Even if you provide this parameter, only the password (`Password`) is used.
- Linux Instances support login with either a password or a key pair. If you set both `KeyPairName` and `Password` when calling this API, only the key pair (`KeyPairName`) will be used.

NetworkInterfaces.N.Ipv6AddressCount.description_en:
Number of private IPv6 addresses assigned to the primary NIC. Only 1 is supported
- When you specify this parameter, the system automatically assigns the same number of available private IPv6 addresses from the subnet associated with the NIC as the NIC's private IPv6 addresses
- You can assign an IPv6 address only to the primary NIC when creating an instance. To assign an IPv6 address to a secondary NIC, see [CreateNetworkInterface](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/CreateNetworkInterface)
- Parameter - N: Indicates the NIC index. N = 1 refers to the primary NIC; N ≥ 2 refers to secondary NICs. If you specify N ≥ 2, this parameter will be ignored
Assigning IPv6 addresses to NICs is currently in invite-only testing. Only accounts that have completed [Enterprise Verification](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6261/64937) can apply for a trial. To request access, contact your account manager

NetworkInterfaces.N.SecurityGroupIds.N.description_en:
Security group IDs associated with the network interface
- The first N indicates the network interface number: N = 1 for the primary network interface; N ≥ 2 for secondary network interfaces
- The second N indicates the security group sequence number for the network interface, ranging from 1 to 5
- Separate multiple security group IDs with &

NetworkInterfaces.N.SubnetId.N.description_en:
Private network subnet ID list for the Instance
- The first N: Indicates the network interface index. N = 1 indicates the primary network interface; N ≥ 2 indicates secondary network interfaces
- The second N: Indicates the list of private network subnets for that network interface
- Use & to separate multiple private network subnet IDs
If you provide subnet ID lists from multiple availability zones, the system will select and bind the subnet that matches the availability zone recommended by the 'Random Availability Zone' feature

Password.description_cn:
To log in to the Instance using the 'Password' method, specify the initial administrator password for the Instance with this parameter. The Linux administrator account is root, and the Windows administrator account is Administrator.
Password complexity requirements:
- Length must be between 8 and 30 characters
- Passwords can only contain uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, and must include at least three of these types
- Allowed special characters: `~!@#$%^&*()_-+=|{}[]:;'<>,.?/
- Passwords cannot start with '/' or '$6$'
Login credentials support three methods: 'Password', 'Key Pair', and 'Retain Image Settings'. When using the 'Password' method to log in to the Instance, we recommend increasing password complexity for better security.

Placement.Affinity.description_en:
For ECS dedicated host instances in stopped with savings mode, some resources are released after the instance stops. This parameter lets you choose whether to keep the dedicated host instance deployed on the original dedicated host when it restarts. Options:

- Host: When you restart a dedicated host instance in stopped with savings mode, it remains on the original dedicated host.
- Default (default): When you restart a dedicated host instance in stopped with savings mode, the instance will preferentially migrate to a dedicated host that supports automatic deployment. If there are insufficient resources on such hosts, the instance will start on the original dedicated host.

Placement.DedicatedHostClusterId.description_en: This is the dedicated host cluster ID where the instance resides. You can call the [DescribeDedicatedHostClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6396/1253698) API to query the dedicated host cluster ID.

Placement.Tenancy.description_en:
Choose whether to create the instance on a dedicated host:
- Default: Create a regular cloud server instance
- Host: Create a dedicated host instance. If you do not specify `Placement.DedicatedHostId`, the system will automatically select a dedicated host for the instance
For supported instance specifications on dedicated hosts, see [Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6396/1253643).

SpotStrategy.description_cn:
Preemptible policy for pay-as-you-go Instances. Options:
- NoSpot (default): Create a standard pay-as-you-go Instance
- SpotAsPriceGo: System sets the bid automatically, following the current market price for preemptible Instances
- SpotWithPriceLimit: Preemptible Instance with a custom bid limit
- This parameter takes effect when `InstanceChargeType` is set to `PostPaid`
- For details on preemptible Instance bidding modes, see [Purchase Preemptible Instances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Buying_spot_instance)

Tags.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key for user tags
- Parameter - N: Indicates the index of the tag key, valid range: 1–20
- Separate multiple tag keys with &

Naming rules:
- Must not start with any case combination of `volc:` or `sys:`
- Only letters, numbers, spaces, and the following symbols are allowed: "_", ".", ":", "/", "=", "+", "-", "@"
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
Tag keys for the same resource must be unique

Tags.N.Value.description_en:
Tag value for the user tag
- Parameter - N: Indicates the tag value's sequence number, range: 1–20

Naming rules:

- Can be empty; length must be 0–256 characters
If you specify this parameter, you must first specify `Tags.N.Key`

UniqueSuffix.description_cn:
Indicates whether to automatically add a sequential suffix to `Hostname` and `InstanceName` when creating multiple instances. Options:
- true: Enable sequential suffix
- false (default): Disable sequential suffix
- If sequential suffix is enabled and `Hostname` is empty, the system will automatically generate a hostname without a sequential suffix
- If sequential suffix is enabled and you specify the `[begin_number,bits]` naming format for `Hostname` or `InstanceName`, see [Set sequential instance or host names in bulk](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Batch-configuring-sequential-instance-names-or-hostnames#openapi) for how the names will ultimately be set

Volumes.N.DeleteWithInstance.description_en:
Whether the cloud disk is released with the instance. Values:
- true (default): The cloud disk is released with the instance
- false: The cloud disk is not released with the instance
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk sequence number. Value range: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk, which is always released with the instance and cannot be retained; N ≥ 2 refers to data disks, which can be set to release with the instance or not
- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceIOPS.description_en:
Extra IOPS performance for cloud disks, supported only by ESSD FlexPL data disks. Unit: operations/second

Set this parameter when `ExtraPerformanceTypeId` is set to `Balance` or `IOPS`. The valid value ranges for each type are:
- IOPS type: 1–50000
- Balance type: 1–50000

- Parameter - N: Indicates the cloud disk sequence number. Valid values: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; when N is 1, this parameter is ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can set this parameter for data disks.
- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceThroughputMB.description_en:
Extra disk throughput (MB/s). Supported only for ESSD FlexPL data disks.

Set this parameter when `ExtraPerformanceTypeId` is set to `Throughput`.
Value range: 1–650.

- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk sequence number. Valid values: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; if N is set to 1, this parameter will be ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can set this parameter normally.
- Use & to separate multiple disks.

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceTypeId.description_en:
Types of extra disk performance supported only by ESSD FlexPL data disks. Options:
- Balance: Balanced extra performance
- IOPS: IOPS-based extra performance
- Throughput: Throughput-based extra performance

For more information about extra performance, see [Extra Disk Performance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/essd_flexpl_volume).

- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk index, valid values: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; when N is 1, this parameter is ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can set this parameter for data disks.
- Use & to separate multiple disks.

Volumes.N.Size.description_en:
Cloud disk capacity, in GiB. N ranges from 1 to 16. N = 1 indicates a system disk; N ≥ 2 indicates a data disk. Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.

Cloud disk capacity ranges:
- System disk:
  - ESSD_PL0: 20–2048
  - ESSD_FlexPL: 20–2048
Default: max{40, the image size for the specified ImageId}.


- Data disk:
  - ESSD_PL0: 10–32768
  - ESSD_FlexPL: 10–32768
If this parameter is not specified, the data disk capacity uses the snapshot size of `Volumes.N.SnapshotId`. If `Volumes.N.SnapshotId` is not provided, an error LimitExceeded.DataVolumeSize is returned.

Volumes.N.SnapshotId.description_en:
Create a cloud disk from a snapshot. Only data disks are supported. You can use the [DescribeSnapshots](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Describesnapshots) API to query the snapshot ID.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the cloud disk. Valid values: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; when N is set to 1, this parameter is ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can specify the target data disk snapshot ID.
- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.
- Only Ultra SSDs support creating cloud disks from snapshots. Performance SSDs do not support snapshot-related features.
- Only snapshots in the 'Available' state can be used to create new cloud disks. Snapshots in 'Creating', 'Rolling Back', 'Deleting', or 'Error' states cannot be used to create new cloud disks.

Volumes.N.VolumeType.description_en:
Cloud disk type, possible values:
- ESSD_PL0 (default): Ultra-fast SSD PL0
- ESSD_FlexPL: Ultra-fast SSD FlexPL
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk number, value range: 1–16. N = 1 indicates the system disk; N ≥ 2 indicate data disks
- Separate multiple cloud disks with &

CommandContent.description_cn:
Command content

- Enter the command content according to the `ContentEncoding` parameter
- Make sure the first line of your script specifies the interpreter as follows before encoding:
    - For shell scripts: The first line must be `#!/bin/bash`
    - For Python scripts: The first line must be `#!/usr/bin/python`
- Command content must not exceed 16 KB
- When `EnableParameter=true`, command content supports custom parameters:
    - Define custom parameters using double curly braces `{{}}`
    - Spaces and line breaks before and after parameter names inside `{{}}` are ignored

Eip.Bandwidth.description_en:
Maximum bandwidth for public IP, unit: Mbps

- Value range: 1–500
- Default value: 1

 tip
When you configure Eip.Bandwidth or Eip.ISP, the scaling group assigns a public IP to the Instance when it is created. By default, billing is pay-as-you-go—based on fixed bandwidth.

Eip.BandwidthPackageId.description_en:
Shared bandwidth package ID, used to add a public IP to a shared bandwidth package. You can call the [DescribeBandwidthPackages](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/bandwidthpackage/DescribeBandwidthPackages) API to query the shared bandwidth package ID. To add a public IP to a shared bandwidth package, the following conditions must be met:

- Both must have the same security protection type
- Both must have the same line type
- The shared bandwidth package must be of IPv4 type

Eip.BillingType.description_en:
Public IP billing method possible values:

- 2: Pay-As-You-Go (by bandwidth cap)
- 3: Pay-As-You-Go (by actual traffic)

Eip.ISP.description_en:
Public IP line type options:

- BGP: BGP (multi-line)

- If your account has applied for and enabled static single-line permission, you can use the following values:
    - ChinaMobile: China Mobile static single-line
    - ChinaTelecom: China Telecom static single-line
    - ChinaUnicom: China Unicom static single-line

 tip
When you configure Eip.Bandwidth or Eip.ISP, the scaling group assigns a public IP when creating an Instance. By default, billing is pay-as-you-go with fixed bandwidth pricing.

Eip.ReleaseWithInstance.description_en:
Whether the public IP is released when the Instance is deleted applies only to pay-as-you-go public IPs. Options: 
- true: The public IP is released with the Instance. When the Instance is automatically recycled by the system (such as 24 hours after unsubscribing or upon expiration) or deleted using the [DeleteInstance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DeleteInstance) or [DeleteInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DeleteInstances) APIs, the public IP is released together with the Instance. 
- false (default): The public IP is not released when the Instance is deleted.

Eip.SecurityProtectionInstanceId.description_en:
DDoS Native Protection (Enterprise Edition) ID.

- You can call the [DescInstanceList](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6352/1282916) API to query the ID of DDoS Native Protection (Enterprise Edition).

- When SecurityProtectionTypes.N is set to AntiDDoS_Enhanced, this parameter is required.

Eip.SecurityProtectionTypes.N.description_en:
Security protection types for public IP addresses

- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the security protection type. Currently, only 1 is supported

- Value:

    - AntiDDoS_Enhanced: Apply for a public IP address with enhanced protection. Can be added to a DDoS Native Protection (Enterprise Edition) instance

 tip

- If AntiDDoS_Enhanced is specified, EipAddress.ChargeType cannot be PrePaid, and EipAddress.ISP must be set to BGP

- Enhanced protection public IP addresses are currently in invitation-only testing. To request a trial, please [submit a ticket](https://console.volcengine.com/workorder/create/) or contact your account manager

HostName.description_cn:
Instance hostname requirements:

- You can use periods (.) to separate the hostname into segments
- Each segment can contain letters, numbers, or hyphens (-)
- The hostname cannot start or end with a hyphen (-) or period (.), and hyphens or periods cannot appear consecutively
- For Linux, the hostname must be 2 to 59 characters long
- For Windows, the hostname must be 2 to 10 characters long, cannot contain periods (.), and cannot be entirely numeric

If not specified, the hostname is generated automatically as follows:

- Format: iv- + initial hostname, for example iv-3tigy72q3u3vj0******
- Initial hostname generation:
  - Linux: uses all characters after 'i-' in the Instance ID
  - Windows: uses the 12 characters immediately following 'i-' in the Instance ID

Volumes.N.DeleteWithInstance.description_en:
Whether the cloud disk is released with the Instance

- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk index. Valid values: 1–15. N = 1 refers to the system disk, which is always released with the Instance by default and cannot be retained. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks.

- Value - DeleteWithInstance: Specifies whether the cloud disk is released with the Instance.

    - true (default): The cloud disk is released with the Instance. Setting this to false has no effect on the system disk; the system disk is always released with the Instance and cannot be retained.

    - false: The cloud disk is not released with the Instance.

- Use '&' to separate multiple cloud disks.

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceIOPS.description_en:
Extra IOPS performance for cloud disks, supported only by ESSD FlexPL data disks. Unit: operations per second. Set this parameter when `ExtraPerformanceTypeId` is `Balance` or `IOPS`. The valid range for extra performance is:
- IOPS type: 1–50000
- Balance type: 1–50000
- Parameter N indicates the disk index. Valid values: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; this parameter is ignored when N is 1. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can set this parameter for data disks.
- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceThroughputMB.description_en:
Extra cloud disk throughput performance size (MB/s). Supported only for ESSD FlexPL data disks. Set this parameter when `ExtraPerformanceTypeId` is `Throughput`. Valid range: 1–650.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the cloud disk index. Valid values: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; this parameter is ignored when N is 1. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can set this parameter for these disks.
- Separate multiple cloud disks with &

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceTypeId.description_en:
Types of additional disk performance, supported only by ESSD FlexPL data disks. For more information, see [Additional Disk Performance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/essd_flexpl_volume). Available values: 
- Balance: Balanced performance
- IOPS: IOPS performance
- Throughput: Throughput performance
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk index. Valid range: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; when N is set to 1, this parameter is ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can set this parameter normally.
- Use & to separate multiple disks.

Volumes.N.Size.description_en:
Cloud disk capacity

- Parameter - N: Indicates the cloud disk number. Valid values: 1–15. N = 1 indicates the system disk; N ≥ 2 indicates data disks

- Value - Size: Indicates the cloud disk capacity in GiB. Valid values:

- System disk:
    - ESSD_PL0: 20–2048
    - PTSSD: 10–500

- Data disk:
    - ESSD_PL0: 10–32768
    - PTSSD: 20–8192

- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks

Volumes.N.SnapshotId.description_en:
Use snapshots to create cloud disks; only data disks can be created using snapshots. You can call the [DescribeSnapshots](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Describesnapshots) API to query snapshot IDs
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk sequence number, with a value range of 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; when N is 1, this parameter is ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can specify the target data disk snapshot ID
- Separate multiple cloud disks with &
- Only Extreme SSDs support creating cloud disks from snapshots. Performance SSDs do not support snapshot-related features
- Only snapshots with the status 'Available' can be used to create new cloud disks. Snapshots in 'Creating', 'Rolling Back', 'Deleting', or 'Error' status cannot be used to create new cloud disks

Volumes.N.VolumeType.description_en:
Cloud disk types

- Parameter - N: Indicates the cloud disk index. Valid values: 1–15. N = 1 is the system disk; N ≥ 2 are data disks

- Parameter - VolumeType: Indicates the cloud disk type. Valid values:
    - ESSD_PL0: Ultra-fast SSD PL0
    - PTSSD: Performance SSD

- Separate multiple cloud disks with &

Eip.BandwidthPackageId.description_en:
Shared bandwidth package ID, used to add a public IP to a shared bandwidth package. You can call the [DescribeBandwidthPackages](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/bandwidthpackage/DescribeBandwidthPackages) API to query the shared bandwidth package ID. To add a public IP to a shared bandwidth package, the following conditions must be met:

- Both must have the same security protection type
- Both must have the same line type
- The shared bandwidth package must be of IPv4 type

Eip.BillingType.description_en:
Public IP billing method options:

- 2: Pay-As-You-Go – Billed by bandwidth cap
- 3: Pay-As-You-Go – Billed by actual data usage

Eip.ISP.description_en:
Public IP line type options:

- BGP: BGP (multi-line)

- If your account has applied for and enabled static single-line access, you can use the following values:

    - ChinaMobile: China Mobile static single-line
    - ChinaTelecom: China Telecom static single-line
    - ChinaUnicom: China Unicom static single-line

Eip.ReleaseWithInstance.description_en:
Whether the public IP is deleted along with the Instance applies only to pay-as-you-go public IPs. Options: 
- true: The public IP is deleted with the Instance. When the Instance is automatically reclaimed by the system (such as 24 hours after unsubscribing or upon expiration) or deleted using the [DeleteInstance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DeleteInstance) or [DeleteInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DeleteInstances) APIs, the public IP is released together with the Instance. 
- false (default): The public IP is not deleted with the Instance.

Eip.SecurityProtectionInstanceId.description_en:

- You can call the [DescInstanceList](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6352/1263659) API to query the ID of DDoS Native Protection (Enterprise Edition).

- When SecurityProtectionTypes.N is set to AntiDDoS_Enhanced, this parameter is required.

Eip.SecurityProtectionTypes.N.description_en:
Security protection types for public IP addresses

- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the security protection type. Only 1 is supported

- Values:

    - AntiDDoS_Enhanced: Request a public IP address with enhanced protection. You can add it to a DDoS Native Protection (Enterprise Edition) instance

 tip

- If you select AntiDDoS_Enhanced, EipAddress.ChargeType cannot be PrePaid, and EipAddress.ISP must be set to BGP

- Enhanced protection public IP addresses are currently in invitation-only testing. To request a trial, please [submit a ticket](https://console.volcengine.com/workorder/create/) or contact your account manager
 

- Leave blank to indicate a public IP address with basic protection

HostName.description_cn:
Instance hostname requirements:

- You can use periods (.) to separate the hostname into multiple segments
- Each segment can contain letters, numbers, or hyphens (-)
- The hostname cannot start or end with a hyphen (-) or period (.), and cannot contain consecutive hyphens or periods
- For Linux, the hostname must be 2–59 characters long
- For Windows, the hostname must be 2–10 characters long, cannot contain periods (.), and cannot be composed entirely of numbers

If left blank, the hostname is generated automatically as follows:

- Format: iv- + initial hostname, for example iv-3tigy72q3u3vj0******
- Initial hostname generation logic:
  - Linux: uses all characters after 'i-' in the Instance ID
  - Windows: uses the last 12 characters after 'i-' in the Instance ID

Volumes.N.SnapshotId.description_en:
Create cloud disks from snapshots; only data disks are supported. You can use the [DescribeSnapshots](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Describesnapshots) API to query snapshot IDs.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the cloud disk sequence number, valid values are 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; when N is set to 1, this parameter is ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can specify the target data disk snapshot ID.
- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.
- Only Extreme SSDs support creating cloud disks from snapshots; Performance SSDs do not support snapshot-related features.
- Only snapshots with 'available' status can be used to create new cloud disks. Snapshots in 'creating', 'rolling back', 'deleting', or 'error' status cannot be used to create new cloud disks.

Volumes.N.VolumeType.description_en:
Cloud disk type.

- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the cloud disk, value range: 1–15. N = 1 indicates the system disk, N ≥ 2 indicates a data disk.

- Parameter - VolumeType: Indicates the type of cloud disk, possible values:

    - ESSD_PL0: Ultra-fast SSD PL0

    - PTSSD: Performance SSD

- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.

VpcId.description_cn: Private network ID. You can use the [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) API to query private networks that meet the criteria.
VpcId.description_en: Private network ID. You can use the [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) API to query private networks that meet the criteria.

ZoneId.description_cn: The availability zone ID of the Instance. You can call the [DescribeZones](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeZones) API to query availability zone information for a region.
ZoneId.description_en: The availability zone ID of the Instance. You can call the [DescribeZones](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeZones) API to query availability zone information for a region.

AutoReleaseAt.description_cn:
The instance auto release time must be set to a 10-minute mark (e.g., :00, :10, :20, etc.).
When `ElasticScheduledInstanceType` is set to Segmented, you must specify this parameter. Valid values are:
- If `DeliveryType` is Reserve, the earliest instance release time is one hour after the reserved delivery time slot, rounded up to the next 10-minute mark.
- If `DeliveryType` is Immediate, the earliest instance release time is the next 10-minute mark after the current time. For example, if the current time is 5:02, the earliest auto release time is 5:20.

Count.description_cn:

  - When `DeliveryType` is `Immediate`, the valid range is 1–100
Entering 0 defaults to 1

CpuMaxFrequency.description_cn:
Specify the maximum CPU frequency in GHz. The value must be between the CPU's base frequency and turbo frequency.
- Currently, only g3al (4xlarge, 8xlarge, 16xlarge, 32xlarge), c3al (4xlarge, 8xlarge, 16xlarge, 32xlarge), r3al (4xlarge, 8xlarge, 16xlarge), g4i, c4i, r4i, g4ie, c4ie, and r4ie Instances support this parameter. For details on base/turbo frequencies and more information, see [Instance specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Introduction-to-instance-types).
- This feature is currently in invite-only testing. To use it, please contact your account manager.

DryRun.description_cn:
Whether to only pre-check this request. Options:
- true: Sends a validation request without creating an Instance. The validation checks for required parameters, request format, business restrictions, and ECS inventory. If validation fails, the corresponding error is returned. If validation passes, the error code DryRunOperation is returned.
    When DryRun is set to `true`, if the `Count` or `Mincount` parameter is provided, its value must be 1.
  
- false (default): Sends a normal request. If validation passes, the Instance is created directly.

EipAddress.BandwidthMbps.description_en:
The bandwidth limit for a public IP is 1 Mbps by default.
- When `ChargeType` is set to `PayByBandwidth`: range is 1–500 Mbps
- When `ChargeType` is set to `PayByTraffic`: range is 1–200 Mbps

EipAddress.BandwidthPackageId.description_en:
The ID of the shared bandwidth package, required when adding a public IP to a shared bandwidth package
- You can call the [DescribeBandwidthPackages](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/bandwidthpackage/DescribeBandwidthPackages) API to query the shared bandwidth package ID
- To add a public IP to a shared bandwidth package, the following conditions must be met:
  - Both must have the same security protection type
  - Both must be in the same region
  - The public IP must use pay-as-you-go billing
  - The shared bandwidth package must be of IPv4 type

EipAddress.ChargeType.description_en:
Billing methods for public IP addresses:
- PayByBandwidth (default): Pay-as-you-go—billed by bandwidth cap
- PayByTraffic: Pay-as-you-go—billed by actual data transfer
- PrePaid: Subscription (monthly or yearly)
When the instance billing type (`InstanceChargeType`) is set to `PostPaid`, this parameter cannot be set to `PrePaid`.

EipAddress.ISP.description_en:
The line type for public IP addresses. The default is BGP. Available values:
- BGP: BGP (multi-line)
- If your account has applied for and enabled static single-line access, you can use the following values:
  - ChinaMobile: China Mobile static single-line
  - ChinaTelecom: China Telecom static single-line
  - ChinaUnicom: China Unicom static single-line
- If your account has applied for and enabled BGP single-line access, you can use SingleLine_BGP
- If your account has applied for and enabled static BGP access, you can use Static_BGP

EipAddress.ReleaseWithInstance.description_en:
Whether the public IP is deleted with the instance. Options:
- true: The public IP is deleted with the instance
- false (default): The public IP is not deleted with the instance

EipAddress.SecurityProtectionInstanceId.description_en:
DDoS Native Protection (Enterprise Edition) ID
- You can call the [DescInstanceList](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6352/1263659) API to query the DDoS Native Protection (Enterprise Edition) ID
- When `SecurityProtectionTypes` is set to `AntiDDoS_Enhanced`, this parameter is required

EipAddress.SecurityProtectionTypes.N.description_en:
Security protection types for public IP addresses
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the security protection type. Currently, only 1 is supported
- Values:
   - AntiDDoS_Enhanced: Apply for a public IP address with enhanced protection. You can add it to a DDoS Native Protection (Enterprise Edition) instance
          - If `EipAddress.SecurityProtectionTypes.N` is set to `AntiDDoS_Enhanced`, `EipAddress.ChargeType` cannot be `PrePaid`, and `EipAddress.ISP` must be set to `BGP`
     - Enhanced protection public IP addresses are currently in invite-only testing. To request a trial, contact your account manager to apply
     
   - Leave blank to apply for a public IP address with default protection

ElasticScheduledInstanceType.description_cn:
Flexible Reserved Instance type. Options:
- Esi (default): Flexible Reserved Instance
- Time-Segmented: Flexible Reserved Instance - Time-Segmented
Flexible Reserved Instance - Time-Segmented is currently in invite-only testing. To request access, please contact your account manager.

EndDeliveryAt.description_cn:
The instance end delivery time must be set to a 10-minute mark, and the interval between the end delivery time and `StartDeliveryAt` must be 10 minutes
- When `ElasticScheduledInstanceType` is set to `Esi`, the instance end delivery time must be within 4 to 8 hours after the reservation
- When `ElasticScheduledInstanceType` is set to `Segmented`:
  - If `DeliveryType` is `Reserve`, the instance end delivery time must be within 24 hours after the reservation
  - If `DeliveryType` is `Immediate`, you do not need to provide this parameter

Hostname.description_cn:
The instance hostname is the computer name used within the instance's operating system.
- Linux instance:
  - Letters, numbers, periods ("."), and hyphens ("-") are allowed
  - Cannot start or end with a hyphen or period
  - Cannot use hyphens or periods consecutively, or use a hyphen and period together
  - Length must be between 2 and 63 characters

- Windows instance:
  - Letters, numbers, and hyphens ("-") are allowed; cannot be all numbers
  - Cannot start or end with a hyphen, and cannot use hyphens consecutively
  - Length must be between 2 and 15 characters

- If left blank, the hostname is automatically generated using the rule iv- + initial hostname, for example: iv-3tigy72q3u3vj0******
- Initial hostname generation logic:
  - Linux: Extract all characters after 'i-' in the instance ID
  - Windows: Extract the last 12 characters after 'i-' in the instance ID

- When creating instances in batches, you can customize sequential hostnames using the format `name_prefix[begin_number,bits]name_suffix`. For details, see [Batch set sequential instance names or hostnames](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Batch-configuring-sequential-instance-names-or-hostnames)

InstanceName.description_cn:

KeepImageCredential.description_cn:
Retain image settings. Options:
- true: Retain image settings. The instance will use the preset password or key pair from the image for login.
- false (default): Do not retain image settings.
- Only custom images and shared images support this feature.
- When this parameter is set to `true`, do not specify `PassWord` or `KeyPairName`.

KeyPairName.description_cn:
To log in to an Instance using SSH key authentication, specify the name of an existing key pair.
You can call [DescribeKeyPairs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeKeyPairs) to view existing key pairs. If none are available, call [CreateKeyPair](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/CreateKeyPair) to create a key pair.
- Windows Instances do not support SSH key authentication. Even if you provide this parameter, only the password (`Password`) is used.
- Linux Instances support login with either a password or a key pair. If you set both `KeyPairName` and `Password` when calling this API, only the key pair (`KeyPairName`) is used.

MinCount.description_cn:
Specify the minimum creation quantity for elastic reservation instances. Value range:

- ESI-General, ESI-Scheduled (Reserved Delivery): 1–500
- ESI-Scheduled (Immediate Delivery): 1–100

- Minimum instance creation quantity `MinCount` ≤ creation quantity `Count`
- If inventory > creation quantity `Count`, create according to `Count`
- If minimum creation quantity `MinCount` ≤ inventory ≤ creation quantity `Count`, create according to inventory
- If inventory < minimum creation quantity `MinCount`, creation fails due to insufficient inventory

NetworkInterfaces.N.PrimaryIpAddress.description_en:
Specify the primary IP address for a network interface. Currently, you can specify only one primary IP address, either for the primary network interface or for a secondary network interface.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the interface number. N = 1 refers to the primary network interface; N ≥ 2 refers to secondary network interfaces.
- Use & to separate multiple interfaces

NetworkInterfaces.N.PrivateIpAddresses.N.description_en:
Specify the secondary IP address for the primary network interface card. Currently, only the primary NIC supports secondary IP assignment
- The first N indicates the index of the primary NIC. Only one primary NIC can be bound at this time
- The second N indicates the index of the secondary IP on the primary NIC. The maximum number of assignable secondary IP addresses is the number of private IPs per NIC for this [Instance specification](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Introduction-to-instance-types) minus one primary private IP
- Use & to separate multiple secondary IP addresses

NetworkInterfaces.N.SecurityGroupIds.N.description_en:
Security group ID associated with the network interface card.
- The first N indicates the NIC sequence number. N = 1 means the primary NIC; N ≥ 2 means secondary NICs.
- The second N indicates the sequence number of the security group associated with the NIC. Valid values: 1–5.
- Use & to separate multiple security group IDs.

NetworkInterfaces.N.SubnetId.description_en:
The private subnet ID of the instance. You can attach secondary network interfaces when creating the instance.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the network interface number. N = 1 refers to the primary network interface; N ≥ 2 refers to secondary network interfaces.
- Separate multiple private subnet IDs with &

Password.description_cn:
To log in to the Instance using the password method, specify the initial login password for the administrator account with this parameter. The Linux administrator account is root, and the Windows administrator account is Administrator.
Password complexity requirements:
- Length must be between 8 and 30 characters
- Passwords can only contain uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, and must include at least three of these types
- Allowed special characters: `~!@#$%^&*()_-+=|{}[]:;'<>,.?/
- Passwords cannot start with "/" or "$6$"
Login credentials support three methods: password, key pair, and reserved image settings. When logging in to the Instance using a password, we recommend increasing password complexity to enhance security.

To log in to the Instance using the password method, specify the initial login password for the administrator account with this parameter. The Linux administrator account is root, and the Windows administrator account is Administrator.

Tags.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key for user tags
- Parameter - N: Indicates the index of the tag key, with a value range of 1–20

Volumes.N.DeleteWithInstance.description_en:
Whether the cloud disk is released with the instance. Values:
- true (default): The cloud disk is released with the instance
- false: The cloud disk is not released with the instance
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk number, valid range: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk, which is always released with the instance and cannot be retained. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks, which can be set to release with the instance or not.
- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceIOPS.description_en:
Extra IOPS performance for cloud disks, supported only by ESSD FlexPL data disks. Unit: operations/second.

Set this parameter when `ExtraPerformanceTypeId` is set to `Balance` or `IOPS`. The valid range for each type is:
- IOPS: 1–50000
- Balance: 1–50000

- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk sequence number. Valid values: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; if N is set to 1, this parameter will be ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can set this parameter normally.
- Use & to separate multiple disks.

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceThroughputMB.description_en:
Extra cloud disk throughput (MB/s), supported only by ESSD FlexPL data disks

Set this parameter when `ExtraPerformanceTypeId` is set to `Throughput`
Value range: 1–650

- Parameter - N: Indicates the cloud disk number, valid values: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; if N is 1, this parameter will be ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can set this parameter for these disks
- Separate multiple cloud disks with &

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceTypeId.description_en:
Type of additional disk performance, supported only by ESSD FlexPL data disks. Options:
- Balance: Balanced performance
- IOPS: IOPS performance
- Throughput: Throughput performance
For more information about additional performance, see [Additional Disk Performance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/essd_flexpl_volume).

- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk number, with a valid range of 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; when N is set to 1, this parameter is ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; this parameter is valid.
- Use & to separate multiple disks

Volumes.N.Size.description_en:
Cloud disk capacity, in GiB. N ranges from 1 to 16. N = 1 indicates a system disk; N ≥ 2 indicates a data disk. Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.

Cloud disk capacity ranges:
- System disk:
  - ESSD_PL0: 20–2048
  - ESSD_FlexPL: 20–2048
    Default: max{40, image size of the specified ImageId}
  

- Data disk:
  - ESSD_PL0: 10–32768
  - ESSD_FlexPL: 10–32768
    If this parameter is not specified, the data disk capacity will use the snapshot size of `Volumes.N.SnapshotId`. If `Volumes.N.SnapshotId` is not provided, an error LimitExceeded.DataVolumeSize will be returned.

Volumes.N.SnapshotId.description_en:
Create a cloud disk from a snapshot. Only data disks are supported. You can use the [DescribeSnapshots](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Describesnapshots) API to query the snapshot ID.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the cloud disk sequence number, ranging from 1 to 16. N = 1 refers to the system disk. When N is set to 1, this parameter is ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to a data disk; you can specify the target data disk snapshot ID.
- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.
- Only Ultra SSDs support creating cloud disks from snapshots. Performance SSDs do not support snapshot-related features.
- Only snapshots with the 'Available' status can be used to create new cloud disks. Snapshots in 'Creating', 'Rolling Back', 'Deleting', or 'Error' status cannot be used to create new cloud disks.

Volumes.N.VolumeType.description_en:
Cloud disk types and values:
- ESSD_PL0: Ultra-fast SSD PL0
- ESSD_FlexPL: Ultra-fast SSD FlexPL
- Parameter - N: Indicates the cloud disk number. Valid range: 1–16. N = 1 is the system disk; N ≥ 2 are data disks.
- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.

InvocationStatus.description_cn:
Job status. Determined by the command execution status on all instances specified by the job. Possible values:

- Pending: The command is waiting for validation and scheduling. If any instance has a command status of Pending, the job status is Pending
- Scheduled: The recurring job (Rate) has been scheduled successfully and is waiting to run. If any instance has a command status of Scheduled, the job status is Scheduled
- Running: The job is in progress. If any instance has a command status of Running, the job status is Running
- Success: If all instances have a command status of Success, the job status is Success
- Failed: If all instances have a command status of Failed, the job status is Failed
- Stopped: The recurring or scheduled job was stopped manually
- PartialFailed: In an immediate job, if some instances failed to execute the command, the job status is PartialFailed
- Finished: The recurring job has completed
InvocationStatus.description_en:
Job status. Determined by the command execution status on all instances specified by the job. Possible values:

- Pending: The command is waiting for validation and scheduling. If any instance has a command status of Pending, the job status is Pending
- Scheduled: The recurring job (Rate) has been scheduled successfully and is waiting to run. If any instance has a command status of Scheduled, the job status is Scheduled
- Running: The job is in progress. If any instance has a command status of Running, the job status is Running
- Success: If all instances have a command status of Success, the job status is Success
- Failed: If all instances have a command status of Failed, the job status is Failed
- Stopped: The recurring or scheduled job was stopped manually
- PartialFailed: In an immediate job, if some instances failed to execute the command, the job status is PartialFailed
- Finished: The recurring job has completed

  - Can be empty. Length is limited to 0–256 characters.
- If this parameter is passed, `Tags.N.Key` must be passed first.

Frequency.description_cn:
Execution frequency. This parameter is required only when `RepeatMode=Rate`. Specify the execution interval using a Rate expression in the following format:

- <Interval Value><Interval Unit>
  - Interval unit: Supports minutes (m), hours (h), and days (d). Use for jobs that run at fixed intervals.
  - Interval value range: Minutes 5–60, hours 1–24, days 1–7. The interval must be longer than the job timeout.
- The interval is based on a fixed frequency and does not depend on the actual job duration.
- After the job is created, it runs once at `LaunchTime`, then the next run is scheduled based on the specified interval.

Parameters.description_cn:
When a command includes custom parameters, use this option to pass key-value pairs for those parameters.
For example, if the command is `echo {{name}}`, you can use the `Parameter` option to pass the key-value pair `{"name":"Jack"}`. The custom parameter will automatically replace the variable `name`, generating a new command. The actual command executed will be `echo Jack`. - You can set 0 to 60 custom parameters - Keys cannot be empty strings and can be up to 64 characters long - Values can be empty strings - The combined length of custom parameters and the original command, after Base64 encoding, cannot exceed 16 KB - The set of custom parameter names must be a subset of the parameter set defined when creating the command. Default values will be used for any parameters not provided

CommandContent.description_cn:
The Base64-encoded content of the command.
- Provide the corresponding command content according to the `ContentEncoding` parameter
- Make sure the script specifies the interpreter on the first line before encoding. Follow these rules:
    - For shell scripts: the first line must be `#!/bin/bash`
    - For Python scripts: the first line must be `#!/usr/bin/python`
- Command content cannot exceed 16KB
- When `EnableParameter=true`, custom parameters are supported in the command content. Follow these rules:
    - Define custom parameters using `{{}}`
    - Spaces and line breaks before and after the parameter name inside `{{}}` are ignored

AutoPlacement.description_cn:
Whether to add the dedicated host to the automatic deployment resource pool. Options:
- On: Add to the automatic deployment resource pool. When creating an Instance, you do not need to specify a DDH. The system will select a suitable DDH from the pool to deploy the Instance.
- Off (default): Do not add to the automatic deployment resource pool. You need to deploy the Instance on a DDH yourself, that is, specify the DDH when creating the Instance.

For instructions on creating an Instance, see [RunInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/RunInstances).

DedicatedHostRecovery.description_cn:

- Off (default): Disable automatic failover migration. You can manually replace the physical host by calling [RedeployDedicatedHost](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6396/1253695).

BootMode.description_cn:
Boot mode for the image. Leave blank to keep the current configuration. Options:
- BIOS: BIOS boot mode
- UEFI: UEFI boot mode
* Elastic Bare Metal Instances support only `UEFI` boot mode
* The default for ARM images is `UEFI`, and only `UEFI` can be set
