CpuOptions.CpuAccelerator.description_en:
Enable CPU accelerator. Values:
- CpuAcceleratorOn: Enable CPU accelerator
- CpuAcceleratorOff: Disable CPU accelerator

CpuOptions.HypervisorOff.description_en:
Disable hyper-threading (SMT). Values:
- true: Disable. Each physical core provides only 1 logical thread when disabled.
- false: Enable

CpuOptions.Numa.description_en:
Enable NUMA. Values:
- true: Enable
- false: Disable

CpuOptions.NumaPerSocket.description_en: Number of NUMA nodes per CPU socket.

CpuOptions.ThreadsPerCore.description_en:

CpuOptions.TopologyType.description_en:

- ContinuousCoreToHTMapping: HT continuous mode
- DiscreteCoreToHTMapping: HT discrete mode

- true: Enable instance deletion protection
- false: Disable instance deletion protection

EnableJumboFrame.description_cn:
Whether the Instance enables jumbo frames. Values:
- false: Jumbo frames are disabled. All network interface cards (NICs) of this Instance have an MTU of 1500.
- true: Jumbo frames are enabled. All network interface cards (NICs) of this Instance have an MTU of 8500.
This feature is only supported on certain Instances. For Instances that support jumbo frames, see [Enable/Disable Jumbo Frames](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Enabling_or_Disabling_jumbo_frames).

Hostname.description_cn:
The instance hostname is the computer name inside the instance's operating system.
- Linux instance:
  - Letters, numbers, dots ("."), and hyphens ("-") are allowed.
  - Cannot start or end with a hyphen or dot, and hyphens and dots cannot be used consecutively.
  - Length must be between 2 and 63 characters.
- Windows instance:
  - Letters, numbers, and hyphens ("-") are allowed; the name cannot consist solely of numbers.
  - Cannot start or end with a hyphen, and hyphens cannot be used consecutively.
  - Length must be between 2 and 15 characters.
Hostname.description_en:

  - Length must be between 2 and 63 characters.
- Windows instance:
  - Letters, numbers, and hyphens ("-") are allowed; the name cannot consist solely of numbers.
  - Cannot start or end with a hyphen, and hyphens cannot be used consecutively.
  - Length must be between 2 and 15 characters.

Password.description_cn:
When logging in to the Instance using the password method, set a login password for the Instance
- Password length must be between 8 and 30 characters
- Password can only contain uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, and must include at least three of these types
- Allowed special characters: `~!@#$%^&*()_-+=|{}[]:;'<>,.?/
- Password cannot start with '/' or '$6$'

UserData.description_cn:
Instance custom data lets you customize instance startup behavior and pass in data
- When passing in data, the custom data must be Base64-encoded, and the size of the custom data before encoding cannot exceed 16 KB
- Passing an empty string clears the custom data

AutoPay.description_cn:
Auto Payment Setting:
- true: Auto payment enabled. Make sure your account balance is sufficient. If your balance is insufficient, an exception order will be generated and the billing method change will fail.
- false (default): Only generates the order without charging your account. After the order is created, you can log in to the BytePlus order management page to complete the payment.
If your payment method has insufficient balance, we recommend setting this parameter to `false`.

If your payment method has insufficient balance, we recommend setting this parameter to `false`.

AutoRenew.description_cn:
Whether to automatically renew the Instance after expiration. Values:
- true: auto-renew
- false (default): do not auto-renew
This takes effect only when the `InstanceChargeType` parameter is set to `PrePaid`.

AutoRenewPeriod.description_cn:
Duration of each auto-renewal.
- This parameter is valid only when `AutoRenew` is set to `true`. The default value is 1.
- When `PeriodUnit` is set to `Month`, `AutoRenewPeriod` can be 1, 2, 3, 6, or 12.

DryRun.description_cn:

- true: Sends a validation request without changing the billing mode. Checks include required parameters, request format, business restrictions, and ECS inventory. If validation fails, returns the corresponding error. If validation succeeds, returns the error code DryRunOperation.
- false (default): Sends a normal request. If validation passes, the billing mode is changed immediately.

HttpTokens.description_cn:
Access mode for instance metadata. Specifies whether to enforce hardened mode. Options:
- optional: Not enforced (compatibility mode). You can access instance metadata either directly or using the token-based hardened method.
- required: Enforced (hardened-only mode). Only token-based hardened access to instance metadata is supported.
- For details on how to view metadata and which metadata items are supported, see [View Instance Metadata](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Viewing-instance-metadata).
- Hardened-only mode is currently in invite-only testing. To request access, contact your account manager.

Affinity.description_cn:
Indicates whether the instance is associated with a dedicated host. Possible values:
- Host: The instance is associated with a dedicated host. When you restart an instance with Stop-Save Mode enabled, it will be deployed on the original host.
- Default: When you restart an instance with Stop-Save Mode enabled, it will first try to migrate to a host that supports automatic deployment. If resources are insufficient, the instance will start on the original host.

DedicatedHostId.description_cn:
Target dedicated host ID. You can call the [DescribeDedicatedHosts](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6396/1253691) API to view available dedicated hosts.
- To migrate the instance to a specified dedicated host, you must provide this parameter.
- To migrate the instance to a dedicated host in the system's automatic deployment resource pool, leave this parameter empty and set `Tenancy` to `Host`. For details on automatic deployment, see [Feature Overview](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6396/1253641).

DryRun.description_cn:
Perform pre-check only for this request. Values:
- true: Send a check request without changing the Instance host deployment. The check includes required parameters, request format, business rules, and resource inventory. If the check fails, an error is returned. If the check passes, the error code DryRunOperation is returned.
- false (default): Send a normal request. If the check passes, the Instance host deployment is adjusted immediately.
DryRun.description_en:
Perform pre-check only for this request. Values:

- false (default): Send a normal request. If the check passes, the Instance host deployment is adjusted immediately.

InstanceTypeId.description_cn:
Specify the target instance type for the change. When adjusting the instance's host, you can also change its type. The target instance type must match the specifications of the specified dedicated host.
- This parameter takes effect when `MigrationType` is set to `ColdMigration`.
- To deploy the instance on a DDH after the change, you must specify the value of `DedicatedHostId`. If you want the instance to be placed on a shared host, you do not need to specify this value.
InstanceTypeId.description_en:
Specify the target instance type for the change. When adjusting the instance's host, you can also change its type. The target instance type must match the specifications of the specified dedicated host.
- This parameter takes effect when `MigrationType` is set to `ColdMigration`.
- To deploy the instance on a DDH after the change, you must specify the value of `DedicatedHostId`. If you want the instance to be placed on a shared host, you do not need to specify this value.

MigrationType.description_cn:
Specify the migration method for instances when adjusting their deployment on the host machine. Options:
- LiveMigration: Hot migration (migrates without shutting down). The instance must be in the running state
- ColdMigration: Cold migration (migrates after shutting down). The instance must be stopped. You can also change the instance type
MigrationType.description_en:
Specify the migration method for instances when adjusting their deployment on the host machine. Options:
- LiveMigration: Hot migration (migrates without shutting down). The instance must be in the running state
- ColdMigration: Cold migration (migrates after shutting down). The instance must be stopped. You can also change the instance type

Tenancy.description_cn:
Whether to deploy the instance on a dedicated host. Options:
- Host: If `DedicatedHostId` is not specified, the instance can be deployed in the automatic deployment pool
- Default: The instance can be deployed on a shared host
Tenancy.description_en:

PrimaryIpAddress.description_cn:
The new primary private IP address must be within the subnet CIDR block
- You can call [DescribeNetworkInterfaceAttributes](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeNetworkInterfaceAttributes) to query the primary private IP address of the network interface
- If you do not specify this parameter, the system randomly assigns an address from the subnet CIDR block

SecurityGroupIds.description_cn:
Security group IDs added to the instance after modifying the VPC
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the security group. Valid values: 1–5
- Separate multiple security group IDs with &
- You must provide this parameter only when you specify `VpcId`
- You can call [DescribeSecurityGroups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSecurityGroups) to query security group IDs

SubnetId.description_cn:
New subnet ID
- You cannot specify the subnet ID where the instance currently resides
- If `VpcId` is empty, the new subnet and the original subnet must be in the same availability zone and the same VPC. You can call [DescribeSubnets](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSubnets) to query subnet IDs in the target VPC that are in the same availability zone as the original subnet
- If `VpcId` is not empty, the specified subnet ID must belong to that VPC and be in the same availability zone as the original subnet

- If `VpcId` is empty, the new subnet and the original subnet must be in the same availability zone and the same VPC. You can call [DescribeSubnets](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSubnets) to query subnet IDs in the target VPC that are in the same availability zone as the original subnet
- If `VpcId` is not empty, the specified subnet ID must belong to that VPC and be in the same availability zone as the original subnet

VpcId.description_cn:
Target VPC ID
- If you do not specify this parameter, you change the subnet within the same VPC
- You can call [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) to query available VPCs in the same region as the Instance
VpcId.description_en:

Password.description_cn:

- Length must be between 8 and 30 characters
- Password can only contain uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, and must include at least three of these types
  Allowed special characters: `~!@#$%^&*()_-+=|{}[]:;'<>,.?/
- Cannot start with '/' or '$6$'
- Login credentials support three methods: password, key pair, or keep image settings. When logging in to an Instance using a password, we recommend increasing password complexity for better security
- When `KeepImageCredential` is set to `false`, this parameter and `KeyPairName` cannot both be empty

Frequency.description_cn:
Execution frequency. This parameter is required only when `RepeatMode=Rate`. Specify the execution cycle using a rate expression in the following format:

- <interval value><interval unit>
    - Interval unit: Supports minutes (m), hours (h), and days (d). Use for jobs that run at fixed intervals.
    - Interval value range: 5–60 (minutes), 1–24 (hours), 1–7 (days). The interval must be longer than the job's timeout period.
- The execution interval is based on a fixed frequency and is not affected by the actual job duration.
- After the job is created, it runs once at `LaunchTime`. The next execution time is determined by the specified interval.

Parameters.description_cn:
When a command includes custom parameters, use this parameter to provide key-value pairs for those parameters. For example, if the command is `echo {{name}}`, you can pass the key-value pair `{"name":"Jack"}` using the `Parameter` parameter. The custom parameter will automatically replace the variable `name`, resulting in a new command: `echo Jack`.
Custom parameter rules: - You can set 0 to 60 custom parameters - Keys cannot be empty and can be up to 64 characters - Values can be empty - The combined length of the custom parameters and the original command, after Base64 encoding, cannot exceed 16 KB - The set of custom parameter names must be a subset of the parameter set defined when the command was created. Default values will be used for any parameters not provided

CreditSpecification.description_en:

- Standard: Standard mode
- Unlimited: No performance constraints (not supported yet)
- This parameter takes effect only when `InstanceTypeId` is set to an ecs.t2 series, that is, a burstable performance Instance.
- If not specified or left empty, the burstable performance Instance defaults to Standard mode.

DeletionProtection.description_cn:
Instance deletion protection attribute. Specifies whether deletion of the instance through the console or API is allowed. Values:
- true: Enable instance deletion protection
- false (default): Disable instance deletion protection
DeletionProtection.description_en:
Instance deletion protection attribute. Specifies whether deletion of the instance through the console or API is allowed. Values:
- true: Enable instance deletion protection
- false (default): Disable instance deletion protection

DeploymentSetGroupNumber.description_cn: When an ECS instance is to join or adjust its deployment set policy to AvailabilityGroup, you can use this parameter to specify the instance's group number within the deployment set. Valid values: 1 to 7
DeploymentSetGroupNumber.description_en: When an ECS instance is to join or adjust its deployment set policy to AvailabilityGroup, you can use this parameter to specify the instance's group number within the deployment set. Valid values: 1 to 7

DeploymentSetId.description_cn: Deployment set ID the instance needs to join
DeploymentSetId.description_en: Deployment set ID the instance needs to join

Description.description_cn:
Instance description (default: empty string)
- Must start with a letter or Chinese character
- Can only include Chinese characters, letters, numbers, period (.), space, underscore (_), hyphen (-), equals sign (=), English comma (,), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。)
- Maximum length: 255 characters
Description.description_en:
Instance description (default: empty string)
- Must start with a letter or Chinese character
- Can only include Chinese characters, letters, numbers, period (.), space, underscore (_), hyphen (-), equals sign (=), English comma (,), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。)
- Maximum length: 255 characters

DryRun.description_cn:
Whether to perform a dry run for this request. Valid values:
- true: Sends a validation request without creating an Instance. The validation checks required parameters, request format, business limits, and ECS inventory. If the check fails, the corresponding error is returned. If the check passes, the error code DryRunOperation is returned.
    When `DryRun` is set to `true`, if you specify the `Count` or `Mincount` parameter, the value must be 1.
  
- false (default): Sends a normal request. If the check passes, the Instance is created directly.
DryRun.description_en:
Whether to perform a dry run for this request. Valid values:
- true: Sends a validation request without creating an Instance. The validation checks required parameters, request format, business limits, and ECS inventory. If the check fails, the corresponding error is returned. If the check passes, the error code DryRunOperation is returned.
    When `DryRun` is set to `true`, if you specify the `Count` or `Mincount` parameter, the value must be 1.
  
- false (default): Sends a normal request. If the check passes, the Instance is created directly.

EipAddress.BandwidthMbps.description_en:
Maximum bandwidth for public IP. Default value: 1. Unit: Mbps
- When `ChargeType` is set to `PayByBandwidth`: range is 1–500
- When `ChargeType` is set to `PayByTraffic`: range is 1–200

EipAddress.BandwidthPackageId.description_en:
The ID of the shared bandwidth package, required when adding a public IP to a shared bandwidth package
- You can call the [DescribeBandwidthPackages](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/bandwidthpackage/DescribeBandwidthPackages) API to query the shared bandwidth package ID
- To add a public IP to a shared bandwidth package, the following conditions must be met:
  - Both must have the same security protection type
  - Both must be in the same region
  - The public IP must use pay-as-you-go billing
  - The shared bandwidth package must be of IPv4 type

EipAddress.ChargeType.description_en:
Billing methods for public IP addresses:
- PayByBandwidth (default): Pay-as-you-go—billed by bandwidth cap
- PayByTraffic: Pay-as-you-go—billed by actual data transfer
- PrePaid: Subscription (monthly or yearly)
When the instance billing type (`InstanceChargeType`) is set to `PostPaid`, this parameter cannot be set to `PrePaid`.

EipAddress.ISP.description_en:
Public IP line type. Default is BGP. Available values:
- BGP: BGP (multi-line)
- If your account has applied for and enabled static single line, you can use:
  - ChinaMobile: China Mobile static single line
  - ChinaTelecom: China Telecom static single line
  - ChinaUnicom: China Unicom static single line
- If your account has applied for and enabled BGP single line, you can use SingleLine_BGP
- If your account has applied for and enabled static BGP, you can use Static_BGP

EipAddress.ReleaseWithInstance.description_en:
Whether the public IP is released with the Instance. Only applies to pay-as-you-go public IPs. Options:
- true: The public IP is released with the Instance. When the Instance is automatically recycled (such as 24 hours after unsubscription or upon expiration) or deleted using the [DeleteInstance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DeleteInstance) or [DeleteInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DeleteInstances) APIs, the public IP is released together with the Instance
- false (default): The public IP is not released with the Instance

EipAddress.SecurityProtectionInstanceId.description_en:
DDoS Native Protection (Enterprise Edition) ID
- You can call the [DescInstanceList](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6352/1263659) API to query the DDoS Native Protection (Enterprise Edition) ID
- When `SecurityProtectionTypes` is set to `AntiDDoS_Enhanced`, this parameter is required

EipAddress.SecurityProtectionTypes.N.description_en:
Security protection types for public IP addresses
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the security protection type. Currently, only 1 is supported
- Values:
   - AntiDDoS_Enhanced: Apply for a public IP address with enhanced protection, which can be added to a DDoS Native Protection (Enterprise Edition) Instance
          - If `EipAddress.SecurityProtectionTypes.N` is set to `AntiDDoS_Enhanced`, `EipAddress.ChargeType` cannot be `PrePaid`, and `EipAddress.ISP` must be set to `BGP`
     - Enhanced protection public IP addresses are currently available by invitation only. To request access, please contact your account manager
     
   - Leave blank to request a public IP address with default protection

EnablePrimaryInterfaceHighBandwidthType.description_cn:
Does the primary network interface card support high bandwidth types? Values:
- true: Supported
- false (default): Not supported
EnablePrimaryInterfaceHighBandwidthType.description_en:
Does the primary network interface card support high bandwidth types? Values:
- true: Supported
- false (default): Not supported

Hostname.description_cn:
The instance hostname is the computer name used within the instance's operating system.
- Linux instance:
  - Letters, numbers, periods ("."), and hyphens ("-") are allowed
  - Cannot start or end with a hyphen or period
  - Cannot use hyphens or periods consecutively, or use a hyphen and period together
  - Length must be between 2 and 63 characters

- Windows instance:
  - Letters, numbers, and hyphens ("-") are allowed; cannot be all numbers
  - Cannot start or end with a hyphen, and cannot use hyphens consecutively
  - Length must be between 2 and 15 characters

- If left blank, the hostname is automatically generated using the rule iv- + initial hostname, for example: iv-3tigy72q3u3vj0******
- Initial hostname generation logic:
  - Linux: Extract all characters after 'i-' in the instance ID
  - Windows: Extract the last 12 characters after 'i-' in the instance ID

- When creating instances in batches, you can customize sequential hostnames using the format `name_prefix[begin_number,bits]name_suffix`. For details, see [Batch set sequential instance names or hostnames](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Batch-configuring-sequential-instance-names-or-hostnames)

HpcClusterId.description_cn:
High-performance computing cluster ID of the instance
This parameter is required and only applies when creating a high-performance computing GPU instance
HpcClusterId.description_en:
High-performance computing cluster ID of the instance
This parameter is required and only applies when creating a high-performance computing GPU instance

HttpTokens.description_cn:
Access mode for instance metadata. Specify whether to enforce hardened mode. Values:
- optional (default): Not enforced (compatibility mode). You can access instance metadata either directly or using the hardened method with token-based authentication.
- required: Enforced (hardened mode only). Only access via the hardened method with token-based authentication is supported.
- For details on how to view metadata and which metadata items are supported, see [View Instance Metadata](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Viewing-instance-metadata)
- The "hardened mode only" option is currently in invite-only testing. To request access, contact your account manager

Image ID used to launch the instance
You can call the [DescribeImages](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeImages) API and enter the desired instance type ID in the `InstanceTypeId` parameter to query supported images and their IDs for that instance type

ImageReleaseVersion.description_cn:
Specific image version number
- This parameter only applies when selecting a public image
- If left blank, the latest version of the image will be used
ImageReleaseVersion.description_en:

InstanceChargeType.description_cn:
Billing types for instances and cloud disks:
- PostPaid: Pay-as-you-go
- PrePaid: Subscription (yearly or monthly)
Make sure your account supports balance payment or credit payment. Otherwise, you will receive an InvalidInstanceChargeType error message.

InstanceName.description_cn:
Instance Name
- Must start with a letter or Chinese character
- Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), hyphens (-), and periods (.)
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
- If the instance uses an ordered suffix with `SuffixIndex`, the instance name length includes the ordered suffix
- When creating instances in bulk, you can use the format `name_prefix[begin_number,bits]name_suffix` to customize ordered instance names. For details, see [Set Ordered Instance or Host Names in Bulk](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Batch-configuring-sequential-instance-names-or-hostnames)
InstanceName.description_en:
Instance Name
- Must start with a letter or Chinese character
- Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), hyphens (-), and periods (.)
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
- If the instance uses an ordered suffix with `SuffixIndex`, the instance name length includes the ordered suffix
- When creating instances in bulk, you can use the format `name_prefix[begin_number,bits]name_suffix` to customize ordered instance names. For details, see [Set Ordered Instance or Host Names in Bulk](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Batch-configuring-sequential-instance-names-or-hostnames)

InstanceTypeId.description_cn:
Instance Specifications
- Product selection: You can refer to the [Instance Specifications Overview](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Introduction-to-instance-types) or call [DescribeInstanceTypes](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeInstanceTypes) to view performance data for each instance specification. For guidance on how to choose an instance specification, see [Best Practices for Instance Selection](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Instance-type-selection-best-practice).
- Check inventory: You can call [DescribeAvailableResource](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeAvailableResource) to view the available compute resource inventory in each availability zone.

Instance Specifications
- Product selection: You can refer to the [Instance Specifications Overview](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Introduction-to-instance-types) or call [DescribeInstanceTypes](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeInstanceTypes) to view performance data for each instance specification. For guidance on how to choose an instance specification, see [Best Practices for Instance Selection](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Instance-type-selection-best-practice).
- Check inventory: You can call [DescribeAvailableResource](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeAvailableResource) to view the available compute resource inventory in each availability zone.

KeepImageCredential.description_cn:
Retain image settings. Options:
- true: Retain image settings. The instance will use the preset password or key pair from the image for login.
- false (default): Do not retain image settings.
- Only custom images and shared images support this feature.
- When this parameter is set to `true`, do not specify `PassWord` or `KeyPairName`.
KeepImageCredential.description_en:
Retain image settings. Options:
- true: Retain image settings. The instance will use the preset password or key pair from the image for login.
- false (default): Do not retain image settings.
- Only custom images and shared images support this feature.
- When this parameter is set to `true`, do not specify `PassWord` or `KeyPairName`.

KeyPairName.description_cn:
To log in to an Instance using SSH key authentication, specify the name of an existing key pair.
You can call [DescribeKeyPairs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeKeyPairs) to view existing key pairs. If none are available, call [CreateKeyPair](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/CreateKeyPair) to create a key pair.
- Windows Instances do not support SSH key authentication. Even if you provide this parameter, only the password (`Password`) will be used.
- Linux Instances support login with either a password or a key pair. If you set both `KeyPairName` and `Password` when calling this API, only the key pair (`KeyPairName`) will be used.
KeyPairName.description_en:
To log in to an Instance using SSH key authentication, specify the name of an existing key pair.
You can call [DescribeKeyPairs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeKeyPairs) to view existing key pairs. If none are available, call [CreateKeyPair](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/CreateKeyPair) to create a key pair.
- Windows Instances do not support SSH key authentication. Even if you provide this parameter, only the password (`Password`) will be used.
- Linux Instances support login with either a password or a key pair. If you set both `KeyPairName` and `Password` when calling this API, only the key pair (`KeyPairName`) will be used.

MinCount.description_cn:
Set the minimum number of ECS instances to create (range: 1–100)
- The minimum instance creation count (MinCount) must be less than or equal to the creation count (Count)
- If available stock > creation count (Count), create Count instances
- If minimum creation count (MinCount) ≤ available stock ≤ creation count (Count), create the number of instances equal to the available stock
- If available stock < minimum creation count (MinCount), creation fails due to insufficient stock
MinCount.description_en:
Set the minimum number of ECS instances to create (range: 1–100)
- The minimum instance creation count (MinCount) must be less than or equal to the creation count (Count)
- If available stock > creation count (Count), create Count instances
- If minimum creation count (MinCount) ≤ available stock ≤ creation count (Count), create the number of instances equal to the available stock
- If available stock < minimum creation count (MinCount), creation fails due to insufficient stock

NetworkInterfaces.N.Ipv6AddressCount.description_en:
Number of private IPv6 addresses assigned to the primary network interface card. Only 1 is supported
- When you specify this parameter, the system automatically assigns the same number of available private IPv6 addresses from the subnet to the network interface card, and uses them as its private IPv6 addresses
- You can only assign IPv6 addresses to the primary network interface card when creating an instance. To assign IPv6 addresses to an auxiliary network interface card, see [CreateNetworkInterface](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/CreateNetworkInterface)
- Parameter - N: Indicates the index of the network interface card. N = 1 refers to the primary network interface card; N ≥ 2 refers to an auxiliary network interface card. If you specify N ≥ 2, this parameter will be ignored
Assigning IPv6 addresses to network interface cards is currently in invite-only testing. Only accounts that have completed [enterprise verification](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6261/64937) can apply for a trial. To request access, contact your account manager

NetworkInterfaces.N.PrimaryIpAddress.description_en:
Specify the primary IP address for a network interface. Currently, you can specify only one primary IP address, either for the primary network interface or for a secondary network interface.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the interface number. N = 1 refers to the primary network interface; N ≥ 2 refers to secondary network interfaces.
- Use & to separate multiple interfaces

NetworkInterfaces.N.PrivateIpAddresses.N.description_en:
Specify the secondary IP addresses for the primary network interface card. Currently, only the primary NIC supports assigning secondary IPs.
- The first N indicates the index of the primary NIC. Only one primary NIC can be bound at this time.
- The second N indicates the index of the secondary IP on the primary NIC. The maximum number of secondary IP addresses you can assign is the number of private IPs supported by the [Instance specification](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Introduction-to-instance-types) for a single NIC, minus one primary private IP.
- Separate multiple secondary IPs with &.

NetworkInterfaces.N.SecurityGroupIds.N.description_en:
Security group ID associated with the network interface card.
- The first N indicates the NIC sequence number. N = 1 means the primary NIC; N ≥ 2 means secondary NICs.
- The second N indicates the sequence number of the security group associated with the NIC. Valid values: 1–5.
- Use & to separate multiple security group IDs.

NetworkInterfaces.N.SubnetId.description_en:
Private network subnet ID for the Instance. When creating an Instance, you can also bind secondary network interfaces.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the network interface index. N = 1 indicates the primary network interface; N ≥ 2 indicates secondary network interfaces.
- Separate multiple private network subnet IDs with &.

NetworkOptions.EnableJumboFrame.description_en:
Whether the Instance enables jumbo frames. Values:
- false: Jumbo frames are disabled. All network interfaces of this Instance have an MTU value of 1500.
- true: Jumbo frames are enabled. All network interfaces of this Instance have an MTU value of 8500.
This feature is only supported for certain Instances. For Instances that support jumbo frames, see [Enable/Disable Jumbo Frames](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Enabling_or_Disabling_jumbo_frames).

Password.description_cn:
To log in to the Instance using the password method, specify the initial login password for the administrator account with this parameter. The Linux administrator account is root, and the Windows administrator account is Administrator.
Password complexity requirements:
- Length must be between 8 and 30 characters
- Passwords can only contain uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, and must include at least three of these types
- Allowed special characters: `~!@#$%^&*()_-+=|{}[]:;'<>,.?/
- Passwords cannot start with "/" or "$6$"
Login credentials support three methods: password, key pair, and reserved image settings. When logging in to the Instance using a password, we recommend increasing password complexity to enhance security.
Password.description_en:
To log in to the Instance using the password method, specify the initial login password for the administrator account with this parameter. The Linux administrator account is root, and the Windows administrator account is Administrator.
Password complexity requirements:
- Length must be between 8 and 30 characters
- Passwords can only contain uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, and must include at least three of these types
- Allowed special characters: `~!@#$%^&*()_-+=|{}[]:;'<>,.?/
- Passwords cannot start with "/" or "$6$"
Login credentials support three methods: password, key pair, and reserved image settings. When logging in to the Instance using a password, we recommend increasing password complexity to enhance security.

Period.description_cn:
Resource purchase duration (months)
- Allowed values: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60
- Default value: 1
This parameter is required and only takes effect when `InstanceChargeType` is set to `PrePaid`.
Period.description_en:
Resource purchase duration (months)
- Allowed values: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60
- Default value: 1
This parameter is required and only takes effect when `InstanceChargeType` is set to `PrePaid`.

PeriodUnit.description_cn:
Duration unit for purchasing resources. Value: Month (default).
This parameter is valid and required only when `InstanceChargeType` is set to `PrePaid`.
PeriodUnit.description_en:
Duration unit for purchasing resources. Value: Month (default).
This parameter is valid and required only when `InstanceChargeType` is set to `PrePaid`.

Placement.Affinity.description_en:
For ECS instances in stopped with savings mode, some resources are released after the instance stops. This parameter lets you choose whether to redeploy the instance on the original dedicated host when restarting. Options:

- Host: When you restart an instance in stopped with savings mode, it is redeployed on the original dedicated host
- Default (default): When you restart an instance in stopped with savings mode, the instance is first migrated to a dedicated host that supports auto-deployment if resources are available; if not, it starts on the original dedicated host

Placement.DedicatedHostClusterId.description_en:
Dedicated host cluster ID where the instance resides
You can call the [DescribeDedicatedHostClusters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6396/1253698) API to query the host cluster ID

Placement.DedicatedHostId.description_en:
Dedicated host ID where the instance resides
Call the [DescribeDedicatedHosts](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6396/1253691) API to query the list of dedicated hosts

Placement.Tenancy.description_en:
Whether to create an instance on a dedicated host. Options:
- Default: Create a standard cloud server instance
- Host: Create an instance on a dedicated host. If you do not specify `Placement.DedicatedHostId`, the system will automatically select a dedicated host for the instance
For supported instance types on dedicated hosts, see [Instance Types](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6396/1253643)

PrimaryNetworkInterfacePciBus.description_en:
Specify primary NIC PCI bus (default: empty)
Value range: 0

ProjectName.description_cn: Project to which the resource belongs. Each resource can belong to only one project. Use only letters, numbers, underscores (_), periods (.), and hyphens (-). Maximum length: 64 characters.
ProjectName.description_en: Project to which the resource belongs. Each resource can belong to only one project. Use only letters, numbers, underscores (_), periods (.), and hyphens (-). Maximum length: 64 characters.

SecurityEnhancementStrategy.description_cn:
Whether to enable security hardening. Values:
- Active: Enable security hardening; applies to public images only
- Inactive: Disable security hardening; applies to all image types
SecurityEnhancementStrategy.description_en:
Whether to enable security hardening. Values:
- Active: Enable security hardening; applies to public images only
- Inactive: Disable security hardening; applies to all image types

SpotPriceLimit.description_cn:
Maximum hourly price for spot instances, supports up to three decimal places
This parameter takes effect only when `SpotStrategy` is set to `SpotWithPriceLimit`
SpotPriceLimit.description_en:
Maximum hourly price for spot instances, supports up to three decimal places
This parameter takes effect only when `SpotStrategy` is set to `SpotWithPriceLimit`

SpotStrategy.description_cn:
Preemptible strategy for pay-as-you-go Instances. Valid values:
- NoSpot (default): Creates a standard pay-as-you-go Instance
- SpotAsPriceGo: System sets the bid automatically based on the current market price for a preemptible Instance
- SpotWithPriceLimit: Preemptible Instance with a custom bid price limit
- This parameter takes effect only when `InstanceChargeType` is set to `PostPaid`
- For details on preemptible Instance bidding modes, see [Purchase Preemptible Instances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Buying_spot_instance)
SpotStrategy.description_en:
Preemptible strategy for pay-as-you-go Instances. Valid values:
- NoSpot (default): Creates a standard pay-as-you-go Instance
- SpotAsPriceGo: System sets the bid automatically based on the current market price for a preemptible Instance
- SpotWithPriceLimit: Preemptible Instance with a custom bid price limit
- This parameter takes effect only when `InstanceChargeType` is set to `PostPaid`
- For details on preemptible Instance bidding modes, see [Purchase Preemptible Instances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Buying_spot_instance)

SuffixIndex.description_cn: Starting number for ordered suffix. Range: 1–999, default: 1
SuffixIndex.description_en: Starting number for ordered suffix. Range: 1–999, default: 1

Tags.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key for user tags
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag key, range: 1–20
- Separate multiple tag keys with &

Naming rules:
  - Cannot start with any case combination of `volc:` or `sys:`
  - Only letters, numbers, spaces, and the following symbols are allowed: "_", ".", ":", "/", "=", "+", "-", "@"
  - Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
Tag keys for the same resource must be unique

Tags.N.Value.description_en:
Tag value for user tags
- Parameter - N: Indicates the index of the tag value, range: 1–20
- Separate multiple tag values with &

Naming rules:
  - Only letters, numbers, spaces, and the following symbols are allowed: "_", ".", ":", "/", "=", "+", "-", "@"
  - Can be empty; length must be between 0 and 256 characters
If you pass this parameter, you must first pass `Tags.N.Key`

UniqueSuffix.description_cn:
Indicates whether to automatically add a sequential suffix to `Hostname` and `InstanceName` when creating multiple Instances. Values:
- true: Enable sequential suffix
- false (default): Disable sequential suffix
- When sequential suffix is enabled and `Hostname` is empty, the system will automatically generate a hostname without a sequential suffix.
- When sequential suffix is enabled and you specify the `[begin_number,bits]` naming format for `Hostname` or `InstanceName`, see [Batch set sequential instance names or hostnames](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Batch-configuring-sequential-instance-names-or-hostnames) for details on the final result.
UniqueSuffix.description_en:
Indicates whether to automatically add a sequential suffix to `Hostname` and `InstanceName` when creating multiple Instances. Values:
- true: Enable sequential suffix
- false (default): Disable sequential suffix
- When sequential suffix is enabled and `Hostname` is empty, the system will automatically generate a hostname without a sequential suffix.
- When sequential suffix is enabled and you specify the `[begin_number,bits]` naming format for `Hostname` or `InstanceName`, see [Batch set sequential instance names or hostnames](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Batch-configuring-sequential-instance-names-or-hostnames) for details on the final result.

Volumes.N.BurstEnabled.description_en:
Enable Burst (performance burst) feature for cloud disk?
- true: Enabled
- false (default): Not enabled

Volumes.N.DeleteWithInstance.description_en:
Whether the cloud disk is released with the instance. Options:
- true (default): The cloud disk is released with the instance
- false: The cloud disk is not released with the instance
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk number, valid range: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk, which is always released with the instance and cannot be retained. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks, which can be set to release with the instance or not
- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceIOPS.description_en:
Extra IOPS performance size for cloud disks. Only ESSD FlexPL data disks support this feature. Unit: operations/second

Set this parameter when `ExtraPerformanceTypeId` is set to `Balance` or `IOPS`. The valid value ranges for each type are:
- IOPS type: 1–50000
- Balance type: 1–50000

- Parameter N: Indicates the disk sequence number. Valid values: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; when N is 1, this parameter is ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can set this parameter for these disks.
- Use & to separate multiple disks.

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceThroughputMB.description_en:
Extra disk throughput (MB/s). Supported only for ESSD FlexPL data disks.

Set this parameter when `ExtraPerformanceTypeId` is set to `Throughput`.
Value range: 1–650.

- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk sequence number. Valid values: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; if N is 1, this parameter is ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can set this parameter for data disks.
- Use & to separate multiple disks.

Volumes.N.ExtraPerformanceTypeId.description_en:
Types of additional disk performance, supported only by ESSD FlexPL data disks. Options:
- Balance: Balanced performance
- IOPS: IOPS performance
- Throughput: Throughput performance

For more information about additional performance, see [Additional Disk Performance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/essd_flexpl_volume).

- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk index, with a valid range of 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; when N is set to 1, this parameter is ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can set this parameter normally.
- Use & to separate multiple disks.

Volumes.N.Size.description_en:
Cloud disk capacity, in GiB. N ranges from 1 to 16. N = 1 indicates a system disk; N ≥ 2 indicates a data disk. Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.

Cloud disk capacity ranges:
- System disk:
  - ESSD_PL0: 20–2048
  - ESSD_FlexPL: 20–2048
    Default value: max{40, the image size of the specified ImageId}.
  

- Data disk:
  - ESSD_PL0: 10–32768
  - ESSD_FlexPL: 10–32768
    If this parameter is not specified, the capacity of the data disk is set to the size of the snapshot specified by `Volumes.N.SnapshotId`. If `Volumes.N.SnapshotId` is not provided, an error LimitExceeded.DataVolumeSize is returned.

Volumes.N.SnapshotId.description_en:
Create a cloud disk from a snapshot. Only data disks are supported. You can use the [DescribeSnapshots](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Describesnapshots) API to query snapshot IDs.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the cloud disk index, valid values: 1–16. N = 1 refers to the system disk; if you set N to 1, this parameter will be ignored. N ≥ 2 refers to data disks; you can specify the target data disk snapshot ID.
- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.
- Only Ultra SSDs support creating cloud disks from snapshots. Performance SSDs do not support snapshot-related features.
- Only snapshots with the 'Available' status can be used to create new cloud disks. Snapshots in 'Creating', 'Rolling Back', 'Deleting', or 'Error' status cannot be used to create new cloud disks.

Volumes.N.VolumeType.description_en:
Cloud disk type options:
- ESSD_PL0 (default): Ultra-fast SSD PL0
- ESSD_FlexPL: Ultra-fast SSD FlexPL
- Parameter N: Indicates the cloud disk number. Valid range: 1–16. N = 1 is the system disk. N ≥ 2 are data disks
- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks

ForceStop.description_cn:
Whether to force shutdown. Valid values:
- true: Force shutdown. This is equivalent to a typical power-off operation; all cached data not written to storage devices will be lost.
- false (default): Normal shutdown.
For the following types of Instances, `ForceStop` will always perform a forced shutdown, regardless of whether it is set to `true` or `false`.
- Elastic Bare Metal Instances
- High Performance Computing GPU types: ebmhpcpni2l, ebmhpcpni2, ebmhpchfpni2 Instances
  > ebmhpcpni2l, ebmhpcpni2, and ebmhpchfpni2 are currently in invitation testing. If you want to try them, please contact your account manager to apply.

StoppedMode.description_cn:
Shutdown mode. Valid values:
- KeepCharging: Standard shutdown mode. After shutdown, the instance and its associated resources are retained and continue to be billed at the same rate as before shutdown.
- StopCharging: Saving shutdown mode. After shutdown, the instance's compute resources (vCPU, GPU, and memory) are released and billing for them stops. Attached cloud disks, images, and public IPs are retained and continue to be billed.
  For activation requirements of saving shutdown mode, see [Description of Pay-As-You-Go Saving Shutdown Mode](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Economical-mode-for-pay-as-you-go-instances).

Default value: If you have [enabled the default saving shutdown mode](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Economical_mode_for_pay-as-you-go_instances-1#%E5%BC%80%E5%90%AF%E9%BB%98%E8%AE%A4%E8%8A%82%E7%9C%81%E5%81%9C%E6%9C%BA%E6%A8%A1%E5%BC%8F) in the cloud server console and meet the activation requirements, the default value is `StopCharging`. Otherwise, the default value is `KeepCharging`.

- true: Force shutdown. This is similar to a power-off operation; any cached data not written to storage devices will be lost.
- false (default): Normal shutdown.

- Elastic bare metal Instances
- High-performance computing GPU types: ebmhpcpni2l, ebmhpcpni2, ebmhpchfpni2 Instances. These Instances are currently in invite-only testing. To request a trial, please contact your account manager.

MinCount.description_cn:
Specify the minimum number of ECS instances to create; valid range: 1–100.
- The minimum number of instances to create (`MinCount`) must be less than or equal to the creation quantity (`Count`).
- If the inventory quantity is greater than the creation quantity (`Count`), create `Count` instances.
- If the minimum creation quantity (`MinCount`) is less than or equal to the inventory quantity and the inventory quantity is less than or equal to the creation quantity (`Count`), create instances equal to the inventory quantity.
- If the inventory quantity is less than the minimum creation quantity (`MinCount`), creation fails due to insufficient inventory.

- If the inventory quantity is less than the minimum creation quantity (`MinCount`), creation fails due to insufficient inventory.

NetworkInterfaces.N.PrimaryIpAddress.description_en:

- Parameter - N: Indicates the serial number of the network interface card. N = 1 indicates the primary network interface card; N ≥ 2 indicates a secondary network interface card.
- Use & to separate multiple network interface cards.

NetworkInterfaces.N.SecurityGroupIds.N.description_en:
Security group ID associated with the network interface card.
- The first N: indicates the index of the network interface card, where N = 1 means the primary network interface card; N ≥ 2 means a secondary network interface card.
- The second N: indicates the index of the security group associated with the network interface card, with values ranging from 1 to 5.
- Separate multiple security group IDs with &.

NetworkInterfaces.N.SubnetId.description_en:

- Parameter - N: Indicates the network interface sequence number. N = 1 refers to the primary network interface; N ≥ 2 refers to auxiliary network interfaces.
- Separate multiple private network subnet IDs with &.

Volumes.N.Size.description_en:
Cloud disk capacity, measured in GiB. N ranges from 1 to 16; N = 1 indicates a system disk, N ≥ 2 indicates a data disk. Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.

Cloud disk capacity ranges:
- System disk:
  - ESSD_PL0: 20–2048
  - ESSD_FlexPL: 20–2048
    Default value: max{40, the capacity of the image corresponding to ImageId}.
  

- Data disk:
  - ESSD_PL0: 10–32768
  - ESSD_FlexPL: 10–32768
    If this parameter is not specified, the data disk capacity will be set to the snapshot size corresponding to `Volumes.N.SnapshotId`. If `Volumes.N.SnapshotId` is not provided, an error LimitExceeded.DataVolumeSize will be returned.

- Use & to separate multiple cloud disks.

ForceStop.description_cn:
Whether to force shutdown. Values:
- true: Force shutdown. This is equivalent to a typical power-off operation; any cached data not written to storage devices will be lost.
- false (default): Normal shutdown.
For the following types of Instances, the `ForceStop` parameter will result in a forced shutdown regardless of whether it is set to true or false.
- Elastic Bare Metal Instances.
- High-performance computing GPU types: ebmhpcpni2l, ebmhpcpni2, ebmhpchfpni2 Instances.
  > ebmhpcpni2l, ebmhpcpni2, and ebmhpchfpni2 are currently in invitation testing. To request a trial, please [submit a ticket](https://console.volcengine.com/workorder/create/) or contact your account manager.

InstanceIds.description_en:
Instance IDs to be tagged

- You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/HBase/DescribeDBInstances) API to query basic information for all HBase instances in the target region, including instance IDs
- You can enter multiple instance IDs at once, separated by commas (,). You can specify up to 20 instance IDs per request, and each instance can have up to 50 tags

Tags.description_en:
An array object containing the tag keys and tag values to be bound
- You can enter multiple sets of tag key-value pairs at once, separated by commas (,)
- You can enter up to 20 sets of tag key-value pairs at a time; each instance can bind up to 50 tags
- Tag keys and values must follow the configuration rules. For details, see [Tag configuration rules](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/HBase/Tag_overview#%E6%A0%87%E7%AD%BE%E8%AE%BE%E7%BD%AE%E8%A7%84%E5%88%99)

AllowListIds.description_en:
The allowlist ID that needs to be bound to the instance.

- You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/HBase/DescribeAllowLists) API to query all allowlist information in a specified region, including allowlist IDs.
- You can enter multiple allowlist IDs at once, separated by commas (,).
- You cannot specify multiple instance IDs and multiple allowlist IDs at the same time. You can only bind multiple instances to the same allowlist at once, or bind a single instance to multiple allowlists at once.

InstanceIds.description_en:
Instance IDs that need to be bound to the whitelist.

- You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/HBase/DescribeDBInstances) API to query basic information for all HBase instances in the target region, including instance IDs.
- You can enter multiple instance IDs at once, separated by English commas (,).
- You cannot enter multiple instance IDs and multiple whitelists in a single operation. You can only bind multiple instances to the same whitelist in one operation, or bind one instance to multiple whitelists in one operation.

AllowList.description_en:
Enter an IP address or a CIDR-formatted IP range.

- Each whitelist can contain up to 300 IP addresses or IP ranges. Duplicate addresses are not allowed. Separate multiple addresses with commas (,).
- Setting `127.0.0.1` blocks access from all addresses.
- Setting CIDR `192.168.1.0/24` allows access from IP addresses within that range.
- Setting `192.168.1.1` allows access only from that IP address.
- Do not set `0.0.0.0/0`.

AllowListDesc.description_en: Whitelist remark cannot exceed 200 characters

AllowListName.description_en:
Whitelist name requirements:

- Do not start with a number or hyphen (-)
- Only Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-) are allowed
- Length must be 1 to 32 characters
- Name must not duplicate an existing whitelist name

Parameters.description_cn:
Initial parameter configuration for Kafka instances

Refer to the table below for the list of supported parameters and their default values. For detailed information on each parameter, see the documentation at [Modify Parameter Configuration](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/modifying-instance-parameter).

When calling the API using Postman or similar tools, make sure to escape parameters properly. For example: {"LogRetentionHours":"72","MessageMaxByte":"10","MessageTimestampType":"CreateTime","OffsetRetentionMinutes":"4320"}

Parameter descriptions

- "MessageMaxByte":"10": Maximum message size in MB. Valid range: 1–12. Default: 10
- "LogRetentionHours":"72": Message retention period in hours. Valid range: 0–2160 (up to 90 days). Default: 72
- "OffsetRetentionMinutes":"4320": Offset retention period in minutes. Valid range: 1–10080 (up to 7 days). Default: 4320
- "MessageTimestampType":"LogAppendTime": Message timestamp type. Can be set to LogAppendTime or CreateTime. LogAppendTime indicates the time the message is written to the server; CreateTime indicates the time the producer creates the message

When calling the API using Postman or similar tools, make sure to escape parameters properly. For example: {"LogRetentionHours":"72","MessageMaxByte":"10","MessageTimestampType":"CreateTime","OffsetRetentionMinutes":"4320"}

Parameter descriptions

- "MessageMaxByte":"10": Maximum message size in MB. Valid range: 1–12. Default: 10

- "OffsetRetentionMinutes":"4320": Offset retention period in minutes. Valid range: 1–10080 (up to 7 days). Default: 4320
- "MessageTimestampType":"LogAppendTime": Message timestamp type. Can be set to LogAppendTime or CreateTime. LogAppendTime indicates the time the message is written to the server; CreateTime indicates the time the producer creates the message

Parameters.description_cn:
New Kafka instance parameter configuration

For the list of supported parameters and their default values, see the table below: Parameters Description. You can also view detailed information for each parameter in the documentation [Modify Parameter Configuration](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/modifying-instance-parameter).

When calling the API using Postman or similar tools, make sure to escape parameters, for example: `{"LogRetentionHours":"72","MessageMaxByte":"10","MessageTimestampType":"CreateTime","OffsetRetentionMinutes":"4320"}`.

Parameters Description

- "MessageMaxByte":"10": Maximum message size in MB. Valid values: 1–12. Default is 10
- "LogRetentionHours":"72": Message retention period in hours. Valid values: 0–2160 (up to 90 days). Default is 72
- "OffsetRetentionMinutes":"4320": Offset retention period in minutes. Valid values: 1–10080 (up to 7 days). Default is 4320
- "MessageTimestampType":"LogAppendTime": Message timestamp type. Supports 'LogAppendTime' and 'CreateTime'. LogAppendTime is the time the message is written to the server; CreateTime is the time the Producer creates the message
- "AutoDeleteGroup":"false": Whether to automatically delete the group. Default is false. If set to true, when all consumers in the group are in Empty status and the offset retention period is exceeded, the backend service will automatically delete the consumer group. If set to false, automatic deletion of consumption progress does not affect the group status; groups in Empty status will not be automatically deleted

- "AutoDeleteGroup":"false": Whether to automatically delete the group. Default is false. If set to true, when all consumers in the group are in Empty status and the offset retention period is exceeded, the backend service will automatically delete the consumer group. If set to false, automatic deletion of consumption progress does not affect the group status; groups in Empty status will not be automatically deleted

RebalanceTime.description_cn:
Execution time for automatic rebalancing. Use the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, for example, 2023-01-02 15:04:05. The time must be at least 5 minutes later than the current time.
- This parameter takes effect only when NeedRebalance is set to true. If you do not set this parameter, the rebalancing task runs immediately after configuration is complete.
- We recommend scheduling rebalancing during off-peak hours, such as at night, to minimize the impact of data migration on your business.
- If you do not specify this parameter, rebalancing runs immediately after the upgrade.

CleanupPolicy.description_cn:
Topic message cleanup policies support the following three options:

- ["delete"]: The default message cleanup policy. When disk space is sufficient, messages are retained within the maximum retention period. If disk space is low, older messages are deleted early to ensure service availability.

Note

The default disk cleanup threshold for Kafka instances is 90%. Actual values may vary. For details, see Setting Disk Cleanup Threshold.


- ["compact"]: The COMPACT cleanup policy consolidates messages by key. For messages with the same key, only the latest value is kept; older records are removed.
- ["delete","compact"]: Enables both DELETE and COMPACT cleanup policies. Messages are deleted if they meet the criteria of either policy.

The COMPACT cleanup policy cannot be enabled for messages without a key.

- ["compact"]: The COMPACT cleanup policy consolidates messages by key. For messages with the same key, only the latest value is kept; older records are removed.
- ["delete","compact"]: Enables both DELETE and COMPACT cleanup policies. Messages are deleted if they meet the criteria of either policy.

The COMPACT cleanup policy cannot be enabled for messages without a key.

Parameters.description_cn:
Kafka topic-level parameter configuration

For the list of supported parameters and their default values, see the table below: Topic Parameters. For detailed information on each parameter, refer to the documentation [Modify Parameter Configuration](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/kafka/modifying-instance-parameter).

When calling the API using Postman or similar tools, make sure to escape characters as shown: {\"LogRetentionHours\":\"72\",\"MessageMaxByte\":\"10\",\"MinInsyncReplicaNumber\":\"2\"}.

Parameter descriptions

- "MinInsyncReplicaNumber":"2": Minimum number of in-sync replicas. If the number of in-sync replicas falls below this value, messages cannot be written to the topic. Increasing this value improves data reliability but reduces availability. The default is the number of replicas minus one. For better topic availability, set this to the number of replicas minus one.
- "MessageMaxByte":"10": Maximum message size in MB. Valid range: 1–12. By default, this follows the instance's maximum message size setting.
- "LogRetentionHours":"72": Message retention period in hours. Valid range: 0–2160 (up to 90 days). By default, this follows the instance's message retention period setting.

PartitionNumber.description_cn: Number of partitions for this topic. The greater the number of partitions, the higher the consumption concurrency. You can only increase this value; you cannot decrease it. Do not exceed the remaining available partition count in the Kafka instance.
PartitionNumber.description_en: Number of partitions for this topic. The greater the number of partitions, the higher the consumption concurrency. You can only increase this value; you cannot decrease it. Do not exceed the remaining available partition count in the Kafka instance.

ReplicaNumber.description_cn:
The number of replicas for a partition indicates how many copies of the data are backed up. If one broker fails, data remains available. A higher replica count increases reliability.
- Increasing the replica count uses more instance disk capacity; make sure you have enough capacity.
- Adding replicas consumes instance bandwidth resources; we recommend making changes during business off-peak hours.
- Reducing the replica count lowers data availability; proceed with caution.
- Topics with only 1 replica cannot ensure data reliability and are unavailable for read/write operations during instance upgrades; we recommend using 2 or 3 replicas.

ResetOffsetsInfo.ResetOffset.description_cn:
Reset the consumer offset to a specified Offset. Only set this parameter when ResetType is Offset. If not specified, the offset will be reset to the latest message position.
Value range:
- -1 (default): Reset the consumer offset to the latest message
- -2: Reset the consumer offset to the earliest message
- Other integer values: Reset the consumer offset to a specific Offset within the specified topic and partition. The value must be between the partition's minimum and maximum offsets, that is, [StartOffset, EndOffset]
- You can only specify other integer values for ResetOffset when both TopicName and PartitionId are set
- Use DescribeTopicPartitions to view StartOffset and EndOffset
ResetOffsetsInfo.ResetOffset.description_en:
Reset the consumer offset to a specified Offset. Only set this parameter when ResetType is Offset. If not specified, the offset will be reset to the latest message position.
Value range:
- -1 (default): Reset the consumer offset to the latest message
- -2: Reset the consumer offset to the earliest message
- Other integer values: Reset the consumer offset to a specific Offset within the specified topic and partition. The value must be between the partition's minimum and maximum offsets, that is, [StartOffset, EndOffset]
- You can only specify other integer values for ResetOffset when both TopicName and PartitionId are set
- Use DescribeTopicPartitions to view StartOffset and EndOffset

ResetOffsetsInfo.ResetTimestamp.description_cn:
Reset the consumption offset to the specified time point. The value should be a timestamp in milliseconds. Only required when ResetType is set to Timestamp. 
- The consumption timestamp is when the message was stored on the server. 
- The valid reset range is determined by the topic's instance message retention duration; you can set this parameter between [current time - instance message retention duration, current time]. 
- If no message exists at the specified time, the offset resets to the nearest message position.
ResetOffsetsInfo.ResetTimestamp.description_en:
Reset the consumption offset to the specified time point. The value should be a timestamp in milliseconds. Only required when ResetType is set to Timestamp. 
- The consumption timestamp is when the message was stored on the server. 
- The valid reset range is determined by the topic's instance message retention duration; you can set this parameter between [current time - instance message retention duration, current time]. 
- If no message exists at the specified time, the offset resets to the nearest message position.

ResetOffsetsInfo.ResetType.description_cn:
Consumer position reset method defaults to Offset. The options are:
- Offset (default): Reset consumer position based on the specified offset. The group starts consuming from the designated position in the current partition. By default, resets to the latest offset, or you can specify an offset using the ResetOffset parameter
- Timestamp: Reset consumer position based on a specified time. The group starts consuming from a selected time point within a past time range. Set the time point using the ResetTimestamp parameter

Message.description_cn:
Signed message, Base64 encoded

If MessageType is RAW: When original message data is provided, the hash algorithm specified in Algorithm generates a digest from the original message, then signs it. Valid message length: 1 to 4096 bytes

If MessageType is DIGEST:
- If Algorithm is RSA_PSS_SHA_256, RSA_PKCS1_SHA_256, ECDSA_SHA_256, or SM2_DSA, message length must be 32 bytes
- If Algorithm is RSA_PSS_SHA_384, RSA_PKCS1_SHA_384, or ECDSA_SHA_384, message length must be 48 bytes
- If Algorithm is RSA_PSS_SHA_512, RSA_PKCS1_SHA_512, or ECDSA_SHA_512, message length must be 64 bytes

SecretValue.description_cn:
Secret value, up to 30,720 bytes.

When SecretType is set to Generic, you can define the value as needed. We recommend using a JSON key-value pair format.

When SecretType is set to IAM, the SecretValue format is:
    {"AccessKeys":[{"AccessKeyId":"","AccessKeySecret":""}]}
    AccessKeyId: Access key ID
    AccessKeySecret: Access key secret
    The number of AccessKeys must be 1 or 2. AccessKeyId is required.

When SecretType is set to RDS, the SecretValue format is:
    {"Accounts":[{"AccountName":"","AccountPassword":""}]}
    AccountName: Account name for the RDS instance
    AccountPassword: Password for the RDS instance
    If SecretSubType is SingleUser, Accounts must contain 1 item. If SecretSubType is DoubleUsers, Accounts must contain 2 items. AccountName is required, and the two AccountNames must be different.

When SecretType is set to Redis, the SecretValue format is:
    {"Accounts":[{"AccountName":"","AccountPassword":""}]}
    AccountName: Account name for the Redis instance
    AccountPassword: Password for the Redis instance
    If SecretSubType is SingleUser, Accounts must contain 1 item. If SecretSubType is DoubleUsers, Accounts must contain 2 items. AccountName is required, and the two AccountNames must be different.

When SecretType is set to ECS, the SecretValue format is:
    If SecretSubType is Password: {"UserName":"","Password":""}
    UserName: Username for logging in to the ECS instance
    Password: Password for logging in to the ECS instance
    If SecretSubType is SSHKey: {"UserName":"","PublicKey":"","PrivateKey":""}
    PublicKey: SSH public key for logging in to the ECS instance
    PrivateKey: Private key for logging in to the ECS instance

Filters.description_cn:
Query keyrings that match specified criteria using key-value pairs.

Key
Description: The attribute to query
Type: String
Options:
    KeyringName: Keyring name
    KeyringType: Keyring type
    Description: Keyring description
    CreationDateRange: Keyring creation date range
    UpdateDateRange: Keyring update date range

Values
Description: Specific values for the attribute
Type: List of strings
Capacity: 1–10
Value details:
    When Key is KeyringName: Supports fuzzy search, case-insensitive. Example: ["hello", "world"]
    When Key is KeyringType: Options are CustomKeyring, ManagedKeyring, ServiceKeyring (case-sensitive). Example: ["CustomKeyring", "ManagedKeyring"]
    When Key is Description: Supports fuzzy search, case-insensitive. Example: ["hello", "world"]
    When Key is CreationDateRange: Enter both start and end times. Example: ["2024-08-13 10:00:00", "2024-08-14 10:00:00"]
    When Key is UpdateDateRange: Enter both start and end times. Example: ["2024-08-13 10:00:00", "2024-08-14 10:00:00"]

Filters: Multiple values under the same Key use OR logic; different Keys use AND logic.

For example, input [{"Key":"KeyringName", "Values":["hello","world"]},{"Key":"KeyringType", "Values":["CustomKeyring"]}] means: (KeyringName=hello OR KeyringName=world) AND (KeyringType=CustomKeyring)

        ProtectionLevel: Key protection level
        RotateState: Key rotation status
        Origin: Key origin
        CreationDateRange: Key creation time range
        UpdateDateRange: Key update time range

Values
    Description: Specific values for the attribute.
    Type: List of strings
    Capacity: 1–10
    Value instructions:
        When Key is KeyName: Supports fuzzy search, case-insensitive. Example: ["hello","world"]
        When Key is KeySpec: Options are SYMMETRIC_256, SYMMETRIC_128, RSA_2048, RSA_3072, RSA_4096, EC_P256K, EC_P256, EC_P384, EC_P521, EC_SM2. Case-sensitive. Example: ["SYMMETRIC_256","SYMMETRIC_128"]
        When Key is Description: Supports fuzzy search, case-insensitive. Example: ["hello","world"]
        When Key is KeyState: Options are Enable, Disable, PendingDelete, Archived, PendingImport. Case-sensitive. Example: ["Enable","PendingDelete"]
        When Key is KeyUsage: Options are ENCRYPT_DECRYPT, SIGN_VERIFY. Case-sensitive. Example: ["ENCRYPT_DECRYPT","SIGN_VERIFY"]
        When Key is ProtectionLevel: Options are SOFTWARE, HSM. Case-sensitive. Example: ["SOFTWARE","HSM"]
        When Key is RotateState: Options are Enable, Disable. Case-sensitive. Example: ["Enable","Disable"]
        When Key is Origin: Options are CloudKMS, External. Case-sensitive. Example: ["CloudKMS","External"]
        When Key is CreationDateRange: Enter both start and end time. Example: ["2024-08-13 10:00:00","2024-08-14 10:00:00"]

Filters.description_cn:

Key

    Type: String.
    Values:
        SecretName: Credential name.

        RotationState: Credential rotation status.

        CreationDateRange: Credential creation time range.
        UpdateDateRange: Credential update time range.
Values
    Description: Specific values for the attribute.
    Type: String list.
    Capacity: 1~10.
    Value instructions:
        When Key is SecretName: Supports fuzzy search, case-insensitive. Example: ["hello","world"].

        When Key is ManagedState: Values are true, false; case-sensitive. Example: ["true"].
        When Key is OwningService: Supports fuzzy search, case-insensitive. Example: ["kms","tos"].
        When Key is RotationState: Values are Enable, Disable, Rotating; case-sensitive. Example: ["Enable","Rotating"].
        When Key is Description: Supports fuzzy search, case-insensitive. Example: ["hello","world"].
        When Key is CreationDateRange: Must enter start time and end time. Example: ["2024-08-13 10:00:00","2024-08-14 10:00:00"].
        When Key is UpdateDateRange: Must enter start time and end time. Example: ["2024-08-13 10:00:00","2024-08-14 10:00:00"].
For Filters, multiple Values under the same Key use OR logic; different Keys use AND logic.
For example: Input [{"Key":"SecretName", "Values":["hello","world"]},{"Key":"SecretType", "Values":["ECS"]}] means: (SecretName=hello OR SecretName=world) AND (SecretType=ECS).

ReservationConfig.RecurrenceEndTime.description_cn:
End date for recurring appointment plan recurrence
- Must follow RFC3339 format, for example: 2025-04-17T00:00:00+08:00. Hours, minutes, and seconds must all be set to 0
- Time zone specification is supported
- The end date is inclusive. For example, if set to 2025-04-17T00:00:00+08:00, a delivery plan will be generated for April 17, 2025
- The end date cannot be earlier than the start date and must not exceed (start date + 28 days)
Do not set this field for time slot-based appointment plans

- The end date cannot be earlier than the start date and must not exceed (start date + 28 days)
Do not set this field for time slot-based appointment plans

ReservationConfig.RecurrenceEndTime.description_cn:
End Date for Recurring Appointment Plan
- Must follow the RFC3339 format, for example: 2025-04-17T00:00:00+08:00, with hour, minute, and second all set to 0
- Time zone can be specified
- The end date is inclusive; for example, if set to 2025-04-17T00:00:00+08:00, a delivery plan will also be generated for April 17, 2025
- The end date cannot be earlier than the start date and must not exceed (start date + 28) days
Do not enter this field for time-slot-based appointment plans

InstanceIds.description_cn:
Instance IDs for tag binding

- You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describedbinstances) API to view basic information for all MongoDB instances in the target region, including instance IDs
- You can enter multiple instance IDs at once, separated by commas (,). You can specify up to 20 instance IDs at a time

Tags.description_cn: Array object of tag keys and tag values that need to be bound
Tags.description_en: Array object of tag keys and tag values that need to be bound

Tags.Key.description_cn:
A tag key is required to bind tags.
- When binding tags to an instance, the tag key (Key) is required and the tag value (Value) is optional. If you leave the tag value empty, the tag value for the corresponding tag key will be empty.
- You can enter multiple tag key-value pairs at once, separated by commas (,). Up to 20 tag key-value pairs can be entered at the same time.
- Each instance can have up to 50 tags. Tag keys must follow the configuration rules. For details, see [Tag configuration rules](../6447/162957#标签设置规则).

AllowListIds.description_cn:
Whitelist ID required to bind to the instance

- You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describeallowlists) API to query all whitelists in a specified region, including whitelist IDs
- You can enter multiple whitelist IDs at once, separated by English commas (,)
- You cannot enter multiple instance IDs and whitelist IDs at the same time. You can only bind multiple instances to the same whitelist at once, or bind one instance to multiple whitelists at once

AllowList.description_cn:
Enter an IP address or a CIDR-formatted IP range

- Each whitelist group supports up to 1000 IP addresses or CIDR-formatted IP ranges
- Duplicate addresses are not allowed; separate multiple addresses with commas (,)
- Setting `0.0.0.0/0` allows access from all addresses
- Setting `127.0.0.1` blocks access from all addresses
- Setting both `0.0.0.0/0` and `127.0.0.1` allows access from all addresses
- Setting CIDR `192.168.1.0/24` allows access from IP addresses within that subnet
- Setting `192.168.1.1` allows access only from that IP address
AllowList.description_en:

- Setting CIDR `192.168.1.0/24` allows access from IP addresses within that subnet
- Setting `192.168.1.1` allows access only from that IP address

AllowListCategory.description_cn:
Whitelist type. Available values:

- `Ordinary` (default): Ordinary whitelist
- `Default`: Default whitelist
Each BytePlus account can set up to one default whitelist per region. When you set a new default whitelist, it automatically replaces the previous one, which will become a non-default whitelist. For more details, see [Constraints and limitations](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/product-limit).

AllowListDesc.description_cn:

AllowListName.description_cn:

- May contain only Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)

ProjectName.description_cn:
Set the project to which the whitelist belongs
A project is a virtual concept that includes a group of resources, users, and roles. Projects let you view and manage resources in a unified way, and control user and role permissions within the project. For more details, see [Resource Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6649/94333).
If you do not set this parameter, the newly created whitelist will be added to the default project.

AllShard.description_cn:
Whether to batch create connection addresses for all shard partitions in the current instance. Valid values:
- `true`: Batch create
- `false`: Do not batch create
- This parameter applies only to sharded cluster instances.
- When requesting connection addresses for shards or ConfigServer components in a sharded cluster, you are only allowed to select one parameter from `ObjectId`, `ObjectIds`, or `AllShard` to pass in. Otherwise, the API call will return an error.

EipIds.description_cn:
List of EIP IDs to bind when applying for a public network address

- This parameter is required only when `NetworkType` is set to `Public`. The number of EIP IDs you need to provide depends on the instance or component type:
  - When applying for a public network address for Mongos nodes, the number of EIP IDs must match the number of `MongosNodeIds`. For example, if you provide only one Mongos node ID, you only need to provide one EIP ID.
  - When applying for a public network address for replica set instances, Shard nodes, or ConfigServer nodes, you must provide two EIP IDs for each instance or component. For details on the number of EIP IDs required for each public network address, see [View connection addresses](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/addresses-introduction).
- You can call the [DescribeEipAddresses](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/eip/DescribeEipAddressAttributes) API to query the list of all EIP information, including available EIP IDs.

ObjectId.description_cn:
Single Shard or ConfigServer component ID for which you need to create a connection address

- This parameter applies only to sharded cluster instances
- When requesting a connection address for a Shard or ConfigServer component in a sharded cluster, you can only select one parameter from `ObjectId`, `ObjectIds`, or `AllShard`. Otherwise, the API call will return an error
- You can use the [DescribeDBEndpoint](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describedbendpoint) API to view all component IDs in the target sharded cluster instance
- Currently, you can only create connection addresses at the instance or component level via the API. Creating a separate connection address for a specific node (such as a primary or secondary node) within a component is not supported

ObjectIds.description_cn:

- This parameter applies only to sharded cluster instances
- When requesting a connection address for a Shard or ConfigServer component in a sharded cluster, you can only pass one of the following parameters: `ObjectId`, `ObjectIds`, or `AllShard`. Otherwise, the API call will fail
- You can use the [DescribeDBEndpoint](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describedbendpoint) API to view all component IDs under the target sharded cluster instance
- Currently, you can only create connection addresses at the instance or component level via the API. Creating separate connection addresses for individual nodes (such as primary or secondary nodes) within a component is not supported
