AllowListIds.description_cn:
Allowlist ID list. The new instance will be bound to the specified allowlist.
* You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describeallowlists) API to query all IP allowlist information under your account in the specified region, including allowlist ID information.
* Each instance supports binding up to 100 allowlists, and you can batch bind up to 100 allowlists at a time.
AllowListIds.description_en:
Allowlist ID list. The new instance will be bound to the specified allowlist.
* You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describeallowlists) API to query all IP allowlist information under your account in the specified region, including allowlist ID information.
* Each instance supports binding up to 100 allowlists, and you can batch bind up to 100 allowlists at a time.

AutoRenew.description_cn:
Enable auto-renewal. Value options:

* `false` (default): Auto-renewal is disabled.
* `true`: Auto-renewal is enabled.

This parameter is required when `ChargeType` is set to `Prepaid`.
AutoRenew.description_en:

* `false` (default): Auto-renewal is disabled.
* `true`: Auto-renewal is enabled.

This parameter is required when `ChargeType` is set to `Prepaid`.

ChargeType.description_cn:
Instance billing type. Available options:
- `PostPaid` (default): Pay-as-you-go (also called postpaid)
- `Prepaid`: Yearly/monthly subscription (also called prepaid)

For more information about billing types, see [Billing Types](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/billing-method).

ConfigServerNodeSpec.description_cn:
Specification code for the ConfigServer node in a sharded cluster. Default value: `mongo.config.2c4g`.
* This parameter is valid only when the instance type is a sharded cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`).
* You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view the specification information for sharded cluster instances, including specification codes.
ConfigServerNodeSpec.description_en:
Specification code for the ConfigServer node in a sharded cluster. Default value: `mongo.config.2c4g`.
* This parameter is valid only when the instance type is a sharded cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`).
* You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view the specification information for sharded cluster instances, including specification codes.

ConfigServerStorageSpaceGB.description_cn:
Storage space for ConfigServer in a sharded cluster, in GiB. Step size: 10. Default value: 20.
* This parameter is valid only when the instance type is a sharded cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`).
* The maximum supported storage space varies by node specification. You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view MongoDB instance specifications, including storage space specifications supported by different nodes.
ConfigServerStorageSpaceGB.description_en:
Storage space for ConfigServer in a sharded cluster, in GiB. Step size: 10. Default value: 20.
* This parameter is valid only when the instance type is a sharded cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`).
* The maximum supported storage space varies by node specification. You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view MongoDB instance specifications, including storage space specifications supported by different nodes.

Count.description_cn:
Number of instances to create. Must be a positive integer greater than or equal to 1. Default is 1.
* Each BytePlus primary account can purchase up to 30 MongoDB instances per region by default. Therefore, when using this API to create instances in bulk, you can create up to 30 instances per request by default. To increase your quota and purchase more instances, go to the **Quota Center** and submit a [quota request](https://console.volcengine.com/quota/productList/coParameterList?ProviderCode=MongoDB_ToB).
* If you specify an instance name and purchase multiple instances at the same time, the system will append a number to the end of each instance name according to the relevant rules for differentiation. For more details, see the rules for **Instance Name** in the [Create Instance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/create-instance#%E6%93%8D%E4%BD%9C%E6%AD%A5%E9%AA%A4) parameter configuration table.

DBInstanceParamTemplateId.description_en:
Select the parameter template ID to apply to the instance.
* Currently, only replica set instances (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ReplicaSet`) support parameter templates, so this parameter only applies to replica set instances. For more details about parameter templates, see [Parameter Template Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/parameter-template-overview).
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceParamTpl](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6447/1362939) API to query all parameter templates under your account and region, including parameter template ID information.
* If this parameter is not specified, no parameter template will be used, and all instance parameters will use default values.
   For example, if you create a new replica set instance with MongoDB version 6.0 and do not specify this parameter, the instance will use the system parameter template for MongoDB 6.0 by default.
* If you select a custom parameter template, but the template does not include all parameters supported by the instance, the instance will use the values from the template for included parameters, and default values for parameters not in the template.

InstanceName.description_cn:
Instance name. The name must meet the following requirements:

* Cannot start with a digit or a hyphen (-)
* Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, digits, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)
* Must be 2–64 characters in length

* If this parameter is not specified, the instance ID will be used as the instance name by default
* You can customize the instance name as needed; uniqueness is not required
* If you set an instance name and purchase multiple instances at once, the system will append a number to the end of each instance name according to specific rules for differentiation. For more details, see the rules for **Instance Name** in the parameter configuration table of [Create Instance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/create-instance#%E6%93%8D%E4%BD%9C%E6%AD%A5%E9%AA%A4)

NodeAvailabilityZone.NodeNumber.description_cn:
Number of read-only nodes to add in the current availability zone.

Currently, only Replica Set instances and Shard partitions within Sharded Cluster instances support adding read-only nodes. Among them:
- If the instance type is Replica Set (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ReplicaSet`), this value indicates the total number of read-only nodes in a single Replica Set instance. Each Replica Set instance supports up to 5 read-only nodes.
- If the instance type is Sharded Cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`), this value indicates the number of read-only nodes in each Shard partition. Each Shard partition supports up to 5 read-only nodes.
For more information about read-only node features and usage limits, see [MongoDB Read-Only Nodes](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/managing_read_only_nodes).

NodeNumber.description_cn:

* If the instance type is sharded cluster (i.e., `InstanceType` is `ShardedCluster`), this parameter specifies the number of nodes in each Shard.

Currently, each replica set instance and each Shard only support 3 nodes. The value is fixed at `3`.

ProjectName.description_cn:

A project is a virtual concept that includes a group of resources, users, and roles. Projects allow unified viewing and management of a group of resources, and control user and role permissions for these resources within the project. For more details, see [Resource Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6649/94333).

SuperAccountPassword.description_cn:
Password for the root account. The password must meet the following requirements:

* Can only contain uppercase and lowercase letters, digits, and the following special characters: `_#!@$%^&*()+=-`
* Must be 8–32 characters in length
* Must include at least three of the following: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, or special characters
* Weak passwords that are easily cracked (such as `Admin@123`) are not allowed

* If this parameter is left blank, no password will be set for the root account. The system will automatically generate a password for the root account to ensure instance security
* You can also change the root account password after instance creation using the [ResetDBAccount](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/resetdbaccount) API
* If you use special characters in the password, you may need to escape them when connecting to the instance. For more details, see [Special Characters That Need Escaping](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/account-and-permission#%E5%BD%93%E8%BF%9E%E6%8E%A5%E4%B8%B2%E4%B8%AD%E8%B4%A6%E5%8F%B7%E5%AF%86%E7%A0%81%E5%8C%85%E5%90%AB%E4%BA%86%E7%89%B9%E6%AE%8A%E5%AD%97%E7%AC%A6%E6%97%B6%EF%BC%8C%E4%B8%BA%E4%BD%95%E4%BC%9A%E5%AF%BC%E8%87%B4%E8%BF%9E%E6%8E%A5%E5%A4%B1%E8%B4%A5%EF%BC%9F)
* For details about prohibited weak passwords in MongoDB, see the [Weak Password List](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/account-overview%E5%BC%B1%E5%AF%86%E7%A0%81%E5%88%97%E8%A1%A8)

Tags.description_cn:
Array object of tag keys and tag values to bind.
Leaving this parameter blank means the new instance will not bind any tags.
Tags.description_en:
Array object of tag keys and tag values to bind.
Leaving this parameter blank means the new instance will not bind any tags.

Tags.Key.description_cn:
You must bind the tag key corresponding to the tag.
* When binding tags to an instance, the tag key (Key) is required. The tag value (Value) is optional. If the tag value is not provided, the tag value for the corresponding tag key will be empty.
* You can submit multiple tag key-value objects at once, separated by commas (,). Up to 20 tag key-value pairs can be submitted simultaneously.
* Each instance can be bound to a maximum of 50 tags. Tag keys must comply with the configuration rules. For details, see [Tag configuration rules](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/associate-tag#%E6%A0%87%E7%AD%BE%E8%AE%BE%E7%BD%AE%E8%A7%84%E5%88%99).

Tags.Value.description_cn:

- Each instance can have up to 50 tags. Tag keys must follow the configuration rules. For details, see [Tag Configuration Rules](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/associate-tag#%E6%A0%87%E7%AD%BE%E8%AE%BE%E7%BD%AE%E8%A7%84%E5%88%99).

Context.description_cn:
Pagination token for log query results, used to mark the current position in pagination.
- DescribeNormalLogs is a streaming API that supports pagination. If your instance contains a large number of log records, you may need to call this API multiple times to retrieve all logs.
- You can use the returned `ListOver` parameter to check if there are more logs to load, and use the `Context` pagination token to fetch logs in segments:
	- If `ListOver` is `false`, there are more logs matching your query that have not been loaded. Call DescribeNormalLogs again and use the `Context` value from the previous response to continue retrieving the remaining logs.
	- If `ListOver` is `true`, all logs matching your query have been loaded.

Keys.description_cn:
Search keywords are used to find running logs or error logs that contain specific keywords
- If you do not enter any keywords, the log search results will not be filtered by keywords
- You can enter multiple keywords separated by spaces. The keywords have an **OR** relationship
  For example, setting the search keywords to `"Keys":"warning error"` will return logs that contain either `warning` or `error`
- The maximum length for a log search query is 4 KiB. In addition to the `Keys` parameter, the query may include system-defined fields. To improve search efficiency and accuracy, we recommend not entering too many keywords
- Reserved keywords are not supported for search. For more information about reserved keywords, see [Log Search Reserved Keywords](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/log-overview#%E6%97%A5%E5%BF%97%E6%A3%80%E7%B4%A2%E9%A2%84%E7%95%99%E5%85%B3%E9%94%AE%E8%AF%8D)

Pagination token for slow log query results, used to mark the current position in pagination.
- DescribeSlowLogs is a streaming API that supports pagination. If your instance has many slow log records, you may need to call this API multiple times to retrieve all logs.
- Use the returned `ListOver` parameter to check if there are more slow log records to load. Combine it with the `Context` pagination token to fetch logs in segments:
    - If `ListOver` is `false`, there are more slow log records that match your query. Call DescribeSlowLogs again and use the `Context` value from the previous response to continue querying the remaining logs.
    - If `ListOver` is `true`, all matching slow log records have been loaded.
Context.description_en:
Pagination token for slow log query results, used to mark the current position in pagination.
- DescribeSlowLogs is a streaming API that supports pagination. If your instance has many slow log records, you may need to call this API multiple times to retrieve all logs.
- Use the returned `ListOver` parameter to check if there are more slow log records to load. Combine it with the `Context` pagination token to fetch logs in segments:
    - If `ListOver` is `false`, there are more slow log records that match your query. Call DescribeSlowLogs again and use the `Context` value from the previous response to continue querying the remaining logs.
    - If `ListOver` is `true`, all matching slow log records have been loaded.

- Enter CIDR `192.168.1.0/24` to allow access from all IP addresses in that subnet
- Enter `192.168.1.1` to allow access only from that IP address

You can only update the SSL certificate validity period after the SSL encryption feature is enabled. Call the [DescribeDBInstanceSSL](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describedbinstancessl) API to check whether the SSL encryption feature is enabled for your instance.

NodeSpec.description_cn:
Instance specification code. Details:

* If the instance type is ReplicaSet (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ReplicaSet`), this parameter specifies the compute node specification for the replica set instance (for example, `mongo.2c4g`).
* If the instance type is ShardedCluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`), this parameter specifies the specification for the Shard node (for example, `mongo.shard.2c4g`).

* You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view instance specification information, including the specification code.
* If this parameter is left empty or is the same as the current instance node specification, you will not change the current instance node specification.
NodeSpec.description_en:

* If the instance type is ShardedCluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`), this parameter specifies the specification for the Shard node (for example, `mongo.shard.2c4g`).

ShardNumber.description_cn:

* If this parameter is left empty or matches the current number of shards, the number of shards will not be changed.
ShardNumber.description_en:

StorageSpaceGB.description_cn:

* To ensure the instance runs properly after modification, the new storage space must be at least 1.2 times the used space.
* When `InstanceType` is `ReplicaSet`, the `StorageSpaceGB` parameter is the total storage space for the instance.
* When `InstanceType` is `ShardedCluster`, total capacity = `StorageSpaceGB` parameter × number of shards.
* If this parameter is left empty or matches the current storage space, the storage space will not be changed.

AccountPassword.description_cn:
Password for the database account. The password must meet all of the following requirements:
- Only uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and the following special characters are allowed: `_#!@$%^&*()+=-`
- Length must be between 8 and 32 characters
- Must include at least three of the following: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, or special characters
- Weak passwords that are easy to guess (such as `Admin@123`) are not allowed
- Changing the password may interrupt database connections that are currently using this account. Proceed with caution
- If your password contains special characters, you may need to escape them when connecting to an instance. For more details, see [Special characters that require escaping](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/account-and-permission#%E5%BD%93%E8%BF%9E%E6%8E%A5%E4%B8%B2%E4%B8%AD%E8%B4%A6%E5%8F%B7%E5%AF%86%E7%A0%81%E5%8C%85%E5%90%AB%E4%BA%86%E7%89%B9%E6%AE%8A%E5%AD%97%E7%AC%A6%E6%97%B6%EF%BC%8C%E4%B8%BA%E4%BD%95%E4%BC%9A%E5%AF%BC%E8%87%B4%E8%BF%9E%E6%8E%A5%E5%A4%B1%E8%B4%A5%EF%BC%9F)
- For details about weak passwords that are not allowed in MongoDB, see [Weak password list](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/account-overview#%E5%BC%B1%E5%AF%86%E7%A0%81%E5%88%97%E8%A1%A8)

BackupId.description_cn:
Backup file ID of the source instance, used to specify the backup for restoration by backup file.
* Either the `BackupId` or `RestoreTime` parameter must be provided.
* You can call the [DescribeBackups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describebackups) API to query all backup information for a specified instance, including backup IDs.
* Currently, only replica set instances support restoring to a new instance by backup set. Sharded cluster instances are not supported. For more information about restoring to a new instance by backup file, see [Restore by Backup File](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/recovery-from-backup-file).

* Currently, only replica set instances support restoring to a new instance by backup set. Sharded cluster instances are not supported. For more information about restoring to a new instance by backup file, see [Restore by Backup File](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/recovery-from-backup-file).

ChargeType.description_cn:

ConfigServerNodeSpec.description_cn:

* This parameter is effective only when the instance type is a sharded cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`).

ConfigServerNodeSpec.description_en:

* You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view specification information for sharded cluster instances, including specification codes.

ConfigServerStorageSpaceGB.description_cn:
Storage space for ConfigServer in a sharded cluster, unit: GiB. Increment: 10. Default: 20
* This parameter only takes effect when the instance type is a sharded cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`)
* The maximum supported storage varies by node specification. You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view MongoDB instance specifications, including supported storage sizes for different nodes
* To ensure the new instance created from a backup can run properly, its storage capacity must be **greater than or equal to 1.2 times the used space of the original instance**. For more details, see [Restore from Backup File](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/recovery-from-backup-file) or [Point-in-Time Recovery](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/recovery-by-time-point)

* The maximum supported storage varies by node specification. You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view MongoDB instance specifications, including supported storage sizes for different nodes
* To ensure the new instance created from a backup can run properly, its storage capacity must be **greater than or equal to 1.2 times the used space of the original instance**. For more details, see [Restore from Backup File](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/recovery-from-backup-file) or [Point-in-Time Recovery](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/recovery-by-time-point)

DBEngine.description_en:

DBEngineVersion.description_cn:

DBEngineVersion.description_en:

InstanceName.description_cn:

* Cannot start with a number or hyphen (-).
* Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-).
* Length must be 2–64 characters.

* If this parameter is not specified, the instance ID will be used as the default instance name.
* You can customize the instance name as needed. Instance names do not need to be unique.

NodeAvailabilityZone.description_en:
Add read-only node information, including the availability zone where the read-only nodes are located and the number of read-only nodes

NodeAvailabilityZone.NodeNumber.description_cn:
Number of read-only nodes to add in the current availability zone

Only Replica Set instances and Sharded Cluster instances support adding read-only nodes to Shard partitions:
- If the instance type is Replica Set (`InstanceType` is `ReplicaSet`), this value indicates the total number of read-only nodes in a single Replica Set instance. You can add up to 5 read-only nodes per Replica Set instance.
- If the instance type is Sharded Cluster (`InstanceType` is `ShardedCluster`), this value indicates the number of read-only nodes in each Shard partition. You can add up to 5 read-only nodes per Shard partition.
For more information about read-only node features and usage limits, see [MongoDB Read-Only Nodes](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/managing_read_only_nodes).

- If the instance type is Sharded Cluster (`InstanceType` is `ShardedCluster`), this value indicates the number of read-only nodes in each Shard partition. You can add up to 5 read-only nodes per Shard partition.

NodeNumber.description_cn:

* If the source instance type is a sharded cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`), this parameter specifies the number of nodes in each Shard of the new sharded cluster instance after recovery.

Currently, each replica set instance and each Shard only support 3 nodes. The value is fixed at `3`.

* If the source instance type is a replica set (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ReplicaSet`), this parameter specifies the compute node specification for the new replica set instance after recovery
* If the source instance type is a sharded cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`), this parameter specifies the Shard node specification for the new sharded cluster instance after recovery

You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view instance specification information, including specification codes

Port.description_cn:
Set the port number for the private network connection address of the restored new instance. Value range: 1000~65535.
* If this parameter is left empty, the instance's private network connection address uses port 3717 by default.
* After the instance is created, you can also modify the connection address port number via the [ModifyDBEndpointPort](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/modifydbendpointport) API. For more details, see [Modify Port Number](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/modifying_ports).

ProjectName.description_cn:
Select the project to which the instance belongs. If this parameter is left blank, the new instance will be added to the default project.
A project is a virtual concept that includes a group of resources, users, and roles. Projects allow unified viewing and management of resources, and control user and role permissions within the project. For more details, see [Resource Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6649/94333).

RestoreTime.description_cn:
Specifies the point in time to restore to during point-in-time recovery. Format: *yyyy-MM-dd*T*HH:mm:ss*Z (UTC).
* You must provide either the `BackupId` or `RestoreTime` parameter.
* You can call the [DescribeRecoverableTime](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describerecoverabletime) API to query the recoverable time range supported by the specified instance.
* We recommend restoring to a point within the last 7 days. Restoring to a point older than 7 days may affect the read/write performance of primary and secondary instances. For more information about point-in-time recovery to a new instance, see [Point-in-Time Recovery](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/recovery-by-time-point).

StorageSpaceGB.description_cn:
Total storage space for a replica set instance, or storage space for a single Shard in a sharded cluster, unit: GiB, increment: 10
* If the instance type is a sharded cluster (that is, `InstanceType` is set to `ShardedCluster`), the total capacity of the instance after creation is the storage space per Shard multiplied by the number of Shards
* You can call the [DescribeNodeSpecs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/describenodespecs) API to view MongoDB instance specifications, including supported storage sizes for different nodes
* To ensure the new instance created from a backup can run properly, its storage capacity must be **greater than or equal to 1.2 times the used space of the original instance**. For more details, see [Restore from Backup File](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/recovery-from-backup-file) or [Point-in-Time Recovery](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/recovery-by-time-point)

SuperAccountPassword.description_cn:
Password for the root account. The password must meet all of the following requirements:

* Must include at least three of the following: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, or special characters.
* Special characters include `!@#$%^&*()_+-=`.
* Length must be 8–32 characters.
* Weak passwords that are easily cracked (such as `Admin@123`) are not allowed.

* If this parameter is left blank, no password will be set for the root account. In this case, the system will automatically generate a password for the root account to ensure instance security.
* You can also modify the root account password after instance creation using the [ResetDBAccount](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/resetdbaccount) API.
* If you use special characters in the password, you may need to escape them when connecting to the instance. For details, see [Special characters that require escaping](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/account-and-permission#%E5%BD%93%E8%BF%9E%E6%8E%A5%E4%B8%B2%E4%B8%AD%E8%B4%A6%E5%8F%B7%E5%AF%86%E7%A0%81%E5%8C%85%E5%90%AB%E4%BA%86%E7%89%B9%E6%AE%8A%E5%AD%97%E7%AC%A6%E6%97%B6%EF%BC%8C%E4%B8%BA%E4%BD%95%E4%BC%9A%E5%AF%BC%E8%87%B4%E8%BF%9E%E6%8E%A5%E5%A4%B1%E8%B4%A5%EF%BC%9F).
* For details about weak passwords prohibited in MongoDB, see the [Weak password list](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/account-overview%E5%BC%B1%E5%AF%86%E7%A0%81%E5%88%97%E8%A1%A8).

Tags.description_cn:
Array object of tag keys and tag values to bind.
Leaving this parameter empty means the new instance will not be bound to any tags.
Tags.description_en:

Tags.Key.description_cn:
You need to bind the tag key corresponding to the tag.
- When binding tags to an instance, the tag key (Key) is required. The tag value (Value) is optional. If you leave the tag value blank, the tag key will have an empty value.
- You can enter multiple tag key-value objects at once, separated by English commas (,). You can enter up to 20 tag key-value pairs at a time.
- Each instance can have up to 50 tags. Tag keys must follow the configuration rules. For details, see [Tag configuration rules](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/associate-tag#%E6%A0%87%E7%AD%BE%E8%AE%BE%E7%BD%AE%E8%A7%84%E5%88%99).

ZoneId.description_cn:

* If you need to deploy the new instance across multiple availability zones, you can specify up to three availability zone IDs, separated by commas (,). For more details, see [Multi-AZ Disaster Recovery Solution](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/feature-introduction).

NodeId.description_cn:

AccountDBPrivileges.description_cn:
List of database permissions to modify for the account
- If you do not set this parameter, the account's permissions for all databases remain unchanged
- Modifying account permissions may cause errors when connecting to the database, such as "no access permission," which can affect your business. Proceed with caution
- Do not leave both `AccountDBPrivileges` and `AccountDesc` parameters empty at the same time
AccountDBPrivileges.description_en:
List of database permissions to modify for the account
- If you do not set this parameter, the account's permissions for all databases remain unchanged
- Modifying account permissions may cause errors when connecting to the database, such as "no access permission," which can affect your business. Proceed with caution
- Do not leave both `AccountDBPrivileges` and `AccountDesc` parameters empty at the same time

AccountDBPrivileges.DBName.description_cn:
Database name to grant account permissions

The MongoDB version of the document database allows you to grant permissions for certain system databases as well as your own custom databases. The following database names are supported:
- System databases: Includes `admin`, `local`, and `config`
- Other databases: Any database you create, such as `testdb`

- For details on permissions available for different types of databases, see [Database and account permissions](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/account-overview#%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE%E5%BA%93%E4%B8%8E%E8%B4%A6%E5%8F%B7%E6%9D%83%E9%99%90)
- You can use the [listDatabases](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v5.0/reference/command/listDatabases/) command to view the database names in your current MongoDB instance
AccountDBPrivileges.DBName.description_en:
Database name to grant account permissions

The MongoDB version of the document database allows you to grant permissions for certain system databases as well as your own custom databases. The following database names are supported:
- System databases: Includes `admin`, `local`, and `config`
- Other databases: Any database you create, such as `testdb`

- For details on permissions available for different types of databases, see [Database and account permissions](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/account-overview#%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE%E5%BA%93%E4%B8%8E%E8%B4%A6%E5%8F%B7%E6%9D%83%E9%99%90)
- You can use the [listDatabases](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v5.0/reference/command/listDatabases/) command to view the database names in your current MongoDB instance

AccountDBPrivileges.RoleNames.description_cn:
Database permissions to grant to the account
The permissions you can grant for each database in MongoDB are as follows:
- `admin` database: You can grant the account the following permissions in the `admin` database: `read`, `userAdmin`, `readAnyDatabase`, `readWriteAnyDatabase`, `userAdminAnyDatabase`, `dbAdminAnyDatabase`, `clusterMonitor`, and `backup`
- `local` database: You can only grant the `read` permission in the `local` database
- `config` database: You can only grant the `read` permission in the `config` database
- Other databases: You can grant the account `read`, `readWrite`, `dbAdmin`, `userAdmin`, and `dbOwner` permissions in databases you create

- For details on permissions available for different database types, see [Database and Account Permissions](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/account-overview#%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE%E5%BA%93%E4%B8%8E%E8%B4%A6%E5%8F%B7%E6%9D%83%E9%99%90)
- Permission changes are overwrite operations. The list of permissions in `RoleNames` under `AccountDBPrivileges` will replace the account's permissions for the specified `DBName` database
- If this parameter is left empty, all permissions for the account in the specified `DBName` database will be removed. Proceed with caution

- `local` database: You can only grant the `read` permission in the `local` database
- `config` database: You can only grant the `read` permission in the `config` database
- Other databases: You can grant the account `read`, `readWrite`, `dbAdmin`, `userAdmin`, and `dbOwner` permissions in databases you create

- For details on permissions available for different database types, see [Database and Account Permissions](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/mongodb/account-overview#%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE%E5%BA%93%E4%B8%8E%E8%B4%A6%E5%8F%B7%E6%9D%83%E9%99%90)

ExternalIp.description_cn:

- For a private NAT gateway, enter its transit IP address
ExternalIp.description_en:

ExternalPort.description_cn:
This parameter specifies the external port or port range for incoming requests
- If PortType is set to any, this parameter must also be set to any
- If PortType is set to specified:
  - Port range must be 1–65535
  - If InternalPort is a port range, ExternalPort must also be a port range with the same number of ports. Use a hyphen (-) to separate the start and end ports. For example, if InternalPort is set to 20-25, ExternalPort should be set to 30-35

SubnetId.description_cn:

- The subnet must have at least one available private IP. The automatically generated NAT Gateway network interface will occupy one private IP in this subnet.
- The subnet's availability zone must have deployed NAT Gateway resources. You can call DescribeSubnets to query the availability zone of the subnet under the private network, and you can also call [ListNatGatewayAvailableZones](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/natgateway/ListNatGatewayAvailableZones) to check which availability zones in the current region have NAT Gateway resources. The subnet's availability zone will be used as the primary availability zone for the NAT Gateway and will automatically associate with a backup availability zone. If the primary availability zone fails, the NAT Gateway will automatically switch to the backup availability zone.

SourceCidr.description_cn:
Specify the network segment for the SNAT rule. Different granularities correspond to different network segments, as follows:

Private network granularity: Specify the network segment of the private network where the NAT gateway is located. All cloud server instances in this private network without a public IP can access the internet through the SNAT rule.

Subnet granularity: Specify the subnet segment (for example, 192.XX.XX.0/24). All cloud server instances in this subnet without a public IP can access the internet through the SNAT rule.

Cloud server granularity: Specify the segment of the cloud server (for example, 192.XX.XX.20/32). The specified cloud server instance without a public IP can access the internet through the SNAT rule.

Custom segment granularity: Specify a custom segment (for example, 192.XX.XX.0/26). All cloud server instances within this custom segment without a public IP can access the internet through the SNAT rule.

Note: You must specify either SubnetId or SourceCidr, but not both. If you enter SubnetId, do not enter SourceCidr. If you enter SourceCidr, do not enter SubnetId. The specified network segment cannot overlap with the network segments of existing SNAT rules.

EipId.description_cn: The ID of the public IP bound to the public NAT gateway. Separate multiple public IP IDs with commas. You can call the [DescribeEipAddresses](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/eip/DescribeEipAddressAttributes) API to query the public IP ID. If you enter a single IP, the SNAT rule will be associated with that public IP, and all business connections will access the public network through it. If you enter multiple public IPs, the SNAT rule will be associated with multiple public IPs. Business connections will access the public network through the public IP assigned by the five-tuple hash algorithm.  When a SNAT rule is associated with multiple public IPs, it is recommended to add the public IPs to a shared bandwidth package to avoid packet loss caused by bandwidth limits on any single public IP.
EipId.description_en: The ID of the public IP bound to the public NAT gateway. Separate multiple public IP IDs with commas. If you enter multiple public IPs, the SNAT rule will be associated with multiple public IPs. Business connections will access the public network through the public IP assigned by the five-tuple hash algorithm.  When a SNAT rule is associated with multiple public IPs, it is recommended to add the public IPs to a shared bandwidth package to avoid packet loss caused by bandwidth limits on any single public IP.

IpAddressVersions.description_cn:
IP protocol type for the endpoint service.

* ipv4 (default)
* ipv6: This option is currently in invitation testing. To use it, please contact your account manager.

* If you specify **ipv4** only, the endpoint service is IPv4 type and supports only IPv4 services.
* If you specify both **ipv4** and **ipv6**, the endpoint service is dual-stack, supporting both IPv4 and IPv6 services. The system automatically assigns an IPv6 address.
     To specify **ipv6**, make sure you meet the following requirements:
   * IPv6 feature for Private Network Connection Service is enabled.
   * The specified service resource supports dual-stack.
* Specifying **ipv6** only is not supported at this time.

IpAddressVersions.description_cn:
The IP protocol type of the interface endpoint. Valid values are **ipv4** and **ipv6**.

* The default protocol for interface endpoints is **ipv4**. If only **ipv4** is used, do not pass this parameter.
* If the interface endpoint is dual-stack (**ipv4&ipv6**), you must pass this parameter. Before passing it, make sure the following conditions are met:
   * Your account has enabled the IPv6 feature for PrivateLink.
   * The subnet to which the interface endpoint belongs has enabled the IPv6 CIDR block.
   * The endpoint service associated with the interface endpoint is dual-stack.
* Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the interface endpoint IP protocol type. The value range is 1–2. Use & to separate the sequence numbers of the two IP protocol types.
* Currently, only passing IPv6 is not supported.

The IPv6 feature for PrivateLink is currently in invitation testing. To use it, please contact your account manager.

IpAddressVersions.description_cn:
IP protocol type for the endpoint service. Valid values are **ipv4** and **ipv6**.

* The default for endpoint service is **ipv4**. If only **ipv4** is used, do not provide this parameter.
* If the endpoint service is dual stack (**ipv4&ipv6**), you must provide this parameter. Before providing it, make sure the following conditions are met:
   * IPv6 functionality for Private Network Connect Service is enabled.
   * The specified service resource supports dual stack.
* Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the endpoint service IP protocol type. Valid values are 1–2. Use & to separate the sequence numbers of the two IP protocol types.
* Currently, only providing IPv6 is not supported.

IPv6 functionality for Private Network Connect Service is currently in invitation testing. To use it, please contact your account manager.

PrivateDNSEnabled.description_cn:
Whether to enable private DNS name for the endpoint service.

* false (default): Not enabled.
* true: Enabled.
PrivateDNSEnabled.description_en:
Whether to enable private DNS name for the endpoint service.

* false (default): Not enabled.
* true: Enabled.

PrivateDNSName.description_cn:
Private DNS name, which is the custom domain name you want to use when accessing the service via private network connection. Only public domain names are supported.
Public domain names do not support passing internal domain names with global resolution configured, nor domain names used for private network connections (including endpoint service domain names and endpoint domain names).

* When `PrivateDNSEnabled` is set to **true**, this parameter is required.
* If a wildcard domain name such as `*.www.example.com` is provided, both the wildcard domain and its root domain `www.example.com` are supported for resolution.

PrivateDNSType.description_cn:

Resources.N.ZoneIds.N.description_en:
Availability zone where the load balancer provides service.

* When ServiceResourceType is **ALB**, this parameter is required.

   * The second N: Indicates the sequence number of the availability zone where the resource provides service, valid values are 1–the maximum number of supported availability zones.
* When ServiceResourceType is **CLB**, you do not need to provide this parameter. The main availability zone of the CLB instance is used by default.

Tags.N.Key.description_en:

* Length limit: 1–128 characters.
* Case sensitive. Cannot start with any case combination of `volc:` or `sys:`.
* Cannot start or end with a space.
* Letters, numbers, spaces (), underscores (_), periods (.), colons (:), slashes (/), equal signs (=), plus signs (+), minus signs (-), and @ are allowed.

Tag keys for the same resource cannot be duplicated.

TagFilters.N.Values.N.description_en:
Tag value for the endpoint service tag. Each tag key can specify up to 3 tag values.

* If this parameter is not provided, queries all endpoint services associated with all tag values under the specified tag key.
* If this parameter is empty, queries endpoint services associated with tags under the specified tag key that have empty tag values.
* If multiple tag values are specified for the same tag key, queries the set of endpoint services associated with each tag value under that tag key.

If you provide this parameter, you must first provide `TagFilters.N.Key`.

IpAddressVersions.description_cn:
IP protocol type of the endpoint service.

* ipv4
* ipv6: This value is currently in invitation testing. To use it, please contact your account manager.

* If you enter only **ipv4**, the endpoint service is converted to IPv4 type and supports only IPv4 services.
* If you enter both **ipv4** and **ipv6**, the endpoint service is converted to dual-stack type, supporting both IPv4 and IPv6 services. The system automatically assigns an IPv6 address.
     To enter **ipv6**, make sure the following conditions are met:
   * IPv6 feature for PrivateLink service is enabled.
   * The specified service resource supports dual-stack.
* Currently, entering only **ipv6** is not supported.
* If you do not change this parameter value, the original configuration remains unchanged.

   * The subnet of the interface endpoint has IPv6 enabled.

PrivateDNSName.description_cn:

ResourceReplaceMode.description_cn:
Mode for replacing service resources.

* grace: Smooth replacement. The current endpoint network interface remains connected to the old service resource. The endpoint creates a new network interface to connect to the new service resource. New traffic is sent to the new connection by default. After the old connection has no traffic, you need to call the [DisableVpcEndpointConnection](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/privatelink/DisableVpcEndpointConnection) API to manually disconnect the old connection.

Smooth switchover is achieved by creating a new network interface for the endpoint. Please carefully evaluate the business impact before proceeding.


* force: Immediate replacement. The endpoint network interface immediately disconnects from the original service resource and connects to the new service resource.

AllowList.description_en:
IP address list that allows access from these IP addresses

- Separate multiple IP addresses with commas (,) and do not repeat any addresses
- Supports the following two formats:

- IP address format, for example: 10.23.12.xx
- CIDR format, for example: 10.23.12.x/xx

- If you have many IP addresses, we recommend combining them into IP ranges, such as 10.23.12.x/24
- Each instance can add up to 300 IP addresses or IP ranges; the total number of IP addresses or IP ranges in all allowlist groups cannot exceed 300

AllowListDesc.description_en: Allowlist description. Maximum 200 characters.

ChargeInfo.description_en: Billing type and other billing information for the RabbitMQ instance.

ClientToken.description_en:
Idempotency token for client requests.
This token is a 1–64 character ASCII string, case-sensitive, generated by the client. Ensure the token is unique for each request.
For how to use idempotency tokens, see [Request Idempotency](/docs/6451/1160443).

ComputeSpec.description_en:
Instance compute specification.
For the list of compute specifications provided by Message Queue for RabbitMQ instances, see [Product Specifications](/docs/6451/72249).

EipId.description_en:
EIP ID.
- Specifying EipId enables public network access for the instance.
- EIP provides independent public IP resources, including public IP addresses and outbound bandwidth services. After enabling public network access by specifying this parameter, the public address will be bound to your Elastic Public IP (EIP), and EIP charges will apply.

InstanceDescription.description_en: Brief description of the RabbitMQ instance. Length must be between 1 and 128 characters.

InstanceName.description_en:
Name of the RabbitMQ instance. Must meet the following requirements:
- Can only contain Chinese Hanzi characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)
- Cannot start with a number or hyphen (-)
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
If no name is specified when creating the instance, the instance ID will be used as the default name.

IsEncrypted.description_en: Use disk encryption (only available for whitelisted financial users)

NetworkTypes.description_en: Network type. Multiple selections separated by commas. This option is only visible to innerapi users.

ProjectName.description_en:
The IAM project to which the currently created RabbitMQ instance belongs.
If no IAM project is specified, Message Queue for RabbitMQ will add the new instance to the IAM project named default.

StorageSpace.description_en:
Instance storage space.
Unit: GiB. Must be a multiple of 100. The value range and default value depend on the specified compute specification.

SubnetId.description_en:
VPC subnet ID where the instance is located.
- After the instance is created, the corresponding private network and subnet cannot be modified. Please operate carefully when creating the instance.
- You can call the DescribeVpcs API of the private network (VPC) to query the list of available VPCs and subnets.

TagMap.description_en: Cloud resource tags. You can categorize instances by tags for easier search and resource aggregation. For details, see [Tag Management].

Tags.description_en: Cloud resource tags. You can categorize instances using tags to make searching and resource aggregation easier. For details, see [Tag Management](/docs/6451/166385).

UserName.description_en:
User name. Must meet the following requirements:
- Consist of letters, numbers, hyphens (-), or underscores (_)
- Length must be between 3 and 64 characters

UserPassword.description_en:
User password. Must meet the following requirements:
- Length must be 8–32 characters
- Must contain at least three of the following: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, special characters
- Supported special characters: `!@#$%^&*()_+-=`

Version.description_en:
Supported RabbitMQ versions. Currently supported versions include:
- 3.8.18: RabbitMQ version 3.8.18
- 3.12: RabbitMQ version 3.12

VpcId.description_en:
Private network (VPC) ID where the instance is located.
- After the instance is created, the corresponding private network and subnet cannot be modified. Please operate carefully when creating the instance.
- You can call the DescribeVpcs API of the private network (VPC) to query the list of available VPCs and subnets.

ZoneId.description_en:

- During the maintenance window, the instance may experience 1 to 2 brief connection interruptions. Make sure your application supports automatic reconnection.
- The maintenance window must be at least 1 hour and no more than 24 hours. The window cannot span across days.
- After the instance is created, use the ModifyDBInstanceMaintenanceWindow API to change the maintenance window. For details, see ModifyDBInstanceMaintenanceWindow.

IgnoreInstanceStatus.description_en:

- true: Ignore
- false: Do not ignore (default)
When this field is set to true, if the status of an instance bound to the current whitelist is not running, pre-validation will be skipped. The whitelist update will only apply to instances in the running state. For instances not in the running state, the whitelist changes will not be synced this time, and their sync status will be set to Not Synced. To sync manually, go to the instance list on the whitelist details page and click Sync Whitelist, or the service will automatically sync instance whitelists every 30 minutes.

AllowList.description_en:
Enter an IP address or a CIDR-formatted IP address range

- Each whitelist group supports up to 300 IP addresses or CIDR-formatted IP address ranges
- Duplicate addresses are not allowed; separate multiple addresses with English commas (,)
- Setting `0.0.0.0/0` allows access from all addresses
- Setting `127.0.0.1` blocks access from all addresses
- Setting both `0.0.0.0/0` and `127.0.0.1` allows access from all addresses
- Setting CIDR `192.168.1.0/24` allows access from IP addresses within that subnet
- Setting `192.168.1.1` allows access only from that IP address
- This field cannot be used together with the UserAllowList field

AllowListCategory.description_en:
Whitelist category. Possible values:

- `Ordinary`: Ordinary whitelist
- `Default`: Default whitelist

When used as a request parameter, the default value is `Ordinary`

AllowListDesc.description_en: Whitelist remark cannot exceed 200 characters

AllowListName.description_en:
Whitelist name requirements (must meet all of the following):

- Must not start with a number or hyphen (-)
- Can only include Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters

AllowListType.description_en: Type of IP address in the whitelist Only IPv4 addresses are supported

This field cannot be used together with SecurityGroupIds

SecurityGroupIds.description_en:
List of security group IDs to associate

- You can call the [DescribeSecurityGroups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSecurityGroups) API to query security group information, including security group IDs. You can add up to 10 security groups to a single whitelist at a time
- This field cannot be used together with SecurityGroupBindInfos

UserAllowList.description_en:
IP addresses outside the security group that need to be whitelisted. Enter an IP address or an IP address range in CIDR format.

This field cannot be used together with the AllowList field.

BackupMeta.description_en:
When creating a logical backup of database tables, use this to specify the database and table information to be backed up.
- For logical backups (BackupMethod=Logical) with the backup method as specified database table backup (BackupType parameter not provided), this parameter is required. For other backup types and methods, this parameter is not applicable.
- Quantity limits: When creating a specified database table backup, the maximum number of databases is 5000, and the maximum number of tables per database is 5000.

BackupMethod.description_en:
Supported backup types vary by instance storage type:
- If the instance storage type is local disk, you can choose physical backup `Physical` (default) or logical backup `Logical`.
- If the instance storage type is cloud disk, only snapshot backup `Snapshot` is available.

BackupName.description_en:
Set the backup name. Naming rules are as follows:
- Cannot start with a hyphen (-).
- Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-).
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters.

If not set, the backup ID will be used as the backup name.

BackupType.description_en:
Backup method.

- Value range:
	- If the backup type is physical backup `Physical` or snapshot backup `Snapshot`, choose full backup `Full` (default) or incremental backup `HighFrequencyIncrement`.
	- If the backup type is logical backup `Logical`, choose full database backup `DumpAll`; for backup sets of specified database tables, you do not need to provide this parameter, just specify the databases and tables in the BackupMeta parameter.

DataBackupTime.description_en: Used to support the feature of re-initiating backup after maintenance operations if still within the backup window

AccountName.description_en:
Database account name. Naming rules:

- Must be 2–32 characters long
- Starts with a letter and ends with a letter or number
- Can include letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)
- Account name must be unique within the instance
- Certain reserved words cannot be used. For disabled reserved words, see the [disabled words list](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/list_of_forbidden_keywords)

You can use the keywords root and admin in high-privilege account names

AccountPassword.description_en:
Password for the database account. Rules:

- Must be 8–32 characters long
- Must contain at least three of the following: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, special characters
- Allowed special characters: `!#$%&()*+,-.=?@^_|/`

AccountPrivileges.description_en:
Specified database permission information for the account

When AccountType is set to `Super`, you do not need to provide a value for AccountPrivileges

AccountType.description_en:
Database account types. Available values:

- `Super`: High-privilege account. Only one can be created per instance
- `Normal`: Standard account

AuthenticationType.description_en:
Authentication type for database accounts. Possible values:
- `MySQLNative`: MySQL native authentication
- `IAM`: IAM authentication

- When used as a request parameter, the default value is `MySQLNative`
- You can only specify the authentication type when creating an account; it cannot be changed after the account is created
- We recommend using IAM authentication only if your application creates fewer than 200 new IAM database authentication connections per second
- The total number of new IAM database authentication connections created per second across all instances under the primary account must not exceed 20,000. If this limit is exceeded, throttling will occur and new connections cannot be established
- After selecting IAM authentication, your application will use a generated temporary Token for authentication when connecting to the database. Frequent creation of IAM database authentication connections may exceed the connection limit. We recommend managing connections centrally through a connection pool so your application can reuse existing connections and reduce the overhead caused by frequent IAM authentication

DryRun.description_en:
Whether to preview the SQL statements for creating the account. Options:
- `true`: Yes
- `false`: No (default)
- If set to `true`, the CreateAccountSQL field will be returned (the account will not actually be created). If set to `false` or not provided, the return value is null
- If you grant permissions to a specified database and the database name contains an underscore (_), the SQL statements returned in the CreateAccountSQL field will escape the underscore (_) as (\\_)

Host.description_en:
Specify the IP address for the account to access the database. The default value is %.

- If Host is set to %, the account can access the database from any IP address
- You can use wildcards to define IP address ranges that can access the database. For example, if Host is set to 192.10.10.%, the account can access the database from IP addresses between `192.10.10.0` and `192.10.10.255`
- The specified Host must be added to the allowlist bound to the instance, or the account will not be able to access the instance. You can call the [ModifyAllowList](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/modifyallowlist1) API to add the Host to the allowlist

If you create a high-privilege account, the host IP can only be set to `%`. That is, when AccountType is `Super`, Host can only be `%`.

AutoUpgradeMinorVersion.description_en:
Upgrade policy for instance kernel minor versions. Options:
- `Auto`: Automatic upgrade. When a new kernel minor version is released, the instance will automatically upgrade to the latest kernel minor version during the configured [maintenance window](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/setting_a_maintenance_period?lang=zh).
- `Manual`: Manual upgrade. When a new kernel minor version is released, you need to manually upgrade to the latest kernel minor version in the console. For details, see [Manually upgrade instance kernel minor version](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/upgrading_instance_kernel_minor_version?lang=zh).
If the kernel minor version of the instance exceeds the maintenance cycle, the system will temporarily ignore the kernel minor version upgrade policy and automatically upgrade the instance kernel minor version.

ChargeInfo.example_en: Please refer to the request example.

DBEngineVersion.description_en:
Compatible versions for green instances. Options:
- `MySQL_5_7`: MySQL 5.7 version.
- `MySQL_8_0`: MySQL 8.0 version.

DBParamGroupId.description_en:
Parameter template ID applied to green instances in blue-green deployment.
- If the database compatibility version of blue and green instances is the same and this parameter is not set, the parameter configuration of the blue instance is inherited.
- If the database compatibility version of blue and green instances differs, this parameter is required.

DeletionProtection.description_en:
Whether to enable deletion protection for the instance. Values:
- `Enabled`: Yes.
- `Disabled`: No (default).

InstanceId.description_en: ID of the blue instance in the blue-green deployment.

InstanceName.description_en:
Name of the green instance. Naming rules:
- Cannot start with a digit or hyphen.
- Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens.
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters.

If you do not set a name for the green instance, it will be named by default in the format `${blue instance name}-green-${uuid6}` and truncated if it exceeds 128 characters.

InstanceType.description_en:
Instance types for green instances. Options:
- `DoubleNode`: Double node type.
- `MultiNode`: Multi node type.
- `SingleNode`: Single node type.

- If the blue instance type is single node, you can select single node or double node type for the green instance.
- If the blue instance type is double node, you can select double node or multi node type for the green instance.
- If the blue instance type is multi node, you can only select multi node type for the green instance.

MinorVersion.description_en: Minor kernel version for the green instance in a blue-green deployment. You can select the minor kernel version of the blue instance or the latest minor kernel version.

NodeInfo.description_en: Specification configuration for the green instance in a blue-green deployment.
NodeInfo.example_en: Please refer to the request example.

PrivateIpAddress.description_en: The default endpoint IP address of the specified instance in the specified VPC and subnet.

ProxyNodeCustom.description_en:
Proxy CPU cores for green instances in blue-green deployment.
- The proxy feature status for green instances is enabled by default to match blue instances. If the proxy feature is enabled for blue instances, the proxy CPU cores for green instances are set to match blue instances by default.
- If the proxy feature for blue instances is disabled and the `CpuNum` parameter is set to a value greater than 0, the proxy feature for green instances will be forcibly enabled, and the specified value will be used as the number of CPU cores for the proxy service.
- If the proxy feature for blue instances is enabled and the `CpuNum` parameter is set to 0, the proxy feature for green instances will be forcibly disabled.
ProxyNodeCustom.example_en: Please refer to the request example.

ServiceArea.description_en: Optional sales zone, public service zone

StorageSpace.description_en: Storage space for the green instance in a blue-green deployment. The value must not be less than the storage space of the blue instance.

StorageType.description_en:
Instance storage type. Value options:
- `LocalSSD`: Local disk.
- `CloudESSD_FlexPL`: FlexPL cloud disk.
- `CloudESSD_PL0`: PL0 cloud disk.
- If you need to set the StorageSpace parameter, the StorageType parameter is required.
- When InstanceType is set to `SingleNode`, StorageType can only be `CloudESSD_FlexPL` or `CloudESSD_PL0`.
- The value range of this parameter varies by interface. Specific rules are as follows:
	- When used as a request parameter in the following interfaces, StorageType can only be `LocalSSD`.
		- RestoreToCrossRegionInstance
		- RestoreToNewInstanceFromUserTos

- In some interfaces, when used as a request parameter, the value range of this parameter depends on the storage type of the original instance. Specific rules are as follows:
	- If the original instance storage type is `LocalSSD` or `CloudESSD_FlexPL`, changing the storage type is not supported.
	- If the original instance storage type is `CloudESSD_PL0`, you can set it to `CloudESSD_PL0` or `CloudESSD_FlexPL`.
	The relevant interfaces are:
		- RebuildDBInstance
		- RestoreToNewInstance
		- ModifyDBNodeSpec

SubnetId.description_en:
Subnet ID

If not set, uses the same subnet as the blue instance.

AutoAddNewNodes.description_en:
When the terminal type is read-write or read-only, you can set whether new nodes join automatically. Options:

- `true`: Join automatically
- `false`: Do not join automatically (default)

ConnectAllSlaveNodes.description_en: Is the read-only terminal in a multi-node setup associated with all slave nodes?

ConnectionMode.description_en:
Connection terminal type. Values:
- `Proxy`: Proxy terminal (default)
- `Direct`: Direct terminal

- You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/describedbinstancedetail) API to check whether the database proxy feature is enabled for the instance.
	- If the database proxy feature is enabled, you can set the value to `Proxy` or `Direct`.
	- If the database proxy feature is disabled, you can only set the value to `Direct`.
- Changing the connection terminal type is not supported for multi-node instances.

ConnectionPoolType.description_en:
Connection pool type for proxy endpoints. Values:
- `Transaction`: Transaction-level connection pool. Default value.
- `Direct`: Direct connection mode.

- This feature is not supported for single-node instances.
- When the ConnectionMode parameter is set to Proxy, this parameter is required. If set to Direct, this parameter is invalid.

CustomRouteStrategy.description_en: SQL forwarding rules for the connection terminal.

Description.description_en: Notes
Description.example_en: This is a note about connecting the terminal.

EnableConnectionPersistent.description_en:
Enable connection keep-alive for proxy endpoints. Values:
- `true`: Yes.
- `false`: No.

When the `ConnectionMode` parameter is set to `Proxy`, this parameter is required. If set to `Direct`, this parameter is invalid.

EndpointName.description_en:
Instance connection terminal name

- Cannot start with a number or hyphen (-)
- Only Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_) and hyphens (-) are allowed
- Length must be between 1 and 64 characters

ExplicitTransSplit.description_en: Enable explicit transaction separation: "true" | "false". For operations only, not visible to customers for now

IdleConnectionReclaim.description_en:
Enable idle connection recycling for the proxy terminal. Values:
- `true`: Yes
- `false`: No (default)
When the ConnectionMode parameter is set to Proxy, this parameter is required. If set to Direct, this parameter is invalid.

ImplicitTransSplit.description_en:
Enable transaction separation. Values:
- `true`: Yes.
- `false`: No. Default value.

When the `ConnectionMode` parameter is set to `Proxy`, this parameter is required. If set to `Direct`, this parameter is invalid.

MasterNodeRouting.description_en:
Enable main node routing. Values:
- `true`: Yes
- `false`: No (default)

When the `ConnectionMode` parameter is set to `Proxy`, this parameter is required. If set to `Direct`, this parameter is invalid.

MasterProtectorTimeout.description_en:
Overload protection timeout. Value range: integer between 60 and 7200. Default value: 60. Unit: seconds.

When the `ConnectionMode` parameter is set to `Proxy`, this parameter is required. If set to `Direct`, this parameter is invalid.

MultiStatementsMode.description_en:
Multi-Statements mode for the proxy terminal. Values:
- `Strict`: Strict mode (default)
- `Loose`: Loose mode

- This feature is not supported for single-node instances.
- When the `ConnectionMode` parameter is set to `Proxy`, this parameter is required. If set to `Direct`, this parameter is invalid.

Nodes.description_en:
List of node IDs for configuring connection endpoints
Required when EndpointType is Custom

- To add the primary node to the endpoint, do not enter the primary node's ID; just enter Primary
- Separate multiple node IDs with English commas (,)

OverloadProtection.description_en:
Enable overload protection. Values:
- `true`: Yes. Default value.
- `false`: No.

When the `ConnectionMode` parameter is set to `Proxy`, this parameter is required. If set to `Direct`, this parameter is invalid.

ReadOnlyNodeDistributionType.description_en:
Read weight allocation mode. This parameter is required when read/write splitting is enabled (`true`). When used as a request parameter in the CreateDBEndpoint and ModifyDBEndpoint APIs, the value range is:
- `LoadSchedule`: Load scheduling.
- `RoundRobinCustom`: Custom weight round-robin scheduling.
- `RoundRobinAuto`: Automatic weight round-robin scheduling.

When used as a response parameter in the DescribeDBInstanceDetail API, the value range is:
- `Default`: Automatic allocation based on specification weight.
- `Custom`: Custom weight allocation.
- `RoundRobin`: Round-robin scheduling.
- `LoadSchedule`: Load scheduling.
- `RoundRobinCustom`: Custom weight round-robin scheduling.
- `RoundRobinAuto`: Automatic weight round-robin scheduling.

- Multi-node instances only support `RoundRobinAuto`.
- This feature is not supported for single-node instances.
- When the `ConnectionMode` parameter is set to `Proxy`, this parameter is required. If set to `Direct`, this parameter is invalid.

ReadOnlyNodeMaxDelayTime.description_en:
Read-only node latency threshold. Value range: 1–3600. Default: 30. Unit: seconds.
When the `ConnectionMode` parameter is set to `Proxy`, this parameter is required. If set to `Direct`, this parameter is invalid.

ReadOnlyNodeWeight.description_en:
Custom read weight allocation policy.
When the `ConnectionMode` parameter is set to `Proxy`, this parameter is required. If set to `Direct`, this parameter is invalid.

ReadWriteMode.description_en:
Read/write mode for the connection terminal. Options:

- `ReadWrite`: Read and write
- `ReadOnly`: Read only

When used as a request parameter, the default value is `ReadWrite`.

ReadWriteSpliting.description_en:
Enable read/write splitting. Values:
- `true`: Yes (default)
- `false`: No
When the ConnectionMode parameter is set to Proxy, this parameter is required. If set to Direct, this parameter is invalid.

EipId.description_cn: EIP ID. Use [DescribeEipAddressAttributes](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/eip/DescribeEipAddresses) to query the basic information of the EIP.
EipId.description_en: EIP ID. Use [DescribeEipAddressAttributes](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/eip/DescribeEipAddresses) to query the basic information of the EIP.

EndpointId.description_cn: Instance Connection Terminal ID
EndpointId.description_en: Instance Connection Terminal ID

AllowListIds.description_en: Whitelist ID. To bind multiple whitelists, separate each whitelist ID with an English comma (,). You can bind up to 100 whitelists to a single instance.

AutoUpgradeMinorVersion.description_en:
Kernel minor version upgrade policy. Options:
- `Auto`: Automatic upgrade. When a new kernel minor version is released, the instance will automatically upgrade to the latest kernel minor version during the configured [maintenance window](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/setting_a_maintenance_period?lang=zh).
- `Manual`: Manual upgrade. When a new kernel minor version is released, you need to manually upgrade the instance to the latest kernel minor version in the console. For details, see [Manually upgrade kernel minor version](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/upgrading_instance_kernel_minor_version?lang=zh).
If the kernel minor version of the instance exceeds the maintenance cycle, the system will temporarily ignore the configured upgrade policy and automatically upgrade the kernel minor version for the instance.

DBEngineVersion.description_en:
Compatible versions. Options:
- `MySQL_5_7`: MySQL 5.7 version
- `MySQL_8_0`: MySQL 8.0 version
- `MySQL 8.4`: MySQL 8.4 version

DBTimeZone.description_en:
Time zone

Default is the time zone of the region

Whether to enable deletion protection for the instance

Enable native replication

Database engine type
Values:
- `InnoDB`: InnoDB engine
- `RocksDB`: RocksDB engine

When used as a request parameter, the default value is `InnoDB`.

InstanceName.description_en:
Instance name. Naming rules for instance names:

- Cannot start with a number or hyphen
- Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens
- Must be 1–128 characters long

- If you do not specify an instance name, the instance name will be the same as the instance ID
- Cloud Database MySQL Edition supports creating up to 50 instances at once. When creating instances in batch:
    - If you do not specify an instance name, each instance will use its instance ID as the instance name
    - If you specify an instance name, a sequence number will be added automatically. For example, if you set the instance name to 'Test Instance' and create 3 instances in batch, their names will be 'Test Instance-1', 'Test Instance-2', and 'Test Instance-3'
    - You can use a specific syntax to assign ordered instance names: `name_prefix[begin_number,bits]name_suffix`. For example, if you set the instance name to 'Prefix[0,2]Suffix' and create 3 instances in batch, their names will be 'Prefix00Suffix', 'Prefix01Suffix', and 'Prefix02Suffix'. For more details, see [Ordered Instance Name Rules](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/Batch_setting_ordered_instance_names)

InstanceTags.description_en:
Instance Tags
- You can assign up to 50 tags to each MySQL instance
- You can add up to 20 tags in a single operation

InstanceType.description_en:
Instance type for the green instance. Options:
- `DoubleNode`: Double-node type
- `MultiNode`: Multi-node type
- `SingleNode`: Single-node type

- If the blue instance type is single-node, you can select single-node or double-node type for the green instance.
- If the blue instance type is double-node, you can select double-node or multi-node type for the green instance.
- If the blue instance type is multi-node, you can only select multi-node type for the green instance.

InternalAccountPassword.description_en: @sdk_hide_next_line For sharding only; used to specify the password for internal accounts byte_rds_admin/byte_rds_proxy

LowerCaseTableNames.description_en:
Table name case sensitivity. Default value: 1. Case is ignored by the backend

Value options:

- 0: Table names are stored as entered and are case-sensitive
- 1: Table names are stored in lowercase and are case-insensitive

MaintenanceWindow.description_en: Specify the maintenance window when creating an instance. This field is optional; if not set, the default is 18:00Z–21:59Z UTC (02:00–05:59 Beijing time) every day of the week.

Port.description_en:
Default terminal's private network port. Port number range: 1000–65534, default value: 3306
When you create a new connection terminal or enable a new address, the default terminal's private network port is used and configured in real time as the default port

PrivateIpAddress.description_en:
The IP address of the default terminal of the specified instance in the specified private network and subnet.
If not set, the default terminal of the instance will automatically be assigned an IP address in the specified private network and subnet.

ProjectName.description_en: Project to which the instance belongs. To specify a project during creation, make sure the project already exists. You can view the project list by calling the [ListProjects](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6649/1131880) API, or create a new project by calling the [CreateProject](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/6649/1131879) API.

ProxyNodeCustom.description_en:
Instance database proxy configuration
- This field is required only when InstanceType is set to `MultiNode`.
- This field does not apply when InstanceType is set to `DoubleNode` or `SingleNode`.

ServiceArea.description_en: Optional Sales Area, Public Service Area

StorageType.description_en:
Instance storage type. Valid values:
- `LocalSSD`: local disk.
- `CloudESSD_FlexPL`: FlexPL cloud disk.
- `CloudESSD_PL0`: PL0 cloud disk.
- If you need to set the StorageSpace parameter, the StorageType parameter is required.
- When InstanceType is set to `SingleNode`, StorageType can only be `CloudESSD_FlexPL` or `CloudESSD_PL0`.
- The valid values for this parameter vary by API. Rules are as follows:
	- When used as a request parameter in the following APIs, StorageType can only be `LocalSSD`:
		- RestoreToCrossRegionInstance.
		- RestoreToNewInstanceFromUserTos.

- In some APIs, the valid values for this parameter depend on the storage type of the original instance. Rules are as follows:
	- If the original instance storage type is `LocalSSD` or `CloudESSD_FlexPL`, changing the storage type is not supported.
	- If the original instance storage type is `CloudESSD_PL0`, you can set it to `CloudESSD_PL0` or `CloudESSD_FlexPL`.
	The relevant APIs are:
		- RebuildDBInstance.
		- RestoreToNewInstance.
		- ModifyDBNodeSpec.

SubnetId.description_en: Subnet ID. Call [DescribeSubnets](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSubnets) and specify VpcId and ZoneId (the availability zone of the primary or standby node) to query available subnets

SuperAccountName.description_en:
High-privilege account name. If you do not provide this parameter, a high-privilege account will not be created by default.
Naming rules for high-privilege account names: - Account name must be 2–32 characters long - Must start with a letter and end with a letter or number - Can contain letters, numbers, underscores (_), or hyphens (-) - Certain reserved words cannot be used. For a list of disabled reserved words, see [Disabled Words List](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/list_of_forbidden_keywords) - Account name must be unique within the instance

SuperAccountPassword.description_en:
Password for the high-privilege account. Password rules:

- Length: 8–32 characters
- Must include at least three of the following: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, special characters
- Allowed special characters: `!#$%&()*+,-.=?@^_|/`

VpcId.description_en:
Private network (VPC) ID. You can use [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) to query.
Shared VPCs are not supported.

WithIopsLimit.description_en: @sdk_hide_next_line Should IOPS limit be enabled for disaster recovery and cross-region instances?

WithoutProxyPLB.description_en: @sdk_hide_next_line Not only removes proxy for sharding, but also does not request PLB or terminal

ZoneId.description_en:
Availability zone ID.
We recommend setting the availability zone for each node of the instance using the ZoneId parameter in NodeInfoObject.

DryRun.description_en: @sdk_hide_next_line Indicates whether it is DryRun. If true, it only generates a pre-scheduling plan and does not execute

EstimateOnly.description_en:
Initiate configuration change assessment. Values:
- `true`: Yes
- `false`: No (default)

If initiated, the system assesses the configuration change based on the specifications determined by other fields, but does not actually perform the change. After assessment, the EstimationResult parameter is returned to indicate the impact of the change.

RequestSource.description_en:
Request Source. Values:
- `EventType_Web`: From Web
- `EventType_OpenAPI`: From Open API

SpecifiedSwitchEndTime.description_en:
End time of the time window (UTC) when executing within a specified period. Format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ`.

- This parameter is required when SwitchType is set to `SpecifiedTime`.
- The minimum duration for the specified time window is one hour and fifty-nine minutes.
- Cross-day time windows are not supported; the task's start and end times must be within the same calendar day.

SpecifiedSwitchStartTime.description_en:
Start time of the time window (UTC) when executing within a specified period. Format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ`.

- This parameter is required when SwitchType is set to `SpecifiedTime`.
- The task start time cannot be later than the 7th day after the current date.

SwitchType.description_en:
Execution time. Valid values:

- `Immediate`: Switch immediately (default)
- `MaintainTime`: Switch during the maintenance window
- `SpecifiedTime`: Switch within the specified time window

- You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/describedbinstancedetail) API to query the maintenance window of the instance.
- If set to `SpecifiedTime`, you must specify the start and end times in the SpecifiedSwitchStartTime and SpecifiedSwitchEndTime parameters.

Database name: naming rules

- Must be unique
- Length: 2–64 characters

AutoUpgradeMinorVersion.description_en:

- `Manual`: Manual upgrade. When a new kernel minor version is released, you need to manually upgrade to the latest kernel minor version in the console. For details, see [Manually upgrade instance kernel minor version](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/upgrading_instance_kernel_minor_version?lang=zh).
If the kernel minor version of the instance exceeds the maintenance cycle, the system will temporarily ignore the configured upgrade policy and automatically upgrade the kernel minor version for the instance.

DBNodeIds.description_cn:
List of node IDs to be deleted.
- The nodes specified in DBNodeIds must belong to the instance specified in InstanceId.
- For dual-node instances, primary and standby nodes cannot be deleted; you can select up to 10 read-only nodes for deletion.
- For multi-node instances, the primary node cannot be deleted. Standby nodes must have at least 1 and at most 8. It is recommended to reserve an independent standby node that does not handle any workloads, so it can be switched to the primary node when necessary. If no independent standby node is set and all standby nodes experience high primary-standby latency, resulting in a failed primary node switch, BytePlus MySQL is not responsible for any resulting issues.

- The nodes specified in DBNodeIds must belong to the instance specified in InstanceId.
