- For multi-node instances, the primary node cannot be deleted. Standby nodes must have at least 1 and at most 8. It is recommended to reserve an independent standby node that does not handle any workloads, so it can be switched to the primary node when necessary. If no independent standby node is set and all standby nodes experience high primary-standby latency, resulting in a failed primary node switch, BytePlus MySQL is not responsible for any resulting issues.

SpecifiedSwitchEndTime.description_cn:
When executing during a specified time window, the end time of the window (UTC time). Format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ`.

- When SwitchType is set to `SpecifiedTime`, this parameter is required.
- The minimum duration for the specified time window is one hour and fifty-nine minutes.
- Cross-day time windows are not supported; the start and end times must be within the same day (not exceeding 24 hours apart).
SpecifiedSwitchEndTime.description_en:

- Cross-day time windows are not supported; the start and end times must be within the same day (not exceeding 24 hours apart).

SpecifiedSwitchStartTime.description_cn:

- The task start time must be within 7 days from the current date.
SpecifiedSwitchStartTime.description_en:

SwitchType.description_cn:

- If the value is `SpecifiedTime`, you must set the start and end times in the SpecifiedSwitchStartTime and SpecifiedSwitchEndTime parameters.

StorageType.description_cn:
Instance storage type. Value range:
- `LocalSSD`: Local disk
- `CloudESSD_FlexPL`: FlexPL cloud disk
- `CloudESSD_PL0`: PL0 cloud disk
- If you need to set the StorageSpace parameter, the StorageType parameter is required
- When InstanceType is set to `SingleNode`, StorageType can only be `CloudESSD_FlexPL` or `CloudESSD_PL0`
- The value range of this parameter varies by API. The specific rules are as follows:
	- When used as a request parameter in the following APIs, StorageType can only be `LocalSSD`:
		- RestoreToCrossRegionInstance
		- RestoreToNewInstanceFromUserTos

- When used as a request parameter in some APIs, the value range of this parameter depends on the storage type of the original instance. The specific rules are as follows:
	- If the original instance storage type is `LocalSSD` or `CloudESSD_FlexPL`, changing the storage type is not supported
	- If the original instance storage type is `CloudESSD_PL0`, the value can be `CloudESSD_PL0` or `CloudESSD_FlexPL`
	The related APIs are:
		- RebuildDBInstance
		- RestoreToNewInstance
		- ModifyDBNodeSpec

SpecifiedSwitchEndTime.description_en:

- Cross-day time periods are not supported; the task's start and end times must not exceed 24 hours.

SpecifiedSwitchStartTime.description_en:

- `Immediate`: Switch immediately (default)
- `MaintainTime`: Switch during the maintenance window
- `SpecifiedTime`: Switch within the specified time period

- You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/describedbinstancedetail) API to query the maintenance window for the instance.
- If `SpecifiedTime` is selected, you must set the start and end times in the `SpecifiedSwitchStartTime` and `SpecifiedSwitchEndTime` parameters.

AllowList.description_en:
IP addresses outside the security group that need to be added to the whitelist. You can enter individual IP addresses or IP ranges in CIDR format.

- Each whitelist supports up to 300 IP addresses or CIDR-format IP ranges
- Duplicate addresses are not allowed; separate multiple addresses with English commas (,)
- Entering `0.0.0.0/0` allows access from all addresses
- Entering `127.0.0.1` blocks access from all addresses
- Entering both `0.0.0.0/0` and `127.0.0.1` allows access from all addresses
- Entering CIDR `192.168.1.0/24` allows access from all IP addresses in that subnet
- Entering `192.168.1.1` allows access only from that IP address
- This field cannot be used together with UserAllowList

AllowListCategory.description_en:
Whitelist category. Possible values:

- `Ordinary`: Ordinary whitelist
- `Default`: Default whitelist

When used as a request parameter, the default value is `Ordinary`

AllowListDesc.description_en: Remark information for the whitelist cannot exceed 200 characters

AllowListId.description_en:
Allowlist ID

You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/describeallowlists1) API to query all allowlist lists information in a specified region, including allowlist IDs

AllowListName.description_en:
Allowlist name

- To modify the IP address of an existing allowlist, enter the original allowlist name. You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/describeallowlists1) API to view all allowlist information in a specific region, including allowlist names.
- To change the allowlist name, enter a new name. The name must meet the following requirements:
  - Cannot start with a number or hyphen (-)
  - Can only contain letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)
  - Must be 1–32 characters long

ApplyInstanceNum.description_en:
Number of instances bound to the current whitelist.

- This parameter is required when modifying the AllowList or UserAllowList parameters.
- You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/describeallowlists1) API to query all whitelist information in a specified region, including the total number of instances bound to each whitelist.

IgnoreInstanceStatus.description_en:
Ignore instance status validation
- `true`: Yes
- `false`: No (default)

ModifyMode.description_en:
Modification mode. Available options:

- `Cover` (default): Replace the original whitelist with the IP addresses specified in the `AllowList` parameter.
- `Append`: Add the IP addresses entered in the `AllowList` parameter to the existing whitelist.
- `Delete`: Remove the IP addresses entered in the `AllowList` parameter from the existing whitelist. At least one IP address must be retained.

SecurityGroupIds.description_en:

- You can add up to 10 security groups to a single whitelist at a time.
- This field cannot be used together with SecurityGroupBindInfos.

UpdateSecurityGroup.description_en:
Update the security group bound to the allowlist

- `true`: Update
- `false`: Do not update (default)

This field is only effective if the allowlist is already bound to a security group. You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/describeallowlists1) API to check whether the allowlist is bound to a security group.

UserAllowList.description_en:

This field and AllowList cannot be used at the same time

- `false`: No

- `false`: Not enabled

BinlogLimitCount.description_en: Local Binlog retention count (6–1000, unit: count). Logs exceeding the retention count are deleted automatically

BinlogLocalRetentionHour.description_en: Local Binlog retention period. Valid range: 0–168 hours. Logs older than the retention period are deleted automatically. If set to 0, local logs are not deleted automatically.

BinlogSpaceLimitEnable.description_en:
Enable automatic binlog cleanup when storage usage is too high. When the total storage usage of the instance exceeds 80% or the remaining space is less than 5 GiB, the system will automatically start cleaning up the earliest local binlog until the total storage usage drops below 80% and the remaining space is greater than 5 GiB.

- `true`: Enable
- `false`: Disable

BinlogStoragePercentage.description_en:
Maximum storage usage rate can be set from 20% to 50%. When usage exceeds the set limit, the system automatically deletes the oldest Binlog files until usage drops below the threshold.

Local Binlog storage usage rate = Local Binlog size / Total available (purchased) instance storage size

DataBackupAllRetention.description_en:

- `false`: No

- `false`: No

This feature is not supported for cloud disk instances yet

DataBackupRetentionDay.description_en:
Backup file retention duration. The range of backup retention days varies by storage type:

- For local disk instances: selectable range is 7–3650 days, default is 7 days.

- For cloud disk instances: currently only 7 days are supported.

DataFullBackupPeriods.description_en:
Full backup schedule. It is recommended to select at least 2 days each week for full backups. Separate multiple values with commas (,). Available values:

- `Monday`: Monday
- `Tuesday`: Tuesday
- `Wednesday`: Wednesday
- `Thursday`: Thursday
- `Friday`: Friday
- `Saturday`: Saturday
- `Sunday`: Sunday

DataFullBackupStartUTCHour.description_en:
Start time of the full backup window (UTC). The window lasts 1 hour.

Both DataFullBackupStartUTCHour and DataFullBackupTime can specify the full backup window for an instance. DataFullBackupStartUTCHour has higher priority; if both fields are returned, DataFullBackupStartUTCHour takes precedence.

DataFullBackupTime.description_en:
Backup task time window. The time window is 1 hour. Format: `HH:mmZ-HH:mmZ` (UTC time).

- Both DataFullBackupStartUTCHour and DataFullBackupTime can be used to specify the full backup time window for the instance. DataFullBackupStartUTCHour has higher priority. If both fields are returned, DataFullBackupStartUTCHour takes precedence.
- To set a time window starting at 15:00 (UTC), set the end time to 15:59.

DataIncrBackupPeriods.description_en:
Incremental backup schedule. Separate multiple values with commas (,). Valid values:

- `Monday`: Monday
- `Tuesday`: Tuesday
- `Wednesday`: Wednesday
- `Thursday`: Thursday
- `Friday`: Friday
- `Saturday`: Saturday
- `Sunday`: Sunday

The incremental backup schedule must not conflict with the full backup schedule.

DataKeepDaysAfterReleased.description_en: Number of days backups are retained when the instance is released. Supports integer values from 7 to 3650; default is 7

DataKeepPolicyAfterReleased.description_en:
Backup retention policy after instance release. Options:
- `Last`: Keep the most recent backup (default)
- `All`: Keep all backups for the instance
- `None`: Do not keep any backups

HighFrequencySnapshotBackupSecondPeriod.description_en:

IncrBackupHourPeriod.description_en:

- `2`: Perform an incremental backup every 2 hours

- `6`: Perform an incremental backup every 6 hours
- `12`: Perform an incremental backup every 12 hours

- When `HourlyIncrBackupEnable` is set to `true`, `IncrBackupHourPeriod` is required

The backup process blocks DDL. If the blocking time exceeds the specified duration, the backup will automatically stop.

LogBackupRetentionDay.description_en:

Host.description_cn:
Specify the IP address that the account uses to access the database. The default value is `%`.

- If Host is set to `%`, the account can access the database from any IP address
- You can use wildcards to define IP address ranges. For example, if Host is set to `192.10.10.%`, the account can access the database from IP addresses between `192.10.10.0` and `192.10.10.255`
- The specified Host must be added to the whitelist bound to the instance; otherwise, the account cannot access the instance. You can call the [ModifyAllowList](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_MySQL/modifyallowlist1) API to add the Host to the whitelist

If you create a high-privilege account, the host IP can only be set to `%`. That is, when AccountType is set to `Super`, Host must be `%`.

AutoAddNewNodes.description_en:
When the endpoint type is read/write or read-only, you can set whether new nodes are automatically added. Values:

- `true`: Auto add.
- `false`: Do not auto add (default).

- The auto-add new node feature for multi-node instance connection endpoints cannot be adjusted. The auto-add new node feature is enabled by default for default and read-only endpoints, and disabled by default for write endpoints.
- This feature is not supported for single-node instances.

ConnectAllSlaveNodes.description_en:
Whether to associate all standby nodes
Values:
- `true`: Yes (default)
- `false`: No

- This setting is only supported for read-only endpoints of multi-node instances
- You can only disable this feature if the instance has two or more standby nodes

ConnectionMode.description_en:
Connection endpoint type. Available values:
- `Proxy`: Proxy endpoint
- `Direct`: Direct endpoint

- If the database proxy feature is enabled for the instance, you can select either `Proxy` or `Direct`.
- If the database proxy feature is not enabled, only `Direct` is available.

Nodes.description_en:
Node list for configuring connection terminals

- For the primary node, you do not need to provide a node ID. Use the string 'Primary'.
- **Dual-node instance**
    - In read-write mode, a proxy terminal can be associated with only the primary node, or with the primary node and up to 10 read-only nodes. In read-only mode, it can only be associated with read-only nodes, with a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 10 read-only nodes.
    - In read-write mode, a direct terminal can only be associated with the primary node. In read-only mode, it can only be associated with 1 read-only node.
- **Multi-node instance**
    - The default terminal is associated with all nodes in the instance. The write terminal is associated only with the primary node. You cannot adjust the associated nodes for either the default terminal or the write terminal.
    - By default, the read-only terminal is associated with all standby nodes in the instance. You can associate a minimum of 1 and a maximum of all standby nodes. To adjust the associated nodes for a read-only terminal in a multi-node instance, you must disable the 'Associate All Standby Nodes' feature. When a standby node is promoted to primary, it will automatically be disassociated from the read-only terminal.
    - If a standby node associated with a read-only terminal is promoted to primary, the number of standby nodes associated with the read-only terminal will decrease by one. To maintain the original number of standby nodes, you need to manually add a new standby node. It is recommended to configure a sufficient number of standby nodes for terminals to handle business traffic.
- To ensure high availability in read-only mode, it is recommended to associate at least two standby nodes (for multi-node instances) or two read-only nodes (for dual-node instances) with each read-only terminal.

OverloadProtection.description_en:
Enable overload protection. Values:
- `true`: Enable. Default value.
- `false`: Disable.

- Only proxy endpoints support overload protection.
- Overload protection is effective only when read/write splitting is enabled on the connection endpoint and the primary node is not the only node for the current connection endpoint.
- This feature is not supported for single-node instances.

ReadOnlyNodeDistributionType.description_en:
Read weight allocation mode. This parameter is required when read/write splitting is enabled (`true`). For request parameters in the CreateDBEndpoint and ModifyDBEndpoint APIs, the available values are:
- `LoadSchedule`: Load scheduling.
- `RoundRobinCustom`: Custom weight round-robin scheduling.
- `RoundRobinAuto`: Auto-assigned weight round-robin scheduling.

For response parameters in the DescribeDBInstanceDetail API, the available values are:
- `Default`: Auto-assign by specification weight.
- `Custom`: Custom weight assignment.
- `RoundRobin`: Round-robin scheduling.
- `LoadSchedule`: Load scheduling.
- `RoundRobinCustom`: Custom weight round-robin scheduling.
- `RoundRobinAuto`: Auto-assigned weight round-robin scheduling.

- Multi-node instances only support `RoundRobinAuto`.
- This feature is not supported for single-node instances.
- When the `ConnectionMode` parameter is set to `Proxy`, this parameter is required; when set to `Direct`, this parameter is invalid.

ReadOnlyNodeMaxDelayTime.description_en:
Maximum latency threshold for read-only nodes. If a read-only node's latency exceeds this value, read traffic will not be routed to that node. Valid range: 1–3600 seconds. Default: 30 seconds.

For read/write terminals, you can set this parameter after enabling read/write splitting.

ReadOnlyNodeWeight.description_en:
Customize read weight distribution by assigning read request weights to the primary node and read-only nodes. Increase weights in increments of 100, up to a maximum of 10,000. When ReadOnlyNodeDistributionType is set to `Custom`, you must provide this parameter.

- For the primary node, set NodeType to Primary; for read-only nodes, provide the NodeID.
- You cannot set all weights to 0.

- `false`: Disable read/write splitting (default)

AllowList.description_en:
IP addresses included in the whitelist. Separate multiple IP addresses with commas (,). Do not repeat IP addresses. Supports the following two formats:

- IP address format. For example: `10.23.12.24`
- CIDR IP range format. For example: `10.23.12.0/24` (Classless Inter-Domain Routing; 24 indicates the prefix length, range is 1–32)

- Each whitelist can contain up to 300 IP addresses or IP ranges. If you have many IPs, it is recommended to merge them into ranges, such as 10.23.12.0/24
- It is forbidden to add IP addresses in the format `x.x.x.x/0` except for `0.0.0.0/0`
- No default value. If this parameter is not set, the existing whitelist IPs will not be modified

AllowListCategory.description_en:

AllowListName.description_en:
The allowlist name can be the same as the original or different. If different, the allowlist will be renamed using the value of the AllowListName field. Naming rules for allowlist names:

- Must be unique within the current region
- Must start with a Chinese character, letter, or underscore (_)
- Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)
- Length must be 1 to 128 characters

ModifyMode.description_en:
Whitelist modification modes. Options:

- `Cover`: Overwrite—replace the original whitelist with the IP addresses specified in the AllowList field. Default option
- `Append`: Add—add the IP addresses from the AllowList field to the existing whitelist
- `Delete`: Remove—delete the IP addresses specified in the AllowList field from the existing whitelist. At least one IP address must be retained

If the whitelist is bound to a security group, or you need to bind a security group when modifying the whitelist, ModifyMode can only be set to `Cover`.

EstimateOnly.description_en:
Whether to initiate a configuration change assessment. Options:
- `true`: Yes
- `false`: No (default)

If initiated, the assessment is performed based on the specifications determined by other fields, but no actual configuration change is executed. After initiating the assessment, the EstimationResult parameter is returned, indicating the impact of the configuration change.

ModifyType.description_en:
Configuration change mode. Available values:

- `Usually`: Regular configuration change (immediate change, default)
- `Temporary`: Flexible upgrade (temporary upgrade)

The `Temporary` option is only available for instances billed annually or monthly. You can check the billing type by calling the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_PG/describedbinstancedetail) API.

NodeInfo.description_en:
Instance specification configuration
Primary node: 1 only
Secondary node: 1 only
Read-Only nodes: Optional, 0–10

- You must select at least one of this parameter or `StorageSpace`; both can be modified at the same time
- Only include nodes involved in the configuration change in this parameter

NodeSpec.description_en: Instance specification code required for historical compatibility

RollbackTime.description_en:
Restore time. The time format is `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.sssZ` (UTC)

- This parameter is required when ModifyType is set to `Temporary`
- This parameter only takes effect when ModifyType is set to `Temporary`
- The difference between the restore time and the time you call the API must not exceed 2 minutes. The actual restore time is based on the time you call the API
- You can extend the temporary upgrade period multiple times, but the total duration cannot exceed 30 days (counted from the time of the first temporary upgrade)
- You can initiate temporary upgrades multiple times, but you cannot shorten the temporary upgrade period. If the instance is already in a temporary upgrade period:
    - The new restore time cannot be earlier than the effective restore time
    - If there are less than five days remaining before the annual/monthly subscription instance expires, you cannot initiate another temporary upgrade

SpecifiedSwitchEndTime.description_en:
End time for executing within the specified time period. The time format is `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ`.
- When SwitchType is set to `SpecifiedTime`, this parameter is required.
- The minimum duration for the specified time period is one hour and fifty-nine minutes.

SpecifiedSwitchStartTime.description_en: Start time for executing within the specified time period. The time format is `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ`.

StorageSpace.description_en:
Instance storage space. Range: [20, 3000] GB, in increments of 10 GB

- You must specify either this parameter or `NodeInfo`. You can modify both parameters at the same time

- When ModifyType is set to `Temporary`, this parameter cannot be configured

StorageType.description_en:
Instance storage type. Fixed value: `LocalSSD` (local SSD disk).

- You must specify at least one of this parameter or `NodeInfo`; both can be modified at the same time.
- This parameter cannot be set when ModifyType is `Temporary`.

SwitchType.description_en:
Execution time options:

- `Immediate`: Switch immediately (default)
- `MaintainTime`: Switch during the maintenance window
- `SpecifiedTime`: Switch within the specified time period

- You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/RDS_for_PG/describedbinstancedetail) API to query the maintenance window for the instance.
- If set to `SpecifiedTime`, you must specify the start and end times in the SpecifiedSwitchStartTime and SpecifiedSwitchEndTime parameters.

AllowList.description_cn:

* The `AllowList` and `SecurityGroupBindInfos` parameters cannot both be empty
* Duplicate addresses are not allowed; separate multiple addresses with an English comma (,)
* Setting `0.0.0.0/0` allows access from all addresses; setting `127.0.0.1` blocks access from all addresses; setting both `0.0.0.0/0` and `127.0.0.1` allows access from all addresses

SecurityGroupBindInfos.BindMode.description_cn:
Security group association mode. The available values are:

* `IngressDirectionIp`: Ingress direction IP. Allows IPs involved in TCP and ALL protocols in the source address of the security group's ingress direction to access the database. If the source address is configured as a security group, it will be ignored.
* `AssociateEcsIp`: Associate ECS IP. Allows cloud servers within the security group to access the database. Currently, only IP information from the primary network interface is supported.

For more details about security group association modes, see [Create allowlist](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/create-allowlist)

* Each allowlist supports up to 300 IP addresses or IP ranges. If the IP addresses or ranges involved in the associated security groups exceed this limit, the association will fail. You can adjust the IPs in the security group and try again. TargetInstanceName.description_cn:
Set the name of the target instance (i.e., the green instance). The name must meet the following requirements:

* Cannot start with a number or hyphen (-)
* Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)
* Length must be 1–128 characters

* If you do not set a name for the green instance, the default name will be `<blue instance name>-green-<six-digit random code>`.
   For example, if the blue instance name is `redistest`, then when creating a green instance for this instance, the default name may be `redistest-green-b4bf10`.
* The instance name for Redis cache database cannot exceed 128 characters, and `-green-<six-digit random code>` will occupy a fixed 13 characters. Therefore, the `<blue instance name>` part in the green instance name can retain up to the first 115 characters of the blue name to fit the total length limit.

RoleName.description_cn:
Account roles. The following default roles are supported:

* `Administrator`: Allows all supported commands on all Keys in the Redis instance
* `ReadWrite`: Allows all commands except those in the `admin` category on all Keys
* `ReadOnly`: Allows all commands in the `read` category on all Keys
* `NotDangerous`: Allows all commands except those in the `dangerous` category on all Keys
* `NotWrite`: Allows all commands except those in the `write` category on all Keys

* For details on the specific commands supported by each role's ACL rules, see [ACL Syntax](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/create-role#acl-%E8%AF%AD%E6%B3%95).
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceAclCategories](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstanceaclcategories) API to query the command categories supported by the target Redis instance, and call the [DescribeDBInstanceAclCommands](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstanceaclcommands) API to query the details of commands supported under a specified command category.

* You can call the [DescribeAllowLists](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describeallowlists) API to query all IP allowlist information under the specified region for the current account, including allowlist IDs.
* Each instance supports binding up to 100 allowlists, and you can batch bind up to 100 allowlists at a time.
* Each instance supports binding up to 1000 IP addresses or IP address ranges in CIDR format.

NodeNumber.description_cn:
Number of nodes per shard. Value range: 1–6
* By default, each account can create up to 4 nodes of the 256 MiB specification (that is, `ShardCapacity` set to `256`) in each region. To adjust the purchase quota for 256 MiB nodes (maximum 10), see [Account Quota](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/quota-and-limit#%E8%B4%A6%E5%8F%B7%E9%85%8D%E9%A2%9D)
* When the value is `1`, a single-node instance is created; when greater than `1`, a master-replica instance is created. Single-node and master-replica instances support different features. For details on the differences, see [Feature Differences](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/feature-faq#%E4%B8%BB%E5%A4%87%E5%AE%9E%E4%BE%8B%E5%92%8C%E5%8D%95%E8%8A%82%E7%82%B9%E7%B1%BB%E5%9E%8B%E5%AE%9E%E4%BE%8B%E6%94%AF%E6%8C%81%E7%9A%84%E5%8A%9F%E8%83%BD%E7%89%B9%E6%80%A7%E6%9C%89%E4%BD%95%E5%B7%AE%E5%88%AB%EF%BC%9F)

ParameterGroupId.description_cn:
Parameter template to be applied to the new instance.
* Redis provides a default system parameter template for each database version, which includes all configurable parameters and their default values for that version. If this parameter is left blank, the system will select and apply the corresponding version's system parameter template based on your specified database version (`EngineVersion`) and whether the instance is single-node (`NodeNumber` is `1`).
* You can call the [DescribeParameterGroups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describeparametergroups) API to query basic information about all parameter templates under your account and region, including parameter template IDs.

Password.description_cn:
Set the password for the default database account. The password must meet the following requirements:

* Length: 8–64 characters
* Must include at least two of the following: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, or special characters
* Supports the following special characters:

```Plain Text
()`~!@#$%^&*-+=_|{}[];<>,.?
```

* If this parameter is left blank, no password will be set for the default account. In this case, the system will automatically generate a password for the default account to ensure instance security. No account can retrieve this random password, so you must reset the default account password via the [ModifyDBAccount](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/modifydbaccount) API before connecting to the instance.
* You can also set a new account and password as needed via the [CreateDBAccount](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/createdbaccount) API.
* To use passwordless access, you must first enable passwordless access via the [ModifyDBInstanceVpcAuthMode](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/modifydbinstancevpcauthmode) API.

SubnetId.description_cn:
Set the subnet ID for the instance.
* Subnets have availability zone attributes. You must select a subnet in the target VPC that is in the same availability zone as the instance.
* A subnet is an IP address block within a VPC. All cloud resources in the VPC must be deployed within a subnet. Subnets assign private IP addresses to cloud resources. You can call the [CreateSubnet](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/CreateSubnet) API to create a subnet.
* You can call the [DescribeSubnets](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSubnets) API to query all subnet list information in a specified availability zone, including subnet IDs.

Tags.Key.description_cn:
The tag key to be bound.
* Leaving this parameter empty means the new instance will not be bound to any tags. When you need to bind tags to an instance, the tag key (Key) is required, while the tag value (Value) is optional. If the tag value is not provided, the corresponding tag key will have an empty value.
* You can specify multiple tag key-value objects at once, separated by commas (,). Up to 20 tag key-value pairs can be specified at the same time.
* Each instance can be bound to up to 50 tags. Tag keys must comply with the configuration rules. For details, see [Tag Configuration Rules](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/associate-tag#%E6%A0%87%E7%AD%BE%E8%AE%BE%E7%BD%AE%E8%A7%84%E5%88%99).

SubnetId.description_en:
Set the subnet ID for the instance.
* Subnets have an availability zone attribute. You must select a subnet in the target VPC that is in the same availability zone as the instance.
* A subnet is an IP address block within a VPC. All cloud resources in the VPC must be deployed in a subnet. Subnets assign private IP addresses to cloud resources. You can call the [CreateSubnet](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/CreateSubnet) API to create a subnet.
* You can call the [DescribeSubnets](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSubnets) API to query the list of all subnets in a specified availability zone, including subnet IDs.

NodesToRemove.AZ.description_cn:
Configure the availability zone for node reduction.
The number of nodes to reduce (that is, the value of the `NodesNumberToDecrease` parameter) and the availability zone deployment scheme (that is, the value of the `MultiAZ` parameter) both affect how you fill in this parameter. Specifically:

* If the instance is deployed across multiple availability zones (that is, `MultiAZ` is set to `enabled`), **this parameter is required**, and **the number of availability zones provided must equal the number of nodes to reduce per shard** (that is, the value of `NodesNumberToDecrease`).

For example, if you need to reduce 2 nodes from each shard of a multi-availability zone instance, and these two nodes belong to availability zone A and B respectively, you can configure as follows:
```JavaScript
"NodesNumberToDecrease":2,
"NodesToRemove": [
    {
        "AZ": "cn-beijing-a"
    },
    {
        "AZ": "cn-beijing-b"
    }
]    
```

* If the instance is deployed in a single availability zone (that is, `MultiAZ` is set to `disabled`), you do not need to set this parameter. The availability zone for the nodes to reduce is the current availability zone of the instance.

* Each primary/standby instance must retain at least 2 nodes, and for instances deployed across multiple availability zones, the remaining nodes must be distributed across at least 2 different availability zones.
* You can call the [DescribeZones](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describezones) API to query availability zone information in the target region, including availability zone IDs.
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API to query details of a specified instance, including whether multi-availability zone deployment is enabled.

CreateBackup.description_en:
Create a final backup when deleting an instance. Possible values:

* `true` (default): Create a backup
* `false`: Do not create a backup

* This parameter applies only to master-replica node instances. Single-node instances do not support persistence or backup. When you delete a single-node instance, no backup is created by default. All data will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered. Please proceed with caution. For more details about single-node instances, see [Product Architecture](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/product-component-architecture#%E4%BA%A7%E5%93%81%E6%9E%B6%E6%9E%84).
* If you leave this parameter empty, a final backup will be created by default when deleting a master-replica instance to save all data before deletion. After the instance is deleted, you can call the [DescribeBackups](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describebackups) API to view all backup sets for the instance, including backups of deleted instances.

* `Cluster`: Enables sharded cluster (number of shards greater than 1)
* `Standard`: Does not enable sharded cluster (number of shards is 1)

TagFilters.Key.description_cn:
Tag key used for query filtering
* When you need to filter query results by tags, the tag key (Key) is required. The tag value (Value) is optional. If the tag value is not specified, there is no restriction on tag value, and all instances bound to the specified tag key will be searched.
* Up to 10 tag key-value pairs can be passed in a single query for filtering.
* Duplicate tag keys are allowed.

TagFilters.Value.description_cn:
Tag value corresponding to the tag key used for query filtering.
* If this parameter is left blank, no restriction is applied to tag values, and all instances bound to the specified tag key will be filtered.
* If an empty string is entered, instances with an empty tag value under the corresponding tag key will be filtered.

Context.description_cn:
The context of the Fatlog log query result, used when loading more Fatlog log records.
After calling the DescribeFatLogs API, you can determine whether there are remaining Fatlog log records to load based on the value of the returned parameter `ListOver`:

* If `ListOver` is `false`, there are still Fatlog log records matching the query conditions that have not been loaded. You can call the DescribeFatLogs API again and use the `Context` value returned in the previous API call to view the remaining Fatlog log records.
* If `ListOver` is `true`, all Fatlog log records matching the query conditions have been loaded.
Context.description_en:
The context of the Fatlog log query result, used when loading more Fatlog log records.

* If `ListOver` is `true`, all Fatlog log records matching the query conditions have been loaded.

* The total length of the `NodeIds` string must not exceed 1024 bytes. It is recommended to query no more than 8 nodes at a time.

You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstances) API to query basic information for all Redis instances in the target region, including the instance ID.

NodeIds.description_cn:
Node ID(s) required for slow log query
* If this parameter is left blank, slow log details for all nodes in the target instance are queried by default
* You can enter multiple node IDs separated by commas (,)
* To view all node IDs for the target Redis instance, call the [DescribeNodeIds](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describenodeids) API
* The total length of the NodeIds string must not exceed 1024 bytes; it is recommended to specify no more than 8 nodes

QueryStartTime.description_cn:
Query start time, format: `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (UTC)
If this parameter is left blank, the actual query start time defaults to three days before the current time.
For example, if the current time is August 1, 2022, 16:30:00, and `QueryStartTime` is not set, the actual query start time will be July 29, 2022, 16:30:00.

TagFilters.Key.description_cn:
Tag key for query filtering.
* When you need to filter query results by tags, the tag key (Key) is required. The tag value (Value) is optional. If you leave the tag value empty, there is no restriction on the tag value, and all instances bound to the specified tag key will be searched.
* Duplicate tag keys are allowed.
* You can specify up to 10 tags at a time for query filtering.

TagFilters.Value.description_cn:
Tag value corresponding to the tag key for query filtering.
* If this parameter is left empty, there is no restriction on the tag value, and all instances bound to the specified tag key will be filtered.
* If an empty string is entered, only instances where the tag value is empty under the corresponding tag key will be filtered.

NodeNumber.description_cn:

If you need to adjust the purchase quota for 256 MiB nodes (maximum 10), see [Account Quota](https://vsop-online.bytedance.net/doc/manage/detail/6293/6293/71560#%E8%B4%A6%E5%8F%B7%E9%85%8D%E9%A2%9D).

ShardCapacity.description_cn:
Memory capacity per shard, in MiB. The available values are as follows:

* If the instance does not enable sharded cluster (that is, `ShardedCluster` is set to `0`), the selectable memory capacity per shard is: 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 24576, 65536.
* If the instance enables sharded cluster (that is, `ShardedCluster` is set to `1`), the selectable memory capacity per shard is: 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384.

* If this parameter is left blank, the instance memory capacity will not be modified.
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API to query details of the specified instance, including whether sharding is enabled and the memory capacity of each shard.
* If you need to reduce shard capacity, ensure that the instance's current **used memory** does not exceed the new total memory capacity, where new total memory capacity = updated memory per shard x number of shards. For information on **used memory**, see [View Instance Information](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/view-instance).
* Each instance specification supports corresponding shard capacity and bandwidth. When you modify shard capacity, the bandwidth and specification will also be updated accordingly. For more details about Redis instance specifications, see [Product Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/product-specification).

ShardNumber.description_cn:
Number of shards in the instance. Value range: 2–256.
* This parameter is required only when sharded cluster is enabled (that is, `ShardedCluster` value is `1`).
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API to query details of the specified instance, including whether sharding is enabled and the number of shards.
* To reduce the number of shards, ensure the instance's current **used memory** does not exceed the new total memory capacity, where new total memory capacity = memory per shard after change × number of shards. For information on **used memory**, see [View Instance Information](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/view-instance).
* If the single-node instance before the change is a sharded cluster instance and has applied for a direct connection address, then when changing to a primary/standby instance, the number of shards cannot exceed 8. If you need to increase the number of shards in the scenario where direct connection address is enabled, please [submit a ticket](https://console.volcengine.com/workorder/create/) to contact technical support.

BackupPointName.description_cn:
Set a backup name for the full backup created before the change. If you do not specify a backup name, the backup ID is used by default.

To set a backup name, make sure it meets all of the following requirements:

* Starts with a Chinese character, letter, or underscore (_)
* Contains 1–128 characters
* Includes only Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), and hyphens (-)

This parameter is effective only if you choose to create a backup before the change (that is, when `CreateBackup` is set to `true`).

CreateBackup.description_cn:

* `true`: Create a backup
* `false` (default): Do not create a backup

* This parameter applies only to primary-secondary instances (`InstanceClass` set to `PrimarySecondary`). Single-node instances (`InstanceClass` set to `Standalone`) do not support backup, so you do not need to set this parameter.
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API to query details of a specified instance, including its type.

ShardCapacity.description_cn:
Memory capacity per shard, in MiB. Valid values: 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384.
* If this parameter is not specified, the original single-shard capacity will be used as the `ShardCapacity` after enabling the sharded cluster. However, the supported single-shard capacity specifications differ between non-sharded and sharded cluster instances. If you use a single-shard capacity not supported by sharded cluster instances, an error will occur when calling this API. For more details about Redis instance specifications, see [Product Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/product-specification).
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API to query details of a specified instance, including the memory capacity of each shard.
* To reduce shard capacity, ensure that the current used memory of the instance does not exceed 85% of the new total memory capacity (total capacity = single-shard capacity x number of shards).
* Each instance specification has corresponding supported shard capacity and bandwidth. Therefore, when you modify the shard capacity of an instance, its bandwidth and specification will also be updated accordingly. For more details about Redis instance specifications, see [Product Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/product-specification).

ConfigureNewNodes.AZ.description_cn:
Specify the availability zone for new nodes.
The number of new nodes to add (that is, the value of the `NodesNumberToIncrease` parameter) and the deployment scheme for availability zones (that is, the value of the `MultiAZ` parameter) will affect how you fill in this parameter:

* If the instance uses a multi-availability zone deployment scheme (that is, `MultiAZ` is set to `enabled`), **this parameter is required**, and **the number of availability zones provided must equal the number of single-shard nodes to add** (that is, the value of the `NodesNumberToIncrease` parameter).

For example, if you need to add 2 nodes to each shard of a multi-availability zone instance, and these two nodes are in Availability Zone A and B respectively, you can configure as follows:
```JavaScript
"NodesNumberToIncrease":2,
"ConfigureNewNodes": [
    {
        "AZ": "cn-beijing-a"
    },
    {
        "AZ": "cn-beijing-b"
    }
]    
```

* If the instance uses a single-availability zone deployment scheme (that is, `MultiAZ` is set to `disabled`), you do not need to set this parameter. Newly added nodes will automatically join the current availability zone of the instance.

* You can call the [DescribeZones](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describezones) API to query availability zone information in the target region, including availability zone IDs.
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API to query details of a specified instance, including whether a multi-availability zone deployment scheme is set.

* `IngressDirectionIp`: Ingress direction IP. Allows IPs specified in the source address of the security group's ingress direction (for TCP and ALL protocols) to access the database. If the source address is set to a security group, it will be ignored.
* `AssociateEcsIp`: Associate ECS IP. Allows cloud servers within the security group to access the database. Currently, only the primary network interface's IP information can be imported.

ConfigureNodes.AZ.description_cn:
Set the availability zone for the node. The deployment plan for the instance's availability zones affects how you fill in this parameter:

* When `MultiAZ` is set to `enabled` (that is, using a multi-availability zone deployment plan), the number of availability zones you provide must equal the number of nodes per shard in the current instance. The first availability zone is where the primary node is located.

For example, if each shard in the current instance contains 3 nodes, you need to specify the corresponding availability zone for each node.

* When `MultiAZ` is set to `disabled` (that is, using a single availability zone deployment plan), you only need to provide one availability zone. All nodes in the instance will be deployed in this zone.

* You can call the [DescribeZones](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describezones) API to query information about availability zones in the target region, including the availability zone ID.
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API to query details of a specified instance, including whether a multi-availability zone deployment plan is set.
ConfigureNodes.AZ.description_en:
Set the availability zone for the node. The deployment plan for the instance's availability zones affects how you fill in this parameter:

* When `MultiAZ` is set to `enabled` (that is, using a multi-availability zone deployment plan), the number of availability zones you provide must equal the number of nodes per shard in the current instance. The first availability zone is where the primary node is located.

For example, if each shard in the current instance contains 3 nodes, you need to specify the corresponding availability zone for each node.

* When `MultiAZ` is set to `disabled` (that is, using a single availability zone deployment plan), you only need to provide one availability zone. All nodes in the instance will be deployed in this zone.

* You can call the [DescribeZones](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describezones) API to query information about availability zones in the target region, including the availability zone ID.
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API to query details of a specified instance, including whether a multi-availability zone deployment plan is set.

* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API to view details of a specified instance, including its type.

AdditionalBandwidth.description_cn:
Set additional read and write bandwidth for a single shard. After setting, the additional read and write bandwidth for the single shard will both be the specified value. Unit: MB/s.
* It is recommended to use the `AdditionalWriteBandwidth` and `AdditionalReadBandwidth` parameters to set additional read and write bandwidth for a single shard.

AdditionalReadBandwidth.description_cn:
Set the additional read bandwidth for a single shard. This is the extra read bandwidth added on top of the default bandwidth, measured in MB/s.
The value for additional read bandwidth must meet all of the following conditions:

* Must be greater than or equal to 0. If set to 0, no additional read bandwidth is added, and the single shard bandwidth equals the default read bandwidth.
* The sum of the additional read bandwidth and the default bandwidth cannot exceed the maximum bandwidth modification limit allowed for the current instance. For more details about bandwidth limits, see [Bandwidth modification range](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/modify-bandwidth#%E5%B8%A6%E5%AE%BD%E4%BF%AE%E6%94%B9%E8%8C%83%E5%9B%B4).
* **The total bandwidth for a Redis instance cannot exceed 2.5 GB/s.** Therefore, the maximum bandwidth for the instance = min[(number of shards × maximum single shard bandwidth), 2.5 GB/s]. For more details, see [Bandwidth description](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/product-specification#%E5%B8%A6%E5%AE%BD%E8%AF%B4%E6%98%8E).

   * Total bandwidth per shard = default bandwidth of the node specification after the change + additional bandwidth
   * Additional bandwidth = min[ current additional bandwidth per shard, maximum additional bandwidth allowed by the new node specification ]
* For more details about modifying bandwidth, see [Modify Bandwidth](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/modify-bandwidth)

ShardCapacity.description_cn:
Memory capacity per shard, in MiB. The available values are as follows:

* If the instance does not have sharded cluster enabled (that is, `ShardedCluster` is set to `0`), the selectable memory capacity per shard is: 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 24576, 65536.
* If the instance has sharded cluster enabled (that is, `ShardedCluster` is set to `1`), the selectable memory capacity per shard is: 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384.

* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API to query details for a specified instance, including whether sharding is enabled and the memory capacity of each shard.
* If you need to reduce shard capacity, make sure the current used memory of the instance does not exceed 85% of the new total memory capacity (total capacity = single shard capacity x number of shards).
* Each instance specification supports corresponding shard capacity and bandwidth. When you modify the shard capacity, the bandwidth and specification of the instance will be updated at the same time. For more details about Redis instance specifications, see [Product Specifications](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/product-specification).

RetentionDays.description_cn:
Set the release time for the old IP address. Available options:

* `0`: Release immediately
* `1` (default): Release after 1 day
* `2`: Release after 2 days
* `3`: Release after 3 days
* `7`: Release after 7 days

Modifying a private network or subnet does not change the private network address or direct connection address domain name, but the corresponding IP address will change. It is recommended to clear the client cache before the old IP address is released to avoid read/write errors. For more details, see [Modify Private Network or Subnet](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/modify-vpc-or-subnet).

SubnetId.description_cn:

* Subnets have an availability zone attribute. You must select a subnet in the target VPC that is in the same availability zone as the instance.
* A subnet is an IP address block within a VPC. All cloud resources in the VPC must be deployed in a subnet. Subnets assign private IP addresses to cloud resources. You can use the [CreateSubnet](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/CreateSubnet) API to create a subnet.
* You can use the [DescribeSubnets](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeSubnets) API to view all subnets in a specified availability zone, including their subnet IDs.

VpcId.description_cn:

* For optimal performance, place the Redis instance and the ECS instance you want to connect to in the same private network. Otherwise, they cannot communicate over the internal network. You can use the [CreateVpc](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/CreateVpc) API to create a private network
* You can use the [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) API to query private network information that meets specified criteria, including the private network ID

NewAddressPrefix.description_cn:
Modified connection address prefix. The connection address prefix must meet all of the following requirements:

* Consists of lowercase letters, numbers, or hyphens (-)
* Starts with a letter and ends with a letter or number
* Length is 8 to 53 characters
* The modified connection address must be globally unique and cannot duplicate any connection address in any region of Volcengine

* If this parameter is left blank, the connection address prefix will not be modified
* If you need to upgrade the domain suffix (that is, `UpgradeRegionDomain` is `true`), you must also provide the connection address prefix (`NewAddressPrefix` cannot be empty)
* If you do not need to upgrade the domain suffix (that is, `UpgradeRegionDomain` is `false`), you must modify at least one of the `NewAddressPrefix` or `NewPort` parameters
* After modifying the connection address, existing connections will be disconnected. Please update your client connection information promptly and use the new connection address to connect to the instance. For details on how to connect to an instance, see [Connect to Instance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/connect-to-instance)
* Currently, only the connection address prefix can be modified, which is the part before `redis.ivolces.com` or `redis.volces.com`. For more information, see [Modify Connection Address](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/modify-address)

NewPort.description_cn:

* Private and public addresses support ports in the range 1024–65535
* Direct connection addresses support ports in the ranges 1024–4000 and 5100–64512

* If this parameter is left blank, the port number of the connection address will not be changed
* If you do not need to upgrade the domain suffix (that is, `UpgradeRegionDomain` is `false`), you must modify at least one of the `NewAddressPrefix` or `NewPort` parameters
* After modifying the connection address or port number, existing connections will be disconnected. Please update your client connection settings promptly and use the new port number to connect to the instance. * Changing the port may temporarily affect access to some services. Proceed with caution. For more information, see [Modify Port Number](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/modify-port)

UpgradeRegionDomain.description_cn:
Whether to upgrade the domain suffix of the connection address. Valid values:

* `true`: Upgrade
* `false` (default): Do not upgrade

* If you want to upgrade the domain suffix (that is, set `UpgradeRegionDomain` to `true`), you must also provide the connection address prefix (`NewAddressPrefix` cannot be empty)
* After upgrading the domain suffix, existing connections will be disconnected. Update your client connection settings promptly and use the new connection address to connect to the instance. For details on how to connect to an instance, see [Connect to Instance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/connect-to-instance)
* Once the domain suffix is upgraded, you cannot revert to the original suffix. Proceed with caution
* The upgraded domain suffix will automatically include the region information of the instance. The domain suffix will change from `redis.ivolces.com` (or `redis.volces.com`) to `redis.{Region ID}.ivolces.com` (or `redis.{Region ID}.volces.com`). The old connection address will be retained for 12 hours and will be automatically released after the retention period expires. For more details, see [Upgrade Domain Suffix](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/upgrade-domain-suffix)

BackupType.description_cn:
Recovery mode. Available options:

* `Full` (default): Restore using backup files created with the `Full` (full backup) method. This restores by backup set.
* `Inc`: Restore using backup files created with the `Inc` (incremental backup) method. This restores by point in time.

* To restore by point in time (`BackupType` set to `Inc`), you must enable the data flashback feature first. For details, see [Restore to original instance by point in time](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/recovery-by-time-point#%E6%81%A2%E5%A4%8D%E5%88%B0%E5%8E%9F%E5%AE%9E%E4%BE%8B).
* You can call the [StartContinuousBackup](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/startcontinuousbackup) API to enable the data flashback feature for a specified instance.

ApplyImmediately.description_cn:
Whether to perform the blue-green switchover immediately. The value range is as follows:

* `true`: Switch immediately
* `false`: Switch during the maintenance window

If you choose to switch during the maintenance window, the blue-green deployment enters the **Waiting for Switchover** state, which will persist until the task is completed. For more information about blue-green deployment states, see [Blue-Green Deployment States](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/upgrade_major_version_using_blue_green_deployment#NFCgYsLA). For instructions on setting the maintenance window, see [Set Maintenance Window](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/set-maintenance-period).

SecurityGroupBindInfos.BindMode.description_cn:

* `IngressDirectionIp`: Ingress direction IP. Allows IPs involved in TCP and ALL protocols in the ingress direction source address of the security group to access the database. If the source address is configured as a security group, it will be ignored.
* `AssociateEcsIp`: Associate ECS IP. Allows cloud servers within the security group to access the database. Currently, only the primary network interface IP information is supported for import.

For more details about security group association modes, see [Create Allowlist](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/create-allowlist)

FailbackToPrimaryDelayInMinutes.description_cn:
Duration of the fault before automatically switching back to the primary availability zone. Unit: minutes. Valid values:

* 5
* 10
* 15

* This parameter only takes effect when simulating a failover for the instance's primary availability zone (that is, the first availability zone returned in the `ZoneIds` field when calling the [DescribeDBInstanceDetail](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstancedetail) API).
* If this parameter is left blank, automatic failback to the primary availability zone will not occur. After failover, the primary node may be located in the secondary availability zone, and the secondary node may be in the primary availability zone. You can manually switch the instance's availability zone after failover by calling the [ModifyDBInstanceAZConfigure](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/modifydbinstanceazconfigure) API.

You can call the [DescribeDBInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstances) API to query basic information for all Redis instances in the target region, including the instance ID

ProxyNodeIds.description_cn:
Proxy node IDs for simulating failures
You can specify multiple nodes at once, separated by English commas (,)
* You can call the [DescribeNodeIds](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describenodeids) API to query all node information for the target instance, including Proxy node IDs
* If this parameter is left empty, no failover simulation will be performed for any Proxy node in the instance
ProxyNodeIds.description_en:
Proxy node IDs for simulating failures
You can specify multiple nodes at once, separated by English commas (,)
* You can call the [DescribeNodeIds](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describenodeids) API to query all node information for the target instance, including Proxy node IDs
* If this parameter is left empty, no failover simulation will be performed for any Proxy node in the instance

ServerShardIds.description_cn:
Shard ID of the shard to which the Server primary node (where the failure is simulated) belongs
You can specify multiple shards at the same time, separated by English commas (,)
* You can call the [DescribeDBInstanceShards](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/redis/describedbinstanceshards) API to query details of each shard in the target Redis instance, including the Shard ID
* If this parameter is left empty, no failover simulation will be performed for any Server primary node in the instance

DestinationConfig.AutoInstallBlkNone.description_en:
Whether to automatically install blk-none on the target instance or target image
Values:
- true: Automatically install
- false: Default value, do not install automatically
Only applies when migrating to Linux cloud server instances or Linux cloud service images

DestinationConfig.AutoInstallVirtio11.description_en:
Whether to automatically install the Virtio1.1 driver for the target instance or target image. Values:
- true: Automatically install
- false: Default value, do not install automatically
Only valid when migrating to Linux cloud server instances or Linux cloud service images

DestinationConfig.AutoReplicate.description_en:
Whether the migration task automatically starts after passing the pre-check. Values:
* false: Default value; does not start migration automatically
* true: Starts migration automatically
Only valid when migrating to cloud server instances or cloud service images

DestinationConfig.DestinationSystem.description_en:
Target operating system. Possible values:
- Unknown: Unknown
- VeLinux10Centos: Indicates migration to veLinux 1.0 CentOS-compatible operating system
- VeLinux20Centos: Indicates migration to veLinux 2.0 CentOS-compatible operating system
This parameter is required when `DestinationConfig.DestinationType` is set to `ECSSystem`

DestinationConfig.DestinationType.description_en:
Target type, values:
- ECSInstance: Cloud server instance
- ECSImage: Cloud server image
- ECSSystem: Cloud server operating system
- ECSTemplate: Create cloud server instance using migration template
The feature to create cloud server instances using migration templates is currently in invite-only testing. To request access, please contact your account manager.

DestinationConfig.ImageName.description_en:
Image Name
- Must start with a letter or Chinese character
- Can only contain Chinese characters, letters, numbers, underscores (_), hyphens (-), and periods (.)
- Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
This parameter is required when migrating to a cloud server image

DestinationConfig.InstanceId.description_en:
Target Instance ID: You can query and obtain it using the [DescribeInstances](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/DescribeInstances) API
This parameter is required when migrating to a cloud server instance

DestinationConfig.LicenseType.description_en:
License type
Options:
- VolcanoEngine: Default. Uses the official BytePlus license based on your source server's operating system
- BYOL: Bring your own license (BYOL)

DiskConfigs.N.DestinationDiskSize.description_en:
Target cloud image disk capacity after adjustment (in GiB)
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk number; valid range: 0–14
- Separate multiple disk numbers with `&`
- Supported system disk capacity range: 40 GiB ~ 2048 GiB, and must not be less than the total size of all migration partitions
This parameter is currently in invite-only testing. To request access, please contact your account manager

DiskConfigs.N.DiskIndex.description_en:
Source server disk index, starting from `0`
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk number, valid range: 0–14
- Use `&` to separate multiple disk numbers
The value of parameter - N cannot exceed the actual number of disks on the source server

DiskConfigs.N.DiskSize.description_en:
Source server disk capacity, unit: GiB.
- Parameter - N: Indicates the disk sequence number, corresponding to the disk sequence number identified by `DiskConfigs.N.DiskIndex`. Value range: 0–14.
- Use `&` to separate multiple disk sequence numbers.
The value of parameter - N cannot exceed the actual number of disks on the source server.

DiskConfigs.N.Partitions.N.AbortPartitio.description_en:
Whether to skip this partition during migration. Values:
* false: Default, do not skip
* true: Skip
* Supported only for Linux file copy migration to 'Cloud Server Image'
* Partitions with mount points `/` and `/boot` must be migrated
* Currently supports system disk only
* The first N: Disk number, value range: 0–14
* The second N: Partition number
* Use & to separate multiple partition configurations
* This parameter is currently in invite-only testing. To request access, please contact your account manager

DiskConfigs.N.Partitions.N.DestinationPa.description_en:
Adjusted target cloud image partition capacity (unit: Bytes)
- The first N: indicates the disk index, range: 0–14
- The second N: indicates the partition index
* Use `&` to separate multiple partition capacities
* The adjusted partition size cannot be smaller than the used space, and the total size of all partitions cannot exceed the disk size
* This parameter is currently in invite-only testing. To request access, please contact your account manager

- Only letters, numbers, underscores (_), periods (.), and hyphens (-) are allowed.
- Maximum length: 64 characters.

SyncConfig.SyncInterval.description_en:
Incremental sync interval (hours)
Valid range: 1–168
If `SyncConfig.TriggerLastSync` is set to `false`, this parameter is required.

SyncConfig.SyncTimes.description_en:
Incremental Sync Count
Values:
- Maximum: 30
- Default: 0
- Minimum: 0
This parameter is only supported for One-Click Migration.

SyncConfig.SyncType.description_en:
Copy type options:
- File (default): File copy
- Block: Block copy

SyncConfig.TriggerLastSync.description_en:
Should only one full sync be performed? Options:
- true (default): Only one full data sync is performed; incremental sync is not performed
- false: After one full data sync, incremental syncs are performed at intervals specified by the `SyncConfig.SyncInterval` parameter

Tags.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key for user labels
- Parameter - N: Indicates the tag key sequence number, valid range: 1–20
- Separate multiple tag keys with `&`
- Naming rules:
   - Must not start with any case combination of `volc:` or `sys:`
   - Only letters, numbers, spaces, and the following English symbols are allowed: "_", ".", ":", "/", "=", "+", "-", "@"
   - Length must be between 1 and 128 characters
Tag keys for the same resource must be unique

Tags.N.Value.description_en:
Tag value for user tags
- Parameter - N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag value, valid range: 1–20
- Separate multiple tag values with `&`
- Naming rules:
   - Only letters, numbers, spaces, and the following symbols are allowed: "_", ".", ":", "/", "=", "+", "-", "@"
   - Can be empty; length must be between 0 and 256 characters
If you provide this parameter, you must first provide `Tags.N.Key`

CalculatePriceInfos.Action.description_cn:
Operation for which the price quote is requested (case-insensitive). The values are as follows:

- create: Price quote before creating a cloud disk.
- extend: Price quote before expanding a cloud disk.
- modifyChargeType: Change billing mode, e.g., from subscription to pay-as-you-go.
- modifyType: Price quote before changing cloud disk specifications, e.g., from ESSD PL0 to ESSD FlexPL.
- renew: Price quote before renewal.
- terminate: Price quote before unsubscription.
Pay-as-you-go cloud disks do not support renew (renewal price quote) and terminate (unsubscription price quote).
CalculatePriceInfos.Action.description_en:
Operation for which the price quote is requested (case-insensitive). The values are as follows:

- create: Price quote before creating a cloud disk.
- extend: Price quote before expanding a cloud disk.
- modifyChargeType: Change billing mode, e.g., from subscription to pay-as-you-go.
- modifyType: Price quote before changing cloud disk specifications, e.g., from ESSD PL0 to ESSD FlexPL.
- renew: Price quote before renewal.
- terminate: Price quote before unsubscription.
Pay-as-you-go cloud disks do not support renew (renewal price quote) and terminate (unsubscription price quote).

CalculatePriceInfos.InstanceID.description_cn:
ECS instance ID. After setting InstanceID, the expiration time of the ECS instance will be used as the expiration time of the cloud disk. You do not need to set EndTime.
- Only subscription cloud disks support the InstanceID parameter.
- InstanceID and EndTime are mutually exclusive. If both are provided, an error will occur.
- If both InstanceID and Times are provided, the expiration time of the instance corresponding to InstanceID takes precedence.
CalculatePriceInfos.InstanceID.description_en:

ExtraPerformanceTypeId.description_cn:
Type of additional performance. The available values vary by cloud disk type, as follows:

- For ESSD FlexPL data disks, the available values are:

  - Balance: Balanced additional performance

  - IOPS: IOPS additional performance

  - Throughput: Throughput additional performance
For more details about additional performance for ESSD FlexPL data disks, see [Cloud Disk Additional Performance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/essd_flexpl_volume).


- For TSSD_TL0 data disks, only Throughput is supported, which configures additional throughput for TSSD_TL0 cloud disks. For more details, see [Cloud Disk Specifications - Throughput SSD Cloud Disk](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Volume-specification-tssd-tl0-Volume)

- Only ESSD FlexPL data disks of 500 GiB or larger support additional performance configuration.

- Only TSSD_TL0 data disks of 100 GiB or larger support additional performance configuration.

ExtraPerformanceTypeId.description_cn:
Type of extra performance. The available values differ for each disk type, as follows:
- For ESSD FlexPL data disks, the extra performance values are:
	- Balance: Balanced extra performance.
	- IOPS: IOPS-type extra performance.
	- Throughput: Throughput-type extra performance.
    For detailed information about extra performance for ESSD FlexPL data disks, see [Cloud Disk Extra Performance](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/essd_flexpl_volume).
   

- TSSD_TL0 disks only support the value `Throughput`, which means configuring extra throughput for TSSD_TL0 disks. For details, see [Cloud Disk Specifications - Throughput-type SSD Disk](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/ecs/Volume-specification-tssd-tl0-Volume).

EffectiveAt.description_cn: Effective time of the reserved storage capacity package. The date format follows the ISO 8601 standard. The default is empty, which means it takes effect immediately. If the specified effective time is not on the hour, it will take effect at the beginning of the specified hour. For example, if the specified time is 2024-11-25 21:50:05, the actual effective time will be 2024-11-25 21:00:00.

RoleSessionName.description_cn: Role session name, 2–64 characters long; supports English letters, numbers, and .-_@ symbols. IpPrefixMatchMode.description_cn:
Route prefix matching modes

* Include: Fuzzy matching. A match is successful if the route prefix in the matching condition includes the route prefix of the route being matched. For example, a policy entry with the route prefix 10.10.0.0/16 can match a route whose target subnet is 10.10.1.0/24 using fuzzy matching.
* Complete (default): Exact matching. A match is successful only if the route prefix in the matching condition is identical to the route prefix of the route being matched. For example, a policy entry with the route prefix 10.10.0.0/16 can only match a route whose target subnet is 10.10.0.0/16 exactly.
IpPrefixMatchMode.description_en:
Route prefix matching modes

* Include: Fuzzy matching. A match is successful if the route prefix in the matching condition includes the route prefix of the route being matched. For example, a policy entry with the route prefix 10.10.0.0/16 can match a route whose target subnet is 10.10.1.0/24 using fuzzy matching.
* Complete (default): Exact matching. A match is successful only if the route prefix in the matching condition is identical to the route prefix of the route being matched. For example, a policy entry with the route prefix 10.10.0.0/16 can only match a route whose target subnet is 10.10.0.0/16 exactly.

IpPrefixes.description_cn:
Route prefix for the route policy entry. Supports IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR blocks.

* N: Indicates the sequence number of the route prefix, ranging from 1 to 200. Use & to separate multiple route prefixes.
* If this parameter is not provided or no value is specified, the default is an empty string.

The IPv6 feature for transit routers is currently in beta testing. To use this feature, please contact your account manager.

SourceResourceIds.description_cn:
Source instance ID of the routing policy entry.

* You can call the [DescribeVpcs](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/vpc/DescribeVpcs) API to obtain the ID of a VPC instance.
* You can call the [DescribeDirectConnectGateways](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/directconnect/DescribeDirectConnectGateways) API to obtain the ID of a Direct Connect Gateway instance.
* You can call the [DescribeTransitRouters](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouters) API to obtain the ID of a cross-region TR instance.

* N: Indicates the sequence number of the source instance ID, with a value range of 1–10. Use & to separate multiple source instance IDs.
* After a value is provided for the parameter `SourceResourceTypes.N`, this parameter is required.

ApplianceModeEnabled.description_cn:
Enable path consistency mode. Please enter the following enumeration values exactly as shown, including case. Do not use any other values.

* true: Yes. When enabled, TR forwards traffic to this VPC connection using the same availability zone endpoint for both request and response traffic.
* false (default): No.

AutoPublishRouteEnabled.description_cn:
Automatically synchronize TR routes to the network instance route table. Please enter the following enumerated values exactly as shown, including case. Do not enter any other values.

* true: Yes. The system will automatically synchronize route entries from the TR route table associated with the network instance connection to the network instance's route table.
      The system will only automatically synchronize TR routes to the network instance's route table if this parameter is set to true and there are route entries in the TR route table associated with the network instance connection.
   
* false (default): No

ClientToken.description_cn:
Client token, used to ensure idempotency of the request.

* This parameter value is automatically generated by the client to ensure uniqueness for different requests, preventing duplicate operations if the API call times out or a server error occurs and the client retries multiple times.

* If this parameter is not specified, idempotency is not enforced.

TagFilters.N.Key.description_en:
Tag key of the TR route table tag.

* N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag key, with a value range of 1–10.
* Use & to separate multiple tag keys.
* When specifying multiple tag keys, it queries TR route tables that contain all specified tag keys.

TagFilters.N.Values.N.description_en:
Tag value of the TR route table tag.

* The first N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag key, with a value range of 1–10.
* The second N: Indicates the sequence number of the tag value, with a value range of 1–3. For the same tag key, multiple tag values have a logical 'OR' relationship, meaning it queries resources that have any of the tag values under the same tag key.
* Use & to separate multiple tag values.
* If this parameter is provided, TagFilters.N.Key must be provided first.
* If this parameter is empty, it queries resources where the tag value under the specified tag key is empty.

- You can call the [DescribeDirectConnectGateways](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/directconnect/DescribeDirectConnectGateways) API to get the ID of a direct connect gateway instance.

- When the routing policy direction is "In", this field cannot be specified.

IpPrefixMatchMode.description_cn:
Route Prefix Matching Modes
- Include: Contains match. The route prefix in the matching condition contains the route prefix of the route being matched, resulting in a successful match. For example, a policy entry with the route prefix 10.10.0.0/16 can loosely match a route with the target prefix 10.10.1.0/24.
- Complete: Exact match. The route prefix in the matching condition must be identical to the route prefix of the route being matched for a successful match. For example, a policy entry with the route prefix 10.10.0.0/16 can only exactly match a route with the target prefix 10.10.0.0/16.

AutoPublishRouteEnabled.description_cn:
Whether to automatically synchronize TR routes to the network instance route table. Please enter the following enumerated values exactly as shown, including case. Do not use any other values.

* true: Yes. The system will automatically synchronize route entries from the TR route table associated with this network instance connection to the network instance's route table.

* false (default): No.

* Must start with a letter, number, or Chinese character. Can include letters, numbers, Chinese characters, and the following special characters: comma (,), period (.), underscore (_), space ( ), equals sign (=), hyphen (-), Chinese comma (，), and Chinese period (。).
* Length limit: 0–255 characters.
* If you do not change this parameter value, the original configuration remains unchanged.

HealthCheckRevokeRouteEnabled.description_cn:

* true: Yes. Takes effect only when the IPsec connection has health check enabled, and only supports converging static routes. BGP route convergence is not supported.
* false: No.

- You can call [DescribeTransitRouterMulticastDomains](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterMulticastDomains) to get the ID of a 'transitroutermulticastdomain' resource
- You can call [DescribeTransitRouterBandwidthPackages](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/transitrouter/DescribeTransitRouterBandwidthPackages) API to get the ID of a 'transitrouterbandwidthpackage' resource

Tags.N.Key.description_en:
User tag key.
- Length limit: 1–128 characters
- Case-sensitive; cannot start with any combination of 'volc:' or 'sys:' (case-insensitive)
- Cannot start or end with a space
- Can include characters from any language, numbers, spaces (), underscores (_), periods (.), colons (:), slashes (/), equals signs (=), plus signs (+), minus signs (-), and @

- Tag keys for the same resource cannot be duplicated. If the Tags.N.Key you pass is the same as an existing tag key, the newly added tag will overwrite the original tag
- If you do not pass this parameter or do not provide a value, it defaults to empty

Tags.N.Value.description_en:
User tag value.
- Length limit: 1–256 characters
- Case-sensitive; cannot start or end with a space
- Can include characters from any language, numbers, spaces (), underscores (_), periods (.), colons (:), slashes (/), equals signs (=), plus signs (+), minus signs (-), and @

If you pass this parameter, you must first pass Tags.N.Key

AllowList.description_cn:
Enter an IP address or an IP address range in CIDR format.
* If provided together with `UserAllowList`, the value of `UserAllowList` takes precedence.
* Each allowlist group supports up to 300 IP addresses or CIDR-formatted IP address ranges. Duplicate addresses are not allowed. Separate multiple addresses with commas (,). Special examples:
   * Setting `0.0.0.0/0` allows access from all addresses.
   * Setting `127.0.0.1` denies access from all addresses.
   * Setting both `0.0.0.0/0` and `127.0.0.1` allows access from all addresses.
   * Setting `192.168.1.1` allows access only from this IP address.
   * Setting CIDR `192.168.1.0/24` allows access from all IP addresses in this subnet.
